basis_claims.quote: The Beast of Gévaudan ... is the historic name associated with a man-eating cryptid or cryptids that terrorized the former province of Gévaudan ... in the Margeride Mountains of south-central France between 30 June 1764 and 19 June 1767.

statement.id: Binatang Gévaudan (La Bête du Gévaudan) adalah nama historis untuk satu atau lebih kriptid pemangsa manusia yang meneror bekas provinsi Gévaudan di Pegunungan Margeride, Prancis selatan-tengah, antara 30 Juni 1764 dan 19 Juni 1767.
statement.en: The Beast of Gévaudan (La Bête du Gévaudan) is the historic name for one or more man-eating cryptids that terrorised the former province of Gévaudan in the Margeride Mountains of south-central France between 30 June 1764 and 19 June 1767.

basis_claims.quote: were said to have been committed by one or more beasts of a tawny/russet colour with dark streaks/stripes and a dark stripe down its back, a tail "longer than a wolf's" ending in a tuft according to contemporary eyewitnesses.

statement.id: Menurut saksi mata masa itu, serangan dilakukan satu atau lebih binatang berwarna cokelat kemerahan dengan belang gelap dan garis gelap di punggung, berekor lebih panjang daripada serigala dengan jumbai di ujungnya.
statement.en: Contemporary witnesses said the attacks were by one or more tawny-russet beasts with dark stripes and a dark stripe down the back, with a tail 'longer than a wolf's' ending in a tuft.

basis_claims.quote: It was said to attack with formidable teeth and claws, and appeared to be the size of a calf or cow and seemed to fly or bound across fields towards its victims.

statement.id: Ia menyerang dengan gigi dan cakar yang mengerikan, tampak sebesar anak sapi atau sapi, dan seolah terbang atau melompat melintasi ladang ke arah korbannya.
statement.en: It attacked with fearsome teeth and claws, looked the size of a calf or cow, and seemed to fly or bound across fields at its victims.

basis_claims.quote: These descriptions from the period could identify the beast as a striped hyena, a large wolf, a large dog, or a wolfdog, though its identity is still the subject of debate and remains unsolved to this day.

statement.id: Gambaran itu dapat cocok dengan dubuk belang, serigala besar, anjing besar, atau anjing-serigala, tetapi identitasnya masih diperdebatkan sampai kini.
statement.en: These descriptions could fit a striped hyena, a large wolf, a large dog or a wolfdog, but its identity is still debated and unsolved.

basis_claims.statement: The cù-sìth (coin-shìth) is a mythical hound of Irish and Scottish folklore, cú sídhe; like the Welsh Cŵn Annwn.
basis_claims.statement_id: Cù-sìth (coin-shìth) anjing mitos cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish folklore) dan Skotlandia (Scottish folklore), cú sídhe; mirip Cŵn Annwn Wales (Welsh); di Britania dan Irlandia.
basis_claims.quote: is a mythical hound found in Irish folklore and Scottish folklore. In Irish folklore it is spelled cú sídhe, and it also bears some resemblance to the Welsh Cŵn Annwn.

basis_claims.statement: Lives in rock clefts and roams the Highland moors; dark green shaggy coat; size of a small cow.
basis_claims.statement_id: Tinggal di celah batu, menjelajahi padang Dataran Tinggi (Highlands); bulu hijau gelap; seukuran sapi kecil.
basis_claims.quote: The cù-sìth is thought to make its home in the clefts of rocks and to roam the moors of the Highlands. It is usually described as having a shaggy, dark green coat with deeper green fur on the ears and more yellow fur towards the feet. It is said to be the size of a small cow

basis_claims.statement: Egg ghost, or dalgyal gwisin, is a Korean ghost resembling an egg.
basis_claims.statement_id: Egg ghost atau dalgyal gwisin adalah hantu Korea yang bentuknya menyerupai telur.
basis_claims.quote: Egg ghost refers to dalgyal gwisin (Korean: 달걀귀신), a type of Korean ghost. Its name comes from its resemblance to an egg. It does not have arms, legs, nor a head, not even eyes, nose, or mouth. Legend says that when a person sees an egg ghost, they will die. Its origin and personality are not significant.

basis_claims.statement: Its portrayal lacks arms, legs, head, eyes, nose, and mouth.
basis_claims.statement_id: Penggambarannya tidak memiliki lengan, kaki, kepala, mata, hidung, atau mulut.
basis_claims.quote: Egg ghost refers to dalgyal gwisin (Korean: 달걀귀신), a type of Korean ghost. Its name comes from its resemblance to an egg. It does not have arms, legs, nor a head, not even eyes, nose, or mouth. Legend says that when a person sees an egg ghost, they will die. Its origin and personality are not significant.

basis_claims.statement: Black Shuck tales belong to the folklore of Norfolk, Suffolk, the Cambridgeshire Fens and Essex; sometimes an omen of death, sometimes companionable.
basis_claims.statement_id: Kisah Black Shuck bagian dari cerita rakyat Norfolk, Suffolk, Cambridgeshire Fens, Essex (East Anglia); kadang pertanda kematian, kadang teman; anjing hitam (Black dog), Old Shuck, Old Shock; Inggris (English folklore), Kepulauan Britania (British Isles); di Britania Raya.
basis_claims.quote: Accounts of Black Shuck form part of the folklore of Norfolk, Suffolk, the Cambridgeshire Fens and Essex, and descriptions of the creature's appearance and nature vary considerably; it is sometimes recorded as an omen of death, but, in other instances, is described as companionable.

basis_claims.statement: First printed mention by Reverend E. S. Taylor in Notes and Queries, 1850: a shaggy fiery-eyed dog visiting churchyards at midnight.
basis_claims.statement_id: Penyebutan tertulis pertama oleh Pendeta (Reverend) E. S. Taylor, Notes and Queries 1850: anjing hitam berbulu, bermata api, mengunjungi pekuburan tengah malam.
basis_claims.quote: The first mention in print of "Black Shuck" is by Reverend E. S. Taylor in an 1850 edition of the journal Notes and Queries which describes "Shuck the Dog-fiend"

basis_claims.statement: Black Shuck (der Alte Shuck) is a mysterious black ghost dog (schwarzen Geisterhundes) said to haunt Norfolk, Essex and Suffolk.
basis_claims.statement_id: Black Shuck (der Alte Shuck) anjing hantu hitam (schwarzen Geisterhundes) yang menghantui Norfolk, Essex, Suffolk.
basis_claims.quote: Black Shuck oder der Alte Shuck ist der Name eines geheimnisumwobenen schwarzen Geisterhundes, der angeblich in Norfolk, Essex und Suffolk spuken soll.

erdhenne.depicted_variant: Visible warning Erdhenne listened to by anxious household
visual_requirements: Visible warning Erdhenne listened to by anxious household
Coherent anatomy and documented mythic scene
erdhenne.aura: Presence through source-backed form and physical scene; no generic glow, ribbons or magical mist.

basis_claims.quote: Most of the time, the Erdhenne remains unseen, only communicating with the inhabitants of its home by clucking loudly, as if calling chicks. By this, they alert the inhabitants of dangers threatening them or the house. Some legends claim that the spirit answers questions about the danger when asked directly.

statement.id: Erdhenne biasanya tak terlihat dan hanya berkotek keras seperti memanggil anak ayam untuk memperingatkan penghuni akan bahaya bagi mereka atau rumah; beberapa legenda menyebut ia menjawab pertanyaan tentang bahaya itu bila ditanya langsung.
statement.en: The Erdhenne mostly stays unseen, clucking loudly like a hen calling chicks to warn residents of dangers to them or the house; some legends say it answers questions about the danger when asked directly.

basis_claims.quote: the spirit appears as an old, ash grey, shaggy hen with a short neck. By becoming visible, the Erdhenne foretells death within a year, usually that of the person it shows itself to. However, according to another legend, should it cluck and flutter its wings nine times, the head of the house would fall deadly ill.

statement.id: Roh itu tampil sebagai ayam betina tua kelabu abu berbulu kusut berleher pendek; penampakannya meramalkan kematian dalam setahun, biasanya orang yang melihatnya; menurut legenda lain, bila ia berkotek dan mengepakkan sayap sembilan kali, kepala rumah tangga jatuh sakit parah.
statement.en: The spirit appears as an old, ash-grey, shaggy short-necked hen; becoming visible, it foretells a death within a year, usually of the one who sees it; another legend says nine clucks and wing-flaps mean the head of the house will fall mortally ill.

basis_claims.quote: Die Stimme dieses Geistwesens soll aus dem Erdboden oder einer dunklen Ecke der Stube dringen und wie das Glucksen, beziehungsweise Piepsen, einer Henne klingen, die Küklein führt, was ihm den Namen einbrachte. Die Erdhenne soll, wie die Unke oder die Hausotter ein gutartiger Schutzgeist sein

statement.id: Suara roh ini konon keluar dari tanah atau sudut gelap ruangan, terdengar seperti kotek induk ayam yang menuntun anak-anaknya, sehingga ia dinamai demikian; seperti Unke atau Hausotter (ular rumah), Erdhenne dianggap roh pelindung yang baik.
statement.en: This spirit's voice is said to come from the ground or a dark corner of the room, sounding like a hen clucking to her chicks, which gave it its name; like the Unke or the Hausotter (house snake), the Erdhenne is held to be a benign guardian spirit.

artistic_changes: Painterly square composition
Clothing, weather and exact setting details are editorial unless identified in claims

presentation_revision.rationale: Replaces ordinary animal presentation with Visible warning Erdhenne listened to by anxious household

gulon.depicted_variant: Dog body with cat head/claws and fox tail

basis_claims.statement: The gulon looks like a mix of animals, usually dog-sized and dog-shaped with cat-like head, ears and claws, a thick shaggy brown coat and a fox-like tail.
basis_claims.statement_id: Gulon tampak seperti campuran berbagai hewan, biasanya seukuran dan sebentuk anjing dengan kepala, telinga, dan cakar seperti kucing, berbulu cokelat tebal yang kusut dan berekor seperti rubah.
basis_claims.quote: It resembles a hodgepodge of various animals, usually described as being the size and shape of a dog, with some cat-like features such as the head, ears, and claws. It also supposedly has a thick coat of shaggy brown fur and a tail resembling that of a fox.

basis_claims.statement: The jerff, modern spelling järv, is in Scandinavian legend a blend of animals resembling a dog with a cat's head and claws, a thick coat and a fox-like tail; in Germany it is Vielfraß and in English Gulon.
basis_claims.statement_id: Jerff, dalam ejaan modern Järv, dalam legenda Skandinavia adalah campuran berbagai hewan yang mirip anjing dengan kepala dan cakar kucing, berbulu tebal dan berekor seperti rubah; di Jerman ia dikenal sebagai Vielfraß dan dalam bahasa Inggris Gulon.
basis_claims.quote: En Jerff eller med modern stavning Järv, är inom skandinavisk legend en blandning av olika djur men som ska likna en hund, med huvud och klor av en katt. Den ska även ha en tjock päls och en svans liknande den på en räv. I Tyskland är varelsen känd som Vielfraß och på engelska heter det Gulon.

gonggong.depicted_variant: Human-serpentine water deity, red hair and iron forehead

basis_claims.statement: Gonggong is a Chinese water deity portrayed with human and serpentine features.
basis_claims.statement_id: Gonggong adalah dewa air dalam mitologi Tiongkok dengan ciri manusia dan ular.
basis_claims.quote: Gonggong (/ˈɡɒŋɡɒŋ/) is a Chinese water god who is depicted in Chinese mythology and folktales as having a copper human head with an iron forehead, red hair, and the body of a serpent, or sometimes the head and torso are human, with the tail of a serpent. He is destructive and is blamed for various cosmic catastrophes.

basis_claims.statement: His portrayal includes red hair and an iron forehead.
basis_claims.statement_id: Penggambarannya mencakup rambut merah dan dahi besi.
basis_claims.quote: Gonggong (/ˈɡɒŋɡɒŋ/) is a Chinese water god who is depicted in Chinese mythology and folktales as having a copper human head with an iron forehead, red hair, and the body of a serpent, or sometimes the head and torso are human, with the tail of a serpent. He is destructive and is blamed for various cosmic catastrophes.

basis_claims.statement: Gonggong is linked to great floods alongside his subordinate Xiangliu.
basis_claims.statement_id: Gonggong dikaitkan dengan banjir besar bersama bawahannya Xiangliu.
basis_claims.quote: Gonggong was credited in various mythological contexts as being responsible for great floods, often in concert with his minister Xiangliu (a.k.a. Xiangyao), who has nine heads and the body of a snake.

basis_claims.statement: In West Virginia folklore, the Grafton Monster is a cryptid reported around Grafton in 1964.
basis_claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat West Virginia, Monster Grafton adalah kriptid yang dilaporkan di sekitar Grafton pada 1964.
basis_claims.quote: In West Virginia folklore, the Grafton Monster is a cryptid reported in and around Grafton, West Virginia, primarily associated with a cluster of sightings and local publicity in 1964.

basis_claims.statement: The creature is portrayed as very tall, pale, sometimes appearing headless and producing whistling.
basis_claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini digambarkan sangat tinggi, berkulit pucat, kadang tampak tanpa kepala dan bersiul ganjil.
basis_claims.quote: Descriptions vary by source, but the creature is commonly portrayed as a very tall, pale or light-colored figure, sometimes described as appearing headless and producing an unusual whistling sound.

indrik.depicted_variant: Bull body, deer legs, horse head, single snout horn

basis_claims.statement: Indrik (the Indrik-Beast) of the Dove Book and Russian folklore is a fabulous beast, king of all animals, living on "the Holy Mountain" where no other foot may tread; when it stirs the earth trembles.
basis_claims.statement_id: Indrik (Binatang Indrik) dalam Kitab Merpati dan cerita rakyat Rusia adalah binatang dongeng, raja segala binatang, yang tinggal di "Gunung Suci" yang tak boleh diinjak kaki lain; bila bergerak, bumi bergetar.
basis_claims.quote: is a fabulous beast, the king of all animals, who lives on a mountain known as "The Holy Mountain" where no other foot may tread. When it stirs, the Earth trembles.

basis_claims.statement: It is described as a gigantic bull with deer legs, a horse head and an enormous horn on its snout, vaguely like a rhinoceros.
basis_claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai banteng raksasa berkaki rusa, berkepala kuda, dan bercula besar di moncong, agak mirip badak.
basis_claims.quote: It is described as a gigantic bull with legs of a deer, the head of a horse and an enormous horn in its snout, making it vaguely similar to a rhinoceros.

am-fear-liath-mor.depicted_variant: The Big Grey Man of Ben Macdui: an extremely tall, very thin dark-haired humanoid with unusually long arms and broad shoulders, emerging through Scottish mountain fog over gravel. Dark skin and dark body hair, no horns, no wolf face; distinguish the tall thin build from a bulky Bigfoot.

basis_claims.statement: In Scottish folklore Am Fear Liath Mòr (Scottish Gaelic, Big Grey Man; Big Grey Man of Ben Macdui, Greyman) is a cryptid of Ben Macdui in the Cairngorms, second highest in the British Isles after Ben Nevis.
basis_claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore), Am Fear Liath Mòr (Gaelik Skotlandia, Scottish Gaelic, Lelaki Kelabu Besar; Big Grey Man of Ben Macdui, Greyman) kriptid di Ben Macdui, Cairngorms, kedua tertinggi di Kepulauan Britania (British Isles) setelah Ben Nevis; di Britania Raya.
basis_claims.quote: is the name for a presence or cryptid which is said to haunt the summit and passes of Ben Macdui, the highest peak of the Cairngorms and the second highest peak in the British Isles after Ben Nevis.

basis_claims.statement: Very thin, over three metres tall, dark skin and hair, long arms, broad shoulders.
basis_claims.statement_id: Sangat kurus, lebih dari tiga meter, kulit dan rambut gelap, lengan panjang, bahu lebar.
basis_claims.quote: It is said to be very thin and over ten feet (three metres) tall, with dark skin and hair, long arms, and broad shoulders.

basis_claims.statement: Usually unseen in fog; only crunching gravel and unease.
basis_claims.statement_id: Biasanya tak terlihat dalam kabut; hanya bunyi kerikil berderak dan rasa gelisah.
basis_claims.quote: Most often, the creature remains unseen in the fog of the mountain, with encounters limited to the sound of crunching gravel as it walks behind climbers and a general feeling of unease around the mountain.

amomongo.depicted_variant: A hairy man-sized ape with visibly long fingernails, four ape limbs and no tail, at a cave near the forested foot of Mount Kanlaon, Negros. Natural ape face and posture, rough dark fur. No horns, clothing, weapons, or human-wolf hybrid anatomy.

basis_claims.statement: In Philippine folklore, the amomongo is a cryptid described as a hairy, man-sized ape with long nails; its name probably comes from Hiligaynon amó, 'ape' or 'monkey'.
basis_claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Filipina, amomongo adalah kriptid berupa kera berbulu seukuran manusia dengan kuku panjang; namanya kemungkinan dari kata Hiligaynon amó, 'kera' atau 'monyet'.
basis_claims.quote: In Philippine folklore, the Amomongo is a cryptid described as a hairy, man-sized ape with long nails. The name is probably derived from the Hiligaynon word amó, which translates "ape" or "monkey".

basis_claims.statement: La Castellana residents in Negros Occidental see the amomongo as a violent wild creature living in caves near the foot of Mount Kanlaon.
basis_claims.statement_id: Warga La Castellana, Negros Occidental, memandang amomongo sebagai makhluk buas dan liar yang tinggal di gua dekat kaki Gunung Kanlaon.
basis_claims.quote: Residents of La Castellana in Negros Occidental view the Amomongo as a violent, wild creature that lives in caves near the foot of the volcanic Mount Kanlaon.

arkaroo.depicted_variant: One enormous natural serpentine being moving beside the pale salt expanse of Lake Frome toward the red rocky Gammon Ranges in South Australia. One snake head, one continuous thick legless body, long tapering tail; no wings, legs, horns or invented sacred symbols. The immense scale and landscape tell the water-drinking-serpent story.

basis_claims.statement: In dreamtime mythology, the Arkaroo is a serpent who drank all the waters of Lake Frome in South Australia.
basis_claims.statement_id: Pada masa dreamtime, Arkaroo adalah ular yang meminum semua air di Lake Frome di South Australia.
basis_claims.quote: In the dreamtime of Australian Aboriginal mythology, the Arkaroo is a serpent who drank all the waters of Lake Frome in South Australia, the latter remaining a large salt pan most of the time.

basis_claims.statement: The Arkaroo retracted into the mountains, carving the valleys of the Gammon Ranges in the northern Flinders Ranges.
basis_claims.statement_id: Arkaroo beristirahat ke pegunungan barat dan tubuhnya mengukir lembah-lembah Gammon Ranges di Flinders Ranges utara.
basis_claims.quote: Heavily filled and tired, the Arkaroo retracted for a nap into the mountains west, carving by his body the valleys of what is known today as the Gammon Ranges in the northern Flinders Ranges.

basis_claims.statement: Attacked by mystic beasts, water from his rests formed waterholes such as Arkaroola Springs.
basis_claims.statement_id: Ia diserang makhluk mistis lain dan air yang keluar dari tempat istirahatnya menghasilkan mata air seperti Arkaroola Springs.
basis_claims.quote: He was attacked by other mystic beasts and let water on his rests, each position resulting in a waterhole, such as that of Arkaroola Springs and others.

bear-lake-monster.depicted_variant: A large serpent-like lake monster with short legs, each roughly eighteen inches long relative to the enormous elongated trunk, crawling out onto the stony shore of Bear Lake, Utah-Idaho. Show four short legs as an artistic anatomical choice, one reptilian head and a long tapering tail. No wings, horse head, or ocean ship.

basis_claims.statement: The Bear Lake Monster is an urban legend of a lake monster near Bear Lake on the Utah–Idaho border.
basis_claims.statement_id: Bear Lake Monster adalah legenda urban tentang monster danau di sekitar Bear Lake, perbatasan Utah dan Idaho.
basis_claims.quote: The Bear Lake Monster is a lake monster urban legend which appears in folklore near Bear Lake, on the Utah–Idaho border.

basis_claims.statement: Folklorists say it resembles a serpent with legs about eighteen inches long, roaming the shore.
basis_claims.statement_id: Menurut para folklorist, ia mirip ular tetapi berkaki sekitar delapan belas inci yang dipakainya berkeliaran di tepi danau.
basis_claims.quote: is reported to resemble a serpent, but with legs about eighteen inches [46 cm] long on which it marauds along the shoreline.

bobbi-bobbi.depicted_variant: A single huge snake suspended in the cloud-filled heavens, representing Bobbi-Bobbi in Binbinga Dreamtime accounts. One natural snake head, smooth continuous legless coiling body and tapering tail, no dragon horns or feathers. Warm high clouds and a distant northern Australian landscape. No borrowed Aboriginal dot-painting motifs or invented ritual symbols.

basis_claims.statement: Bobbi-Bobbi was a supernatural being living in the heavens in Binbinga Dreamtime myths.
basis_claims.statement_id: Bobbi-Bobbi adalah makhluk gaib suku Binbinga yang tinggal di surga pada masa Dreamtime.
basis_claims.quote: In myths of the Binbinga people of northern Australia, Bobbi-Bobbi was a supernatural being who lived in the heavens in the Dreamtime.

basis_claims.statement: He was a huge snake similar to the Rainbow Serpent, initially benevolent to humans.
basis_claims.statement_id: Bobbi-Bobbi adalah ular raksasa mirip Rainbow Serpent yang mulanya baik hati pada manusia.
basis_claims.quote: He was a huge snake, similar to the Rainbow Serpent, and was originally benevolent towards humans.

b-yg.depicted_variant: The Boyg in its Norwegian giant slimy serpent variant: an immense glossy dark snake coiled across and completely obstructing a narrow rocky forest path. One snake head, continuous legless coils, no horns, wings or humanoid troll parts. Wet stones and northern conifers at dusk.

basis_claims.statement: The Bøyg (Norwegian Bøygen), also called the 'Great Bøyg of Etnedal', is a legendary creature of Scandinavian folklore.
basis_claims.statement_id: Bøyg (Norwegia: Bøygen), juga disebut "Bøyg Besar dari Etnedal", adalah makhluk legenda dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia.
basis_claims.quote: also referred to as the "Great Bøyg of Etnedal" is a legendary gnome-like creature in Scandinavian folklore.

basis_claims.statement: It is a great troll from Telemark and Gudbrandsdalen, usually a giant slimy serpent blocking travellers; the name means 'bend', 'twist' or 'curve', and it appears in the tale of Per Gynt, basis of Henrik Ibsen's play Peer Gynt.
basis_claims.statement_id: Bøyg adalah troll besar dari Telemark dan Gudbrandsdalen, biasanya digambarkan sebagai ular raksasa berlendir yang menghalangi pengembara; namanya berarti "tikungan", "pilinan", atau "lengkungan", dan ia muncul dalam dongeng Per Gynt yang menjadi dasar drama Peer Gynt karya Henrik Ibsen.
basis_claims.quote: It is a great troll from Telemark and Gudbrandsdalen. It is commonly characterized as a giant, slimy serpent which stands as a hindrance to travellers. The name means 'bend', 'twist' or 'curve'. It appears in the fairy-tale of Per Gynt, the basis for Henrik Ibsen's play Peer Gynt.

basis_claims.statement: Bøyg, often called Bøygen ('the bent one'), is a supernatural being or troll in the form of a giant serpent in Norwegian folk belief; it can be invisible, tries to block and spoil people's ways, and is best known today from Henrik Ibsen's 1867 play Peer Gynt.
basis_claims.statement_id: Bøyg, sering disebut Bøygen ("yang membungkuk"), adalah makhluk gaib atau troll berwujud ular raksasa dalam kepercayaan rakyat Norwegia; ia bisa juga tak terlihat, berusaha menghalangi dan merusak urusan orang, dan kini paling dikenal dari drama Peer Gynt (1867) karya Henrik Ibsen.
basis_claims.quote: Bøyg, ofte omtalt i bestemt form Bøygen, det vil si «den som er bøyd», er et overnaturlig vesen eller troll som opptrer i form av en kjempeslange i norsk folketro. Skikkelsen, som også kan være usynlig, prøver å stille seg i veien og ødelegge for folk. I dag er figuren mest kjent fra Henrik Ibsens skuespill Peer Gynt fra 1867.

chernava.depicted_variant: Chernava, the Russian river maiden from Sadko: a human woman's head and upper body with ONE long fish tail instead of legs, beside a quiet river at dawn. Modest linen upper garment as an editorial treatment, unadorned natural face; long tail and broad fish fin fully visible. No wings or bird feet.

basis_claims.statement: In Russian folklore, Chernava is the Sea Tsar's daughter (or niece), spirit and personification of the river of the same name; a mermaid with human head and upper body and a fish tail, famed from the epic of Sadko.
basis_claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, Chernava (Чернава) adalah putri Tsar Laut (atau keponakannya), roh dan perwujudan sungai bernama sama; ia putri duyung berkepala dan bertubuh atas manusia dengan ekor ikan, terkenal dari epos Sadko.
basis_claims.quote: is Sea Tsar's daughter (or, according to some versions, a niece), spirit and personification of the river of the same name. She is a mermaid. Her head and upper body are human, while the lower body is a fish's tail. Chernava is famed from her appearance in the epic of Sadko.

basis_claims.statement: On the wedding night Sadko did not touch her; while he slept Chernava became a river and helped him back to the human world; he woke on the shore of the river Chernava and rejoined his first wife.
basis_claims.statement_id: Pada malam pernikahan Sadko tidak menyentuhnya; ketika ia tidur, Chernava berubah menjadi sungai dan membantunya kembali ke dunia manusia; Sadko terbangun di tepi sungai Chernava dan kembali kepada istri pertamanya.
basis_claims.quote: On their wedding night he did not touch her. When Sadko was asleep, Chernava had transformed into a river, helping him to get into the human world. Sadko woke up on the shore of the river Chernava and rejoined his first wife.

snow-lion.depicted_variant: White celestial lion with turquoise mane

basis_claims.statement: Kappa is an amphibious supernatural being and water spirit in Japanese folklore.
basis_claims.statement_id: Kappa adalah makhluk amfibi gaib dan roh air dalam cerita rakyat Jepang.
basis_claims.quote: Kappa (河童 river-child) is an amphibious supernatural monster and water spirit in Japanese folklore.

basis_claims.statement: A contemporary Japanese image shows kappa with green childlike bodies and round head dishes.
basis_claims.statement_id: Gambaran Jepang masa kini menampilkan kappa bertubuh hijau seperti anak dan memiliki cekungan bundar di kepala.
basis_claims.quote: Contemporary Japanese people typically visualize kappa as having green, hairless bodies shaped like that of a human child. They have smooth, circular dishes on their heads

basis_claims.statement: Contemporary depictions show birdlike beaks and turtlelike shells.
basis_claims.statement_id: Gambaran masa kini menunjukkan paruh burung dan tempurung mirip kura-kura.
basis_claims.quote: pointed beaks like birds, which are often yellow. On their backs, they have what looks like a turtle’s shell

basis_claims.statement: Kinnara is a Hindu and Buddhist mythological creature depicted as part human and part bird.
basis_claims.statement_id: Kinnara adalah makhluk mitologi Hindu dan Buddha yang digambarkan sebagian manusia dan sebagian burung.
basis_claims.quote: A kinnara (Sanskrit: किन्नर Kiṃnara) is a creature from Hindu and Buddhist mythology.  They are described as part human and part bird, and have a strong association with music and love.

basis_claims.statement: In Southeast Asian traditions female kinnaris have female body parts and swan wings and tail.
basis_claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Asia Tenggara, kinnari perempuan memiliki bagian tubuh perempuan dan sayap serta ekor angsa.
basis_claims.quote: kinnaris have the head, torso, and arms of a woman and the wings, tail and feet of a swan.

lamassu.depicted_variant: One immense Assyrian protective LAMASSU in living four-legged BULL variant: dignified bearded HUMAN HEAD, muscular BULL BODY and TWO broad BIRD WINGS. FOUR legs, no extra sculptural fifth leg in this living variant. Palace gateway behind is tiny to emphasize monumental guardian presence, nonletter decorative masonry. Stern protective calm, natural golden dawn and rolling dust at hooves, majestic not malevolent. No elemental attack or invented aura. Coherent human head transitions into massive bull shoulders, wings fully readable. Do not mix lion body with bull legs.

visual_requirements.description: One immense Assyrian protective LAMASSU in living four-legged BULL variant: dignified bearded HUMAN HEAD, muscular BULL BODY and TWO broad BIRD WINGS. FOUR legs, no extra sculptural fifth leg in this living variant. Palace gateway behind is tiny to emphasize monumental guardian presence, nonletter decorative masonry. Stern protective calm, natural golden dawn and rolling dust at hooves, majestic not malevolent. No elemental attack or invented aura. Coherent human head transitions into massive bull shoulders, wings fully readable. Do not mix lion body with bull legs.
Protective monumental palace-gateway presence; basis: documented guardian hybrid frightens chaotic forces

basis_claims.quote: is a Mesopotamian protective deity.

statement.id: Lamassu adalah sosok ilahi pelindung Mesopotamia.
statement.en: Lamassu is a Mesopotamian protective deity.

basis_claims.quote: having a human head, the body of a bull or a lion, and bird wings

statement.id: Bentuk hibridanya menggabungkan kepala manusia, tubuh banteng atau singa, dan sayap burung.
statement.en: Its hybrid form combines a human head, a bull or lion body, and bird wings.

basis_claims.quote: Assyrian sculpture typically placed prominent pairs of lamassu at entrances in palaces

statement.id: Patung berpasangan lamassu ditempatkan pada pintu masuk istana Asyur.
statement.en: Pairs of lamassu sculptures stand at Assyrian palace entrances.

basis_claims.quote: In earlier versions, they have five legs

statement.id: Versi patung awal dapat memiliki lima kaki.
statement.en: Earlier sculptural versions can have five legs.

basis_claims.quote: who adorned palaces and temples to frighten off the forces of chaos.

statement.id: Lamassu menghiasi istana dan kuil untuk mengusir kekuatan kekacauan.
statement.en: Lamassu adorn palaces and temples to frighten away chaotic forces.

artistic_changes: Low-angle framing, painterly materials and environmental color are artistic rendering.
Effects are limited to the cited domains, deeds, attributes or iconography; natural light and scale supply presence where no elemental ability is documented.

presentation_revision.rationale: Big names (major gods, archangels, demon princes, primordial monsters, famous literary beings) must look imposing and powerful: an epic, awe-inspiring or terrifying presence that matches their standing in the tradition.

lightning-bird.depicted_variant: Black and white impundulu bird form

basis_claims.statement: The lightning bird or impundulu is a creature in the folklore of the Zulu people in South Africa.
basis_claims.statement_id: Burung petir atau impundulu adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat suku Zulu di Afrika Selatan.
basis_claims.quote: The lightning bird or impundulu or thekwane (or izulu, inyoni yezulu) is a creature in the folklore of the Zulu people.

basis_claims.statement: The impundulu takes the form of a black and white bird summoning thunder and lightning with its wings and talons.
basis_claims.statement_id: Impundulu berwujud burung hitam-putih seukuran manusia yang memanggil guntur dan kilat dengan sayapnya.
basis_claims.quote: The impundulu (which translates as "lightning bird") takes the form of a black and white bird, the size of a person, which is said to summon thunder and lightning with its wings and talons.

basis_claims.statement: Luanniao, or luan, is a legendary spirit bird of Chinese mythology.
basis_claims.statement_id: Luanniao atau luan adalah burung roh legenda mitologi Tiongkok.
basis_claims.quote: 鸞（らん）は中国神話の伝説の霊鳥。日本の江戸時代の百科事典『和漢三才図会』には、実在の鳥として記載されている。

basis_claims.statement: The Shuowen Jiezi describes red coloring, five-colored markings, and a chicken-like body.
basis_claims.statement_id: Shuowen Jiezi menggambarkannya merah dengan tanda lima warna dan tubuh menyerupai ayam.
basis_claims.quote: The Shuowen Jiezi defines the bird as born from the sperm of Chìdì. It is red in colour with five-coloured markings. Its body is shaped like that of a chicken. It sings in the five standard pitches and appears when hymns of praise are sung to rulers. It also described the luan as being "the essence of divine birds".

okubi.depicted_variant: Giant female head with blackened teeth

basis_claims.statement: Ōkubi is a giant-headed yōkai in Japanese tales.
basis_claims.statement_id: Ōkubi adalah yōkai berkepala besar dalam cerita Jepang.
basis_claims.quote: Ōkubi (大首) (おおくび) (the giant head) is a Japanese yōkai.

basis_claims.statement: It is commonly pictured as a large female head with blackened teeth.
basis_claims.statement_id: Wujudnya sering berupa kepala perempuan besar bergigi hitam.
basis_claims.quote: Its image is mostly a huge female head and has the characteristics of a married woman's teeth painted black.

basis_claims.statement: Onikuma is a bear yōkai from the Kiso Valley tradition.
basis_claims.statement_id: Onikuma adalah yōkai beruang dari tradisi Lembah Kiso.
basis_claims.quote: An onikuma (鬼熊, literally "demon bear") is a mythological Japanese yōkai originating in the Kiso Valley in Nagano Prefecture.

basis_claims.statement: It is described as walking upright.
basis_claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan berjalan tegak.
basis_claims.quote: It is a bear-like creature that has been known to walk upright.

basis_claims.statement: Accounts give it a size exceeding ordinary bears.
basis_claims.statement_id: Kisah-kisah memberinya ukuran yang melebihi beruang biasa.
basis_claims.quote: Onikuma continue growing and reach sizes much larger than even the largest natural bears.

basis_claims.statement: Its dwelling is said to lie deep in the mountains.
basis_claims.statement_id: Tempat tinggalnya konon jauh di pegunungan.
basis_claims.quote: They live deep in the mountains, far away from humans.

jimmy-squarefoot.depicted_variant: Tusked pig-headed biped with calico-wrapped feet

basis_claims.statement: Jimmy Squarefoot, a bipedal pig-headed creature of Manx folklore, Isle of Man.
basis_claims.statement_id: Jimmy Squarefoot, makhluk berkaki dua berkepala babi folklor Manx, Pulau Man (Isle of Man).
basis_claims.quote: In Manx folklore, Jimmy Squarefoot is a legendary bipedal pig-headed creature living on the Isle of Man.

basis_claims.statement: Ridden by a Foawr, stone-throwing giant of Cronk yn Irree Lhaa, husband of the Caillagh ny Groamagh; tusked pig-headed man or white boar.
basis_claims.statement_id: Ditunggangi Foawr, raksasa pelempar batu di Cronk yn Irree Lhaa, suami Caillagh ny Groamagh; lelaki berkepala babi bertaring atau babi hutan putih.
basis_claims.quote: He is thought to have once been ridden by an unnamed Foawr, a type of stone-throwing giant, living on Cronk yn Irree Lhaa who may have been the husband of the Caillagh ny Groamagh.

basis_claims.statement: Large feet wrapped in calico look square, hence the name Squarefoot.
basis_claims.statement_id: Kaki besar dibalut kain belacu tampak persegi, asal nama Squarefoot.
basis_claims.quote: Seine großen Füße sind mit Kaliko-Bändern umwickelt und wirken quadratisch, daher der Name „Squarefoot“.

basis_claims.statement: Kalavinka is an immortal Buddhist creature with a human head, bird body, and long tail.
basis_claims.statement_id: Kalavinka adalah makhluk abadi Buddha berkepala manusia dan berbadan burung dengan ekor panjang.
basis_claims.quote: is a fantastical immortal creature in Buddhism, with a human head and a bird's torso, with long flowing tail.

basis_claims.statement: The Japanese source compares human headed Chinese paintings with Japanese art giving the upper body a winged bodhisattva form.
basis_claims.statement_id: Sumber Jepang membandingkan lukisan Tiongkok berkepala manusia dengan seni Jepang yang memberi bagian atas berbentuk bodhisattva bersayap.
basis_claims.quote: 中国の仏教壁画などには人頭鳥身で表されるが、日本の仏教美術では、有翼の菩薩形の上半身に鳥の下半身の姿で描かれてきた。

krahang.depicted_variant: Flying loincloth-clad man with two winnowing baskets and pestle

basis_claims.statement: Krahang (กระหัง) is a male spirit of Thai folklore appearing as a shirtless man in a traditional loincloth who flies at night.
basis_claims.statement_id: Krahang (กระหัง) adalah roh laki-laki cerita rakyat Thailand yang tampil sebagai laki-laki bertelanjang dada bercawat tradisional yang terbang di malam hari.
basis_claims.quote: is a male spirit of the Thai folklore. It manifests itself as a shirtless man, wearing a traditional loincloth, who flies in the night.

basis_claims.statement: Krahang uses two kradong, round rice-winnowing baskets, to fly at night in rural Thailand, and often rides a long wooden rice-pounding pestle.
basis_claims.statement_id: Krahang memakai dua kradong, tampah bundar penampi beras, untuk terbang malam hari di pedesaan Thailand, dan sering menunggangi alu kayu panjang penumbuk padi.
basis_claims.quote: Krahang uses two large kradong (กระด้ง), round rice winnowing baskets, to fly in the night in rural areas of Thailand. It also often rides a sak tam khao (สากตำข้าว), the long wooden pestle of a traditional manual rice pounder.

likho.depicted_variant: One-eyed skinny old woman in black

basis_claims.statement: Likho (Polish licho) embodies evil fate and misfortune in Slavic mythology, a one-eyed creature often shown as a skinny old woman in black (One-eyed Likho) or an evil male forest goblin.
basis_claims.statement_id: Likho (Лихо, Polandia licho) adalah perwujudan nasib buruk dan kemalangan dalam mitologi Slavia, makhluk bermata satu yang sering digambarkan sebagai perempuan tua kurus berpakaian hitam (Likho Bermata Satu) atau goblin hutan laki-laki yang jahat.
basis_claims.quote: is an embodiment of evil fate and misfortune in Slavic mythology. A creature with one eye who is often depicted as an old, skinny woman in black (Лихо одноглазое, One-eyed Likho) or as an evil male goblin of forests.

basis_claims.statement: In the Russian folk tale "One-eyed Likho" it appears as a thin, one-eyed, man-eating giantess.
basis_claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng rakyat Rusia "Likho Bermata Satu", Likho tampil sebagai raksasa perempuan kurus bermata satu pemakan manusia.
basis_claims.quote: В русской народной сказке «Лихо одноглазое» предстаёт в образе худой одноглазой великанши-людоедки.

llamhigyn-y-dwr.depicted_variant: Legless frog with bat wings and stinging lizard tail

basis_claims.statement: Llamhigyn y Dŵr (Welsh for Water Leaper) is an evil creature of Welsh folklore of swamps and ponds.
basis_claims.statement_id: Llamhigyn y Dŵr (Wales/Welsh: Water Leaper, Pelompat Air) makhluk jahat cerita rakyat Wales, di rawa dan kolam; di Britania Raya.
basis_claims.quote: Llamhigyn y Dŵr (Welsh for 'Water Leaper') is an evil creature from Welsh folklore that lived in swamps and ponds.

basis_claims.statement: A giant frog with bat's wings, no legs, a lizard tail with a sting; leaps over water on its wings.
basis_claims.statement_id: Katak raksasa bersayap kelelawar, tanpa kaki, ekor kadal bersengat; melompat di air dengan sayap.

basis_claims.statement: A giant frog (grenouille géante) with bat (chauve-souris) wings for forelegs, no hind legs, a stinging lizard (lézard) tail.
basis_claims.statement_id: Katak raksasa (grenouille géante), sayap kelelawar (chauve-souris) menggantikan kaki depan, tanpa kaki belakang, ekor kadal (lézard) bersengat.
basis_claims.quote: Il est décrit comme une grenouille géante avec des ailes de chauve-souris à la place des pattes avant, sans pattes arrière et avec une longue queue de lézard avec un dard à la fin.

basis_claims.statement: A matagot is a spirit of French folklore that usually takes the form of a black cat.
basis_claims.statement_id: Matagot adalah roh dalam cerita rakyat Prancis yang biasanya berwujud kucing hitam.
basis_claims.quote: A Matagot is a spirit in French folklore that tends to take the form of a black cat.

basis_claims.statement: Matagots are generally evil, but some help, like the 'magician cat' that brings wealth to a home if well fed.
basis_claims.statement_id: Matagot umumnya jahat, tetapi sebagian dapat membantu, seperti "kucing penyihir" yang membawa kekayaan ke rumah bila diberi makan dengan baik.
basis_claims.quote: Matagots are generally evil, but some may prove helpful, like the "magician cat" said to bring wealth into a home if it is well fed.

basis_claims.statement: It roams mysterious places at night and returns at dawn with gold louis for its master; if neglected or unrewarded it takes offence and may take cruel revenge.
basis_claims.statement_id: Ia berkeliaran di tempat misterius pada malam hari dan pulang saat fajar membawa koin emas louis untuk tuannya; bila diabaikan atau tidak diberi imbalan, ia tersinggung dan dapat membalas dengan kejam.
basis_claims.quote: Il est censé se promener dans quelques lieux mystérieux pendant la nuit, et revenir à l'aube avec un stock de louis d'or pour son maître. Si celui-ci le néglige ou ne le récompense pas, le chat s'offense et peut se venger cruellement.

mongolian-death-worm.depicted_variant: Bright red headless legless sausage-shaped worm

basis_claims.statement_id: Cacing ini bertubuh gemuk, berwarna merah cerah, dan panjangnya 0,6 hingga 1,5 meter.
basis_claims.quote: Cacing ini bertubuh gemuk dan berwarna merah cerah, memiliki panjang 0.6 hingga 1.5 meter.

basis_claims.statement: Because it resembles a cow's intestine, locals call it olgoi-khorkhoi, "intestine worm".
basis_claims.statement_id: Karena mirip usus sapi, warga setempat menyebutnya olgoi-khorkhoi, "cacing usus".
basis_claims.quote: 牛の腸に似ていることから、現地ではオルゴイホルホイ（olgoi-khorkhoi、モンゴル語: олгой-хорхой、腸虫の意）と呼ばれている。

basis_claims.statement: The Dullahan (Dubhlachan, dúlachán) is a legendary creature of Irish folklore, a headless rider on a black horse or coachman carrying his own head.
basis_claims.statement_id: Dullahan (Dubhlachan, dúlachán) adalah makhluk legenda cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish folklore), penunggang kuda hitam tanpa kepala atau kusir yang membawa kepalanya sendiri.
basis_claims.quote: The Dullahan (Irish: Dubhlachan; dúlachán, /ˈduːləˌhɑːn/) is a type of legendary creature in Irish folklore. He is depicted as a headless rider on a black horse, or as a coachman, who carries his own head.

basis_claims.statement: The Dullahan is also called Colainn Gan Cheann, 'without a head' in Irish.
basis_claims.statement_id: Dullahan juga disebut Colainn Gan Cheann, tanpa kepala (without a head) dalam bahasa Irlandia (Irish).
basis_claims.quote: The Dullahan is also called Colainn Gan Cheann, meaning "without a head" in Irish.

basis_claims.quote: It looked like a large cream cheese hung round with black puddings: no speck of colour enlivened the ashy paleness of the depressed features; the skin lay stretched over the unearthly surface almost like the parchment head of a drum. basis_claims.statement_id: El Hombre Caimán ("Manusia Buaya") adalah legenda urban pesisir Karibia Kolombia di kota Plato: Saúl Montenegro yang gemar mengintip perempuan mandi berubah menjadi makhluk berkepala manusia dan bertubuh buaya.

enenra.depicted_variant: Enenra, Japanese smoke yokai: a single loosely human-shaped figure made entirely of swirling dark gray smoke rising from a small rural hearth fire. basis_claims.quote: Enenras mostly reside in bonfires; when they emerge, they take human shape or form.

basis_claims.quote: In fact, they were marked with a sacred rope called a shimenawa

statement.id: Pohon tua yang dihormati dapat ditandai dengan tali suci shimenawa.

basis_claims.quote: KODAMA are the tree spirits that live in the forest. They are invisible to human eyes

basis_claims.quote: Japanese images of dragons are a blend of three influences: China’s mythical dragon, the nāga of Hindu myth and Buddhist scripture, and native Japanese views of it as a water deity.

statement.id: Gambaran naga Jepang memadukan pengaruh naga Tiongkok, nāga Buddha, dan pandangan setempat tentang dewa air.
statement.en: Japanese dragon images blend Chinese dragons, Buddhist nāga, and local water-deity ideas.

basis_claims.quote: Dragons are associated with rain and have long been tied to folk beliefs about water, the creatures often being said to reside in the ocean or other bodies of water.

statement.id: Naga dikaitkan dengan hujan dan dipercaya mendiami laut atau perairan lain.
statement.en: Dragons are linked to rain and believed to dwell in seas or other waters.

basis_claims.quote: Dragons themselves are objects of worship at many shrines, where they are venerated for reasons like bringing rain, stopping floods, and ensuring health, long life, and luck.

statement.id: Di banyak kuil naga dipuja untuk hujan, perlindungan banjir, kesehatan, dan keberuntungan.
statement.en: At many shrines dragons are revered for rain, flood protection, health, and luck.

basis_claims.quote: These near-experimental visual effects, achieved through bold manipulation of the fluid medium, align with the traditional symbolism of dragons as masters of cloud and rain.

statement.id: Lukisan Kanō Tan’yū menampilkan naga sebagai penguasa awan dan hujan.
statement.en: Kanō Tan’yū’s painting draws on dragons’ symbolism as masters of cloud and rain.

basis_claims.quote: This pair of dragons is painted with extensive water washes, visible in the flowing marks where diluted black ink bleeds across the silk surface and creates the impression of rain falling through layered clouds.

statement.id: Sapuan tinta pada lukisan sepasang naga menimbulkan kesan hujan di tengah awan.
statement.en: Ink washes in a painting of paired dragons suggest rain through clouds.

basis_claims.quote: Lyngbakr (Icelandic, lyngi "heather" + bak "back") is the name of a massive whale-like sea monster reported in the Örvar-Odds saga to have existed in the Greenland Sea. According to the saga, Lyngbakr would bait seafarers by posing as a heather-covered island, and when a crew landed on his back, he sank into the sea, drowning the crew.

statement.id: Lyngbakr (Islandia: lyngi, "heather", + bak, "punggung") adalah monster laut raksasa mirip paus yang menurut Örvar-Odds saga hidup di Laut Greenland; ia memancing pelaut dengan menyamar sebagai pulau berlapis heather, dan bila awak mendarat di punggungnya, ia tenggelam dan menenggelamkan mereka.
statement.en: Lyngbakr (Icelandic lyngi 'heather' + bak 'back') is a massive whale-like sea monster said in the Örvar-Odds saga to live in the Greenland Sea; it baited seafarers by posing as a heather-covered island, then sank when a crew landed on its back, drowning them.

basis_claims.quote: Vignir explained to Oddr that, had they landed sooner, the crew would have surely drowned. The "rocks" and "island" must have been two sea monsters—Lyngbakr, the greatest whale in the world, and hafgufa

statement.id: Vignir menjelaskan kepada Oddr bahwa bila mereka mendarat lebih cepat, awak pasti tenggelam; "batu" dan "pulau" itu tentulah dua monster laut, Lyngbakr, paus terbesar di dunia, dan hafgufa.
statement.en: Vignir explained to Oddr that had they landed sooner the crew would surely have drowned; the 'rocks' and 'island' must have been two sea monsters, Lyngbakr, the greatest whale in the world, and hafgufa.

basis_claims.quote: Lyngbakurinn var talinn vera stærstur allra dýra í sjó og lá hann oft þannig á hálfu kafi að hann virtist vera eyja og leit þá út eins og þar á sé vaxið lyng og því er hann kallaður lyngbakur. Fjölmargar sögur eru um lyngbaka víða frá á Íslandi.

statement.id: Lyngbakur dianggap hewan laut terbesar dan sering terapung setengah tenggelam sehingga tampak seperti pulau yang ditumbuhi heather, karena itu disebut lyngbakur; banyak kisah tentangnya tersebar di Islandia.
statement.en: The lyngbakur was held the largest of all sea creatures, often lying half-submerged so it seemed an island grown with heather, hence its name; many tales of it are told across Iceland.

basis_claims.quote: The tilberi (carrier) or snakkur (spindle) is a creature of Icelandic folklore, created by witches to steal milk. Only women can create and own them.

statement.id: Tilberi atau snakkur adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Islandia yang dibuat penyihir untuk mencuri susu; hanya perempuan yang bisa membuat dan memilikinya.
statement.en: The tilberi or snakkur is an Icelandic folklore creature made by witches to steal milk; only women can make and own one.

basis_claims.quote: To create a tilberi, the woman steals a rib from a recently buried body early on Whitsunday, twists around it grey wool which she must steal for the purpose and keeps it between her breasts. ...  The next three Sundays at communion she spits the sanctified wine on the bundle, which will come more alive each time.

statement.id: Perempuan itu mencuri tulang rusuk jenazah yang baru dikubur pada dini hari Minggu Pentakosta, melilitnya dengan wol kelabu curian, dan menyimpannya di antara payudaranya.
statement.en: The woman steals a rib from a newly buried corpse early on Whitsunday, winds stolen grey wool round it and keeps it between her breasts.

basis_claims.quote: It will return to the window of her dairy and call out "Full belly, Mummy!" or "Churn lid off, Mummy!" and vomit the stolen milk into her butter churn. To suck the milk from the animal's udder, it jumps on her back and lengthens itself to reach down

statement.id: Tilberi kembali ke jendela ruang susu, berseru "Perut penuh, Ibu!", dan memuntahkan susu curian ke pengocok mentega; untuk menyedot ambing ia melompat ke punggung hewan dan memanjangkan diri.
statement.en: It returns to the dairy window, calls 'Full belly, Mummy!' and vomits the stolen milk into the churn; to suck an udder it leaps onto the animal's back and stretches itself down.

basis_claims.quote: The tilberi will then either work itself to death or die because as an evil creature it cannot tolerate the number three. Only the human bone will be left lying in the pasture.

statement.id: Tilberi akan bekerja sampai mati atau mati karena, sebagai makhluk jahat, tak tahan angka tiga; hanya tulang manusia yang tertinggal di padang.
statement.en: The tilberi either works itself to death or dies because, as an evil being, it cannot bear the number three; only the human bone remains in the pasture.

statement.en: Ryūjin means dragon kami and names a faith associated with dragons.

basis_claims.quote: Although Japanese ryūjin worship was influenced by China, the Japanese dragon as an object of faith was a deified snake, a symbol of a water kami (suijin).

statement.id: Pemujaan Ryūjin dipengaruhi Tiongkok; naga juga dipahami sebagai ular yang didewakan dan lambang dewa air.

Metal-covered eyes and gilded teeth

statement.en: One mask has gilt horns and teeth and disordered hair.

basis_claims.quote: Hannya is the Noh mask of a female ghost featured in songs, such as “Aoinoue (Lady Aoi)” and "Dojoji (Dojoji Temple).” It expresses “a woman’s face full of jealousy and resentment.” It has two horns, glittering eyes expressed with metal covers, shaggy hair and mouth cut open at the corners.

statement.id: Museum menyebut topeng hannya sebagai roh perempuan bertanduk dalam dua lakon.
statement.en: The museum describes a horned female-ghost mask used in two plays.

statement.id: Yanagita menerbitkan catatan cerita dari Fukuoka pada 1933.
statement.en: Yanagita published Fukuoka accounts in 1933.

basis_claims.quote: The nurikabe in Bakemono no e resembles a white elephant without a trunk, or perhaps a white lion-dog, or komainu, with three eyes and black fangs.

statement.id: Gulungan menampilkan sosok putih bermata tiga yang mirip gajah atau anjing singa.

basis_claims.quote: Some Japanese scholars, however, contend that the nurikabe illustrated in Bakemono no e and the nurikabe of folklore in Kyushu are not the same.

statement.id: Sebagian peneliti meragukan kesamaan nurikabe dalam lukisan dan cerita lisan.

Village-house setting associated with Urikohime tale
Malicious contrary deceitful aura

basis_claims.quote: Amanojaku is a small demon known for defying people, twisting words and actions, and teasing by doing the opposite of what is asked.

statement.id: Amanojaku adalah setan kecil yang melawan dan melakukan kebalikan permintaan.
statement.en: Amanojaku is described as a small demon that defies people and reverses requests.

basis_claims.quote: the young woman is visited by a suspicious spirit, Amanojaku, who already had her in his sights and ends up forcing its entrance.

statement.id: Amanojaku mendatangi Urikohime dan memaksa masuk ke rumah.
statement.en: Amanojaku comes to Urikohime and forces its way inside.

basis_claims.quote: In one version of the tale, the spirit kills the girl and uses her skin, taking her place

statement.id: Dalam satu versi, roh itu membunuh Urikohime dan menggantikannya.
statement.en: In one version, the spirit kills the girl and takes her place.

basis_claims.quote: But the hoax is also revealed - in the version where she is tied up, she screams for help and is eventually saved, the creature then being chased away.

statement.id: Tipu muslihat amanojaku terbongkar dan ia diusir.
statement.en: The deception is exposed and the creature is chased away.

visual_requirements: Apelike mind-reading yokai
Japanese mountain hut setting
Unsettling perceptive intelligence

basis_claims.quote: Satori (覚; "consciousness") in Japanese folklore are mind-reading monkey-like monsters ("yōkai") said to dwell within the mountains of Hida and Mino (presently Gifu Prefecture).

statement.id: Satori adalah yōkai mirip kera yang membaca pikiran dalam folklor pegunungan Hida dan Mino.
statement.en: Satori is a mind-reading, ape-like yōkai of the Hida and Mino mountains.

basis_claims.quote: Upon reading a person's mind, the satori would say the person's thoughts aloud faster than a human could.

statement.id: Satori dikatakan mengucapkan pikiran orang yang dibacanya dengan cepat.
statement.en: Satori is said to speak a person's thoughts aloud quickly.

basis_claims.quote: ■ 地域（都道府県名） 福島県 ■ 地域（市・郡名） 南会津郡 ■ 地域（区町村名） ■ 要約 昔爺様が山小屋で火に当たっていると、得体の知れない化け物がやって来た。爺さんの心の中を見透かすさとりの化け物だった。

statement.id: Catatan Fukushima menyebut makhluk Satori mendatangi seorang kakek di gubuk gunung dan membaca pikirannya.
statement.en: A Fukushima record tells of Satori visiting an old man in a mountain hut and reading his mind.

visual_requirements: Row of many offshore ghost lights
Brighter central parent lights
Viewed from elevated coastal ground

basis_claims.quote: Shiranui (不知火, unknown fire; Shiranuhi in the historical kana orthography) is an atmospheric ghost light told about in Kyushu.

statement.id: Shiranui adalah fenomena cahaya gaib dalam cerita rakyat Kyūshū.
statement.en: Shiranui is a ghost-light phenomenon in Kyūshū folklore.

basis_claims.quote: The phenomenon occurs several kilometers out from the shore in open water.

statement.id: Kisah-kisah menempatkan cahaya itu di perairan terbuka jauh dari pantai.
statement.en: Accounts place the lights offshore over open water.

basis_claims.quote: First, one or two flames called oyabi (親火, lit. "parent-fire") will appear.

statement.id: Kemunculannya konon diawali satu atau dua cahaya induk.
statement.en: An appearance is said to begin with one or two parent lights.

basis_claims.quote: These will split off to the left and right and multiply, eventually producing anywhere from several hundred to several thousand flames in a row.

statement.id: Cahaya itu kemudian membelah dan bertambah banyak membentuk deretan panjang.
statement.en: The lights then divide and multiply into a long row.

basis_claims.quote: They can be seen from elevated parts of the coast, but not from sea level.

statement.id: Cahaya itu dikatakan terlihat dari tempat tinggi di pesisir.
statement.en: The lights are described as visible from high coastal ground.

drak-mythology.depicted_variant: The documented fiery snake with duck's head variant, a small flying house spirit with luminous tail approaching a farmhouse chimney.
visual_requirements: Small fiery serpent with duck head
Long glowing tail
Flight toward farmhouse chimney
Uncanny dangerous household wealth-bringer aura
drak-mythology.aura: Uncanny fiery wealth-bringing household spirit, clever and potentially dangerous.

basis_claims.quote: Der Drak (oder auch Fürdrak, Drakel, Alf, Stöpke und Gluswanz genannt) ist ein fliegender Hausgeist. Obwohl er äußerlich einem Drachen ähnelt, hat er mit diesem wohl nichts gemeinsam.

statement.id: Drak (juga disebut Fürdrak, Drakel, Alf, Stöpke, dan Gluswanz) adalah roh rumah terbang; meski tampak seperti naga, ia agaknya tak ada kaitannya dengan naga.
statement.en: The Drak (also called Fürdrak, Drakel, Alf, Stöpke and Gluswanz) is a flying house spirit; though it looks like a dragon it probably has nothing in common with one.

basis_claims.quote: Er ist in Nord- und Mitteldeutschland beheimatet, sowie auch in angrenzenden slawischen Gebieten und bringt dem Bauern durch den Kamin Korn, Getreide, Butter, Speck, Schinken und Gold. Daher wurde vielen wohlhabenden Bauern auch nachgesagt, dass sie einen Drak in ihren Diensten hätten.

statement.id: Drak berasal dari Jerman utara dan tengah (Nord- und Mitteldeutschland) serta wilayah Slavia di sekitarnya, dan membawa gandum, mentega, daging asap, ham, dan emas kepada petani lewat cerobong; karena itu banyak petani kaya diisukan memelihara Drak.
statement.en: The Drak is at home in northern and central Germany (Nord- und Mitteldeutschland) and adjacent Slavic areas and brings the farmer corn, grain, butter, bacon, ham and gold through the chimney; hence many wealthy farmers were said to have a Drak in service.

basis_claims.quote: Das Erscheinungsbild eines Drak ist das eines kleinen Drachen mit glühendem Schweif, mit dem er durch die Lüfte zieht. Im östlichen Pommern kennt man ihn als Alf und mancherorts auch als feurige Schlange mit Entenkopf oder als glühenden Kessel mit Schwanz.

statement.id: Drak berwujud naga kecil berekor menyala yang melayang di udara; di Pomerania (Pommern) timur ia dikenal sebagai Alf, dan di beberapa tempat sebagai ular api berkepala bebek atau kuali menyala berekor.
statement.en: The Drak looks like a small dragon with a glowing tail as it travels through the air; in eastern Pomerania (Pommern) it is called Alf, and in places a fiery snake with a duck's head or a glowing kettle with a tail.

basis_claims.quote: Drac létá vzduchem a do domu vstupuje skrze komín či díru ve střeše. Má podobu hořícího bidla, mužíčka v červené vestě, nebo zvířete jako kuře, kohout či ještěrka. Jindy vypadá jako ohnivá koule či planoucí hvězda. Je úzce spjat s ohněm, což vedlo k ztotožňování s ďáblem, a přebývá v krbu nebo hluboko v peci.

statement.id: Drac terbang di udara dan masuk rumah lewat cerobong atau lubang atap; ia berwujud batang menyala, lelaki kecil berompi merah, atau hewan seperti ayam dan kadal, kadang bola api; ia erat dengan api dan tinggal di perapian atau jauh di dalam tungku.
statement.en: Drac flies through the air and enters by the chimney or a hole in the roof; it takes the form of a burning pole, a little man in a red vest, or an animal such as a hen or lizard, at times a fireball; it is closely bound to fire and lives in the hearth or deep in the oven.

basis_claims.quote: Drac je získáván skrze smlouvu s ďáblem, ale může se zrodit jinými způsoby. Líhne se například z vejce bez žloutku, proto se má takové vejce vyhodit. ... Draca bylo nutno živit, podávaly se mu tak pokrmy jako koláče, maso, mléko nebo jáhlová kaše. Když není krmen, tak se mstí, typicky založením požáru.

statement.id: Drac diperoleh lewat perjanjian dengan iblis atau menetas dari telur tanpa kuning; ia harus diberi makan kue, daging, susu, atau bubur jawawut, dan bila tidak diberi makan ia membalas dendam, biasanya dengan menyulut kebakaran.
statement.en: Drac is gained through a pact with the devil or hatches from a yolkless egg; it must be fed cakes, meat, milk or millet porridge, and if unfed it takes revenge, usually by setting a fire.

basis_claims.quote: Jorōgumo (Japanese: 絡新婦 (kanji), じょろうぐも (hiragana)) is a type of yōkai, a creature of Japanese folklore. It can shapeshift into a beautiful woman

statement.en: Jorōgumo is a yōkai that can appear as a woman.

basis_claims.quote: Toriyama Sekien’s “Jorōgumo” overlays spider legs onto the robed body of a woman with long hair, surrounded by a swarm of tiny spiders.

statement.id: Ilustrasi Sekien menampilkan perempuan berkaki laba-laba dikelilingi laba-laba kecil.
statement.en: Sekien’s illustration shows a spider-legged woman surrounded by smaller spiders.

basis_claims.quote: Sekien provided no accompanying text outlining supernatural abilities.

statement.id: Ilustrasi itu tidak disertai uraian tentang kekuatan gaib.

statement.en: Umibōzu is a sea yōkai.

statement.en: The name umibōzu is glossed as sea monk.

basis_claims.quote: Normally, umibōzu appears to sailors on calm seas which quickly turn tumultuous.

statement.id: Ia muncul di laut tenang yang kemudian bergolak.
statement.en: It appears on calm seas that turn rough.

basis_claims.quote: It either breaks the ship on emergence or demands a bucket or barrel from the sailors and proceeds to drown them.

statement.id: Ia dapat merusak kapal atau meminta wadah untuk menenggelamkannya.
statement.en: It may break or flood a ship.

basis_claims.quote: Utagawa Kuniyoshi's Tōkaidō gojyūsantugi: Kuwana depicts a sailor from Kuwana, named Tokuzo, who encounters a giant umi-bōzu offshore.

statement.id: Cetakan Kuniyoshi menampilkan Tokuzō bertemu umibōzu raksasa.

statement.id: Tesso adalah yōkai yang dikaitkan dengan tikus dan arwah pendendam biksu Raigō.
statement.en: Tesso is a rat-associated yōkai linked to the monk Raigō’s vengeful spirit.

basis_claims.quote: As a reward, Raigō requested for the construction of an ordination platform (kaidan) building for Mii-dera, but opposition forces from Enryaku-ji at Mount Hiei obstructed this and prevented it from being granted.

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, pembangunan balai penahbisan yang diminta Raigō dihalangi kuil saingannya.
statement.en: One tale says Raigō’s requested ordination hall was blocked by a rival temple.

basis_claims.quote: In the yomihon versions of the Heike Monogatari such as Enkyōhon (延慶本, alternatively read Enkeihon) and Nagatohon (長門本) and in the different book Genpei Jōsuiki, among other sources, the grudges of Raigō became a giant rat and ate away at the sacred books in Enryaku-ji.

statement.id: Beberapa versi tertulis menggambarkan dendamnya menjadi tikus raksasa yang merusak kitab suci.

basis_claims.quote: Its body was as hard as stone and its teeth and claws as strong as iron.

statement.id: Tikus gaib itu digambarkan bertubuh sekeras batu.
statement.en: The monstrous rat is described as having a stone-hard body.

Exactly three independent countable legs
Kumano mountain path and solar dawn
Dignified auspicious sacred guide aura

basis_claims.quote: In the ancient Japanese chronicles Kojiki and Nihon shoki, the Yatagarasu appeared as a servant of Amaterasu-no-Okami, the goddess of the sun.

statement.id: Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki menampilkannya sebagai pelayan Amaterasu.

basis_claims.quote: It was sent to guide the legendary first emperor Jimmu from Kumano to present-day Nara

statement.id: Ia diutus membimbing Jimmu dari Kumano ke Nara.
statement.en: It was sent to guide Jimmu from Kumano to Nara.

basis_claims.quote: The Yatagarasu is both a deity of guidance and a servant of the Kumano deities, including Amaterasu-no-Okami.

statement.id: Yatagarasu disebut dewa penuntun dan pelayan dewa-dewa Kumano.
statement.en: Yatagarasu is called a guiding deity and servant of Kumano deities.

basis_claims.quote: Okami (淤加美神, Okami-no-kami) in the Kojiki, or in the Nihon Shoki: Kuraokami (闇龗) or Okami (龗), is a legendary Japanese dragon and Shinto deity of rain and snow.

statement.id: Kuraokami adalah dewa naga Jepang yang berkaitan dengan hujan dan salju.

basis_claims.quote: The name Kuraokami combines kura 闇 "dark; darkness; closed" and okami 龗 "dragon tutelary of water".

statement.id: Unsur pertama namanya dikaitkan dengan kegelapan.

basis_claims.quote: Then, the blood pooling on the hilt of Izanaki’s sword oozed from between his fingers. The deity that thereupon came into existence was named Kura okami no kami 闇淤加美 神. Next [appeared] Kura mitsuha no kami 闇御津羽神 (8).

statement.id: Versi Kojiki menghubungkan Kuraokami dengan darah yang menetes di antara jari Izanaki.

basis_claims.quote: depicts a scorpion-like creature (or a cross between a serpent, bird or a lobster with pincer claws similar to that of a crab or a scorpion)

statement.id: Gambar Sekien menunjukkan bentuk mirip kalajengking dengan capit.
statement.en: Sekien depicts a scorpionlike being with pincers.

basis_claims.quote: but since Sekien supplies no explanatory text, it is not certain what kind of yōkai it is.

statement.id: Sekien tidak memberi teks penjelas tentang jenis makhluk.

karura.depicted_variant: 734 Karura statue-inspired armored birdlike warrior, not Gigaku mask
visual_requirements: Armored birdlike humanoid warrior
Pronounced beak and bird eyes with humanlike ears/hair
Two arms and two legs, selected statue variant
Dignified sacred Buddhist guardian aura

basis_claims.quote: Karura is one of the Eight Kinds of Mythological Beings, representing a bird or birdlike being that devours snakes.

statement.id: Karura adalah makhluk mirip burung pemakan ular dari Delapan Golongan Makhluk Mitologis.
statement.en: Karura is a snake-eating birdlike being among the Eight Kinds.

basis_claims.quote: It is derived from Hindu, Buddhist and Jain mythology in India, and based on Garuda, the mythical bird of Hinduism.

statement.id: Karura berasal dari Garuda dalam mitologi India.
statement.en: Karura derives from India’s mythical Garuda.

basis_claims.quote: Karura is thus depicted as an armored warrior with a prominent beak and avian eyes but humanlike ears and hair.

statement.id: Patung menampilkan prajurit berparuh dan bermata burung tetapi bertelinga serta berambut manusia.
statement.en: The statue has an armored birdlike warrior with humanlike ears and hair.

basis_claims.quote: Karura is a deified bird. In Indian mythology, the Karura was a sacred bird that ate the poisonous snake. When this deity was taken into Buddhism, it became one of the gods who guard the Buddhist faith.

statement.id: Burung suci pemakan ular menjadi pelindung dalam Buddhisme.
statement.en: The sacred snake-eating bird became a Buddhist guardian.

basis_claims.quote: The work is dated to 734 and was made by the hollow-core dry-lacquer sculpting technique.

statement.id: Patung Karura dibuat pada 734.
statement.en: The Karura statue is dated to 734.

waira.depicted_variant: Source-preserved Edo scroll upper-body form; hind-body anatomy deliberately left unseen
visual_requirements: Bulky grotesque lumpy upper-body form
Two forelimbs with exactly one thick claw each
Lower/back half concealed because unknown
Mountain habitat
Uncanny frightening looming aura

basis_claims.quote: The waira (わいら) is a Japanese yōkai from Japanese emaki (handscrolls) such as the Hyakkai Zukan by Sawaki Suushi and books such as Gazu Hyakki Yagyō (1776) by Sekien Toriyama.

statement.id: Waira adalah yōkai yang digambar dalam gulungan dan buku bergambar Jepang.
statement.en: Waira is a yōkai pictured in Japanese scrolls and illustrated books.

basis_claims.quote: Lee Library, Brigham Young University) it is depicted with the body of a giant ox and thick sharp claws growing on each of its front legs.

statement.id: Gambar-gambarnya memberi tubuh mirip sapi dan cakar depan yang tajam.
statement.en: Pictures give it an ox-like body and sharp front claws.

basis_claims.quote: Each of these sources have no explanatory text besides their name, and furthermore there do not exist any documents recording any folk legends about them, so it is unknown what kind of yōkai these were intending to depict.

statement.id: Gambar lama tidak menjelaskan sifatnya, dan catatan rakyat yang jelas belum ditemukan.
statement.en: The old pictures do not explain its nature, and clear folk records are lacking.

basis_claims.quote: All of the pictures depict only the upper body, and there have been no pictures found that depict its lower half, so it is unknown what its whole body looks like.

statement.id: Gambar awal yang dibahas hanya menampilkan bagian atas tubuhnya.
statement.en: Only its upper body is shown in the early pictures discussed.

basis_claims.quote: Behavior : Waira live deep in the mountains, near heavily wooded temples and shrines.

basis_claims.quote: During harvest season Feldgeister flee deeper into the fields to escape the mowers. With the last cornstalks the corn spirit becomes trapped. Either it is killed by cutting the grain heads, threshing the corn or it is brought to the village in a ceremonial manner, shaped as a corn doll. Direct contact to the Feldgeist causes illness.

statement.id: Feldgeister (Feldgeist, Korndämonen) adalah roh gandum dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang sering juga roh angin; saat panen mereka lari makin dalam ke ladang, terperangkap di batang terakhir, lalu dibunuh dengan dipotong atau diirik, atau dibawa ke desa dengan upacara sebagai boneka gandum; sentuhan langsung menyebabkan sakit.
statement.en: Feldgeister (Feldgeist, Korndämonen) are corn spirits of German folklore, often also wind spirits; at harvest they flee deeper into the field, are trapped in the last stalks, then killed by cutting or threshing, or brought ceremonially to the village as a corn doll; direct contact causes illness.

basis_claims.quote: The Roggenwolf ("rye wolf"), Getreidewolf ("grain wolf") or Kornwolf ("corn wolf") is a field spirit shaped as a wolf. The Roggenwolf steals children and feeds on them.

statement.id: Roggenwolf ("serigala gandum hitam") adalah roh ladang berwujud serigala yang mencuri dan memakan anak-anak; contoh lain mencakup Roggenmuhme, Hafermann, dan Kornkind yang berwujud manusia.
statement.en: The Roggenwolf ('rye wolf') is a wolf-shaped field spirit that steals and eats children; other examples include the human-shaped Roggenmuhme, Hafermann and Kornkind.

basis_claims.quote: Die Anwesenheit eines Korndämons wird im Wogen des Korns gesehen und findet sich auch in Redensarten wie „Die Kornmutter ist im Feld“ wieder.

statement.id: Kehadiran setan gandum terlihat pada gandum yang bergelombang dan tercermin dalam ungkapan seperti "Ibu Gandum (Kornmutter) ada di ladang" (Corn Mother).
statement.en: A corn demon's presence is seen in the waving of the grain and appears in sayings like 'the Corn Mother (Kornmutter) is in the field'.

statement.id: Jenny Greenteeth (Wicked Jenny, Ginny Greenteeth, Grinteeth) sosok cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), nenek sihir sungai mirip Peg Powler, dari grindylow (Grindylow), menenggelamkan anak dan orang tua; di Britania Raya.
statement.en: Jenny Greenteeth (Wicked Jenny, Ginny Greenteeth, Grinteeth) is an English folklore river-hag like Peg Powler, from the grindylow, drowning children and the elderly.

basis_claims.quote: The name is also used to describe pondweed or duckweed, which can form a continuous mat over the surface of a small body of water, making it misleading and potentially treacherous, especially to unwary children. basis_claims.quote: They appear on rainy nights in streets and alleys where people travel.

statement.en: Its movements between people’s legs make walking difficult.

statement.id: Ia tidak digambarkan sengaja mencelakai, meskipun dapat membuat orang tersandung.

basis_claims.quote: Selkolla (literally 'seal-head') is a supernatural being in Icelandic folklore. She is described as a fair woman that is sometimes seen having the head of a seal. She is most prominently attested as an antagonist of Bishop Guðmundur Arason (1161–1237). Tales of Selkolla are noted for combining Christian ideas with concepts found in Scandinavian non-Christian traditions.

statement.id: Selkolla (harfiah "kepala anjing laut") adalah makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Islandia (Icelandic), perempuan cantik yang kadang terlihat berkepala anjing laut; ia terutama tercatat sebagai lawan Uskup Guðmundur Arason (1161–1237), dan kisahnya memadukan gagasan Kristen (Christian) dengan konsep tradisi Skandinavia (Scandinavian) non-Kristen.
statement.en: Selkolla ('seal-head') is a supernatural being of Icelandic folklore, a fair woman sometimes seen with a seal's head; she is chiefly attested as an antagonist of Bishop Guðmundur Arason (1161–1237), and her tales mix Christian ideas with Scandinavian non-Christian concepts.

basis_claims.quote: It is then said that a certain woman is "newly arrived in the district, sometimes with an ordinary face but sometimes with a seal's head. This devil walked about as boldly by day as by night, for which reason this midday-devil was called Selkolla in the district".

statement.id: Lalu disebutkan seorang perempuan baru tiba di daerah itu, kadang berwajah biasa, kadang berkepala anjing laut; setan ini berkeliaran berani siang maupun malam, sehingga "setan tengah hari" ini disebut Selkolla.
statement.en: Then a woman is said to have newly arrived in the district, sometimes with an ordinary face, sometimes with a seal's head; this devil walked boldly by day and night, so this midday-devil was called Selkolla.

basis_claims.quote: First, in the guise of the farmer's wife, she tries to entice him into having sex. When he realises what is actually going on, he tries to turn for home, but Selkolla bars his way

statement.id: Mula-mula, menyamar sebagai istri petani, ia mencoba merayunya; ketika petani menyadarinya dan hendak pulang, Selkolla menghalangi jalannya.
statement.en: First, disguised as the farmer's wife, she tries to seduce him; when he realises and turns for home, Selkolla bars his way.

basis_claims.quote: Selkolla er kynjavera í íslenskri þjóðtrú. Hún er falleg kona, en sést stundum með selshöfuð.

statement.id: Selkolla adalah makhluk ajaib dalam kepercayaan rakyat Islandia (íslenskri); ia perempuan cantik yang kadang terlihat berkepala anjing laut.
statement.en: Selkolla is a wondrous being of Icelandic (íslenskri) folk belief; a beautiful woman, sometimes seen with a seal's head.

statement.en: The sparrow turned the twig lengthwise before building it in; the Ulmers then saw the light and laid the beam lengthwise on their cart rather than across as before; the Ulmer Spatz is a landmark (Wahrzeichen) of Ulm.
