basis_claims.quote: They would come at night to one's pillow side and flip over the pillow.

statement.id: Ia konon membalik bantal orang yang tidur pada malam hari.
statement.en: It is said to turn over a sleeper’s pillow at night.

basis_claims.quote: In the Edo Period collection of yōkai pictures, the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō, they are depicted as a miniature Niō.

statement.id: Ilustrasi zaman Edo menggambarkannya sebagai penjaga Niō kecil.
statement.en: An Edo-period illustration depicts a miniature Niō guardian.

visual_requirements: Iron cooking pot head
Hand holding votive tablet
Animated household-object aura

basis_claims.quote: Narigama (鳴釜; or Narikama, Narukama) or Kamanari (釜鳴) is a Japanese yōkai depicted in Toriyama Sekien's yōkai art collection Gazu Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro.

statement.id: Narigama adalah yōkai yang digambar oleh Toriyama Sekien.
statement.en: Narigama is a yōkai illustrated by Toriyama Sekien.

basis_claims.quote: It is depicted as a hairy figure wearing a kama (iron pot) on its head and holding an ema (votive tablet) in its hand.

statement.id: Gambarnya memakai panci besi di kepala.
statement.en: Its image wears an iron cooking pot on its head.

basis_claims.quote: It is depicted as a hairy figure wearing a kama (iron pot) on its head and holding an ema (votive tablet) in its hand.

statement.id: Sosok itu memegang papan persembahan.
statement.en: The figure holds a votive tablet.

basis_claims.quote: The terms Narigama and Kamanari themselves refer to Shinto rituals in which fortune (good or bad luck) is judged based on the sound produced when a pot is heated with fire, or to folk beliefs that view a pot making unexpected sounds as an omen of good or bad luck.

statement.id: Namanya juga merujuk pada ramalan melalui bunyi panci yang dipanaskan.
statement.en: Its name also refers to divination through the sound of a heated pot.

kuzuryu.depicted_variant: Revered Kuzuryu Daimyojin nine-headed Lake Ashi water dragon
visual_requirements: Exactly nine heads on one shared serpentine body
Wingless water dragon
Lake Ashi/Hakone context
Majestic sacred deity aura
kuzuryu.aura: majestic reverent sacred protective water deity

basis_claims.quote: Kuzuryū (九頭龍, nine-headed dragon), or Kuzuryūshin (九頭龍神, nine-headed dragon god) is a deity that appears in folklore and legends of various parts of Japan, including, for example, Hakone (Kanagawa), Nagano Prefecture and Fukui Prefecture.

statement.id: Kuzuryū adalah dewa naga berkepala sembilan dari Jepang.
statement.en: Kuzuryū is a Japanese nine-headed dragon deity.

basis_claims.quote: In many cases, the Kuzuryū is associated with water.

statement.id: Naga itu biasanya dikaitkan dengan air.
statement.en: The dragon is commonly associated with water.

basis_claims.quote: During the Nara period, a legend arose that the Nine-headed Dragon had settled in Lake Ashi in Hakone, and that it demanded a sacrifice.

statement.id: Legenda Hakone menempatkan naga penuntut kurban di Danau Ashi.
statement.en: The Hakone legend places a dragon demanding sacrifices in Lake Ashi.

basis_claims.quote: As a result of this legend, the dragon came to be worshipped as Kuzuryū Daimyōjin (九頭竜大明神, "Great God Nine-Headed Dragon).

statement.id: Legenda itu menghasilkan pemujaan sebagai Kuzuryū Daimyōjin.
statement.en: The legend leads to worship as Kuzuryū Daimyōjin.

basis_claims.quote: Like most dragons, kuzuryū have power over rain and water.

statement.id: Kisah belakangan memberi para naga kuasa atas hujan dan air.
statement.en: A later account assigns the dragons power over rain and water.

visual_requirements: Blue-white ghost fire with face
Undamaged conifer forest
No solid body

basis_claims.quote: The tsurubebi (釣瓶火, "bucket fire") is a fire yōkai that appears in the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō by Toriyama Sekien.

statement.id: Tsurubebi adalah yōkai api yang digambar oleh Toriyama Sekien.
statement.en: Tsurubebi is a fire yōkai depicted by Toriyama Sekien.

basis_claims.quote: Tsurubebi are small tree spirits which appear at night, deep in coniferous forests.

statement.id: Satu kisah menggambarkannya sebagai roh pohon malam hari di hutan konifer.
statement.en: One account portrays it as a nocturnal tree spirit in coniferous forests.

basis_claims.quote: They take the form of blueish-white orbs of fire which bob up and down in the branches, occasionally dropping to the forest floor and floating back up into the trees.

statement.id: Ia muncul sebagai api putih kebiruan yang bergerak antara cabang dan tanah.
statement.en: It appears as bluish-white fire moving between branches and the ground.

basis_claims.quote: Sometimes the vague shape of a human or bestial face can be seen in the flames.

statement.id: Wajah manusia atau hewan kadang terlihat di dalam apinya.
statement.en: A human or animal face may be visible in its flames.

basis_claims.quote: Their flames produce no heat and do not burn the trees that they live in; nor do these yokai pose any other known threat.

statement.id: Apinya digambarkan tidak menghasilkan panas atau merusak pohon.
statement.en: Its fire is described as producing no heat or damage to trees.

visual_requirements: Horse-headed clothed yokai
Humanlike sitting posture
Eerie former-owner household haunting

basis_claims.quote: is one of the 16 yōkai depicted in the Tosa Obake Zōshi, drawn during the Edo period; it appears as a skeletal, flaming horse, claimed to be the spirit of a horse that perished in a fire.

statement.id: Bakotsu adalah yōkai kuda yang digambar dalam Tosa Obake Zōshi zaman Edo.
statement.en: Bakotsu is a horse yōkai pictured in the Edo-period Tosa Obake Zōshi.

basis_claims.quote: 'horse bone') is one of the 16 yōkai depicted in the Tosa Obake Zōshi, drawn during the Edo period;

statement.id: Namanya secara harfiah berarti tulang kuda.
statement.en: Its name literally means horse bone.

basis_claims.quote: Behavior : Bakotsu are formed from horses that burned to death in fires.

statement.id: Ia konon muncul dari kuda yang mati dalam kebakaran.
statement.en: It is said to arise from a horse that dies in a fire.

basis_claims.quote: Bakotsu look like horses, however they also have several human-like characteristics–they wear clothes and sit on their haunches like a person.

statement.id: Satu kisah memberinya pakaian dan posisi duduk seperti manusia.
statement.en: One account gives it clothing and a human-like sitting posture.

basis_claims.quote: The resentful spirits of the horses, angry at being subjected to such a terrifying and painful death, transform into monsters and haunt their former owners.

statement.id: Kisah itu menggambarkannya menghantui bekas pemilik kuda.
statement.en: That account describes it haunting the horse’s former owner.

basis_claims.quote: The two appear to be sitting and talking beneath a mosquito net.

statement.id: Gulungan itu menggambarkan dua yōkai bersama di bawah kelambu.
statement.en: The scroll depicts two yōkai together beneath a mosquito net.

visual_requirements: Man-sized owllike humanoid
Pointed feather ear tufts and glowing eyes
Black claws and feathered wings

basis_claims.quote: In Cornish folklore, the Owlman (Cornish: Kowanden ), also known as the Cornish Owlman or Owlman of Mawnan, is an owl-like humanoid creature reportedly sighted in 1976 in the village of Mawnan, Cornwall, United Kingdom. The reported sightings of the creature flying above the local church tower have been interpreted by some as misidentifications of a barn owl

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Cornwall (Cornish folklore), Owlman (Cornish: Kowanden; Cornish Owlman, Owlman of Mawnan) humanoid mirip burung hantu, terlihat 1976 di Mawnan, Cornwall, Britania Raya (United Kingdom); terbang di atas menara gereja; mungkin burung hantu gudang.
statement.en: In Cornish folklore the Owlman (Cornish Kowanden; Cornish Owlman, Owlman of Mawnan) is an owl-like humanoid seen in 1976 at Mawnan, Cornwall, United Kingdom, flying over the church tower; perhaps a barn owl.

basis_claims.quote: The story originated with Tony "Doc" Shiels, who had been involved in a series of "monster-raising" exploits in 1976. Shiels claimed to have investigated a report of two young girls on holiday in Mawnan who allegedly saw a large winged creature hovering above the tower of St Mawnan and St Stephen's Church, Mawnan on 17 April 1976.

statement.id: Kisah dari Tony Doc Shiels; dua gadis melihat makhluk bersayap di atas menara gereja Mawnan, 17 April 1976. Kowanden
statement.en: The story came from Tony Doc Shiels; two girls saw a winged creature above Mawnan church tower, 17 April 1976.

basis_claims.quote: The account states that the two girls were camping when they encountered a creature described as a "big owl with pointed ears, as big as a man", with glowing eyes and black, pincer-like claws.

statement.id: 3 Juli: Sally Chapman dan Barbara Perry melihat burung hantu besar bertelinga runcing sebesar manusia, mata menyala, cakar hitam.
statement.en: 3 July: Sally Chapman and Barbara Perry saw a big owl with pointed ears, as big as a man, glowing eyes, black claws.

visual_requirements: Tiny scaly greenish humanoid
Very long arms with sharp claws
Sharp teeth and frightening aquatic predator aura

basis_claims.quote: In English folklore, Grindylow or Grundylow is a creature in the counties of Yorkshire and Lancashire. The name is thought to be connected to Grendel, a name or term used in Beowulf and in many Old English charters where it is seen in connection with meres, bogs and lakes.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), Grindylow (Grundylow) makhluk Yorkshire dan Lancashire; nama terkait Grendel (Beowulf, Inggris Kuno/Old English); di Britania Raya.
statement.en: In English folklore the Grindylow (Grundylow) is a creature of Yorkshire and Lancashire; its name is linked to Grendel (Beowulf, Old English).

basis_claims.quote: Grindylows are supernatural creatures that appear in the folklore of England, most notably the Lancaster area. They are described as diminutive humanoids with scaly skin, a greenish complexion, sharp claws and teeth, and long, wiry arms with lengthy fingers at the end.

statement.id: Humanoid kecil bersisik, kehijauan, cakar dan gigi tajam, lengan panjang; terutama Lancaster.
statement.en: Tiny scaly greenish humanoids with sharp claws and teeth and long arms; especially Lancaster.

basis_claims.quote: They are said to dwell in ponds and marshes waiting for unsuspecting children, which they grab with their shockingly strong grip, and then drag under the surface of the waters.

statement.id: Tinggal di kolam dan rawa, menangkap anak dengan cengkeraman kuat dan menyeretnya ke air.
statement.en: They dwell in ponds and marshes, seizing children with a strong grip and dragging them under.

visual_requirements: Black skin, emerald eyes and dragonlike beard
Male fearsome-faced humanoid
Gentle grieving demeanor and ruby tears
samebito.aura: Gentle sorrowful sea exile despite fearsome visage

basis_claims.quote: is a creature that appears in "The Gratitude of the Samebito", a short story by Lafcadio Hearn.

statement.id: Samebito adalah manusia hiu dalam dongeng yang diceritakan ulang Lafcadio Hearn.
statement.en: Samebito is the shark-person in a folktale retold by Lafcadio Hearn.

basis_claims.quote: It is described as a shark-like humanoid with inky black skin, emerald green eyes, a face like a demon's, and a beard like a dragon's.

statement.id: Ia berkulit hitam, bermata zamrud, berwajah mirip iblis, dan berjanggut mirip naga.
statement.en: He has black skin, emerald eyes, a demonic face and a dragonlike beard.

basis_claims.quote: Although frightening, the creature turns out to be a gentle being who, as punishment for a petty fault, has been expelled from the sea by his former employer Ryūjin.

statement.en: Despite his frightening appearance, he is gentle and expelled from the sea by Ryūjin.
statement.id: Meskipun penampilannya menakutkan, ia lembut dan diusir dari laut oleh Ryūjin.

basis_claims.quote: When the Samebito learns that his master is on his deathbed, he begins to cry tears of blood which become precious rubies when they hit the ground.

statement.id: Air matanya yang seperti darah mengeras menjadi rubi.
statement.en: His bloodlike tears harden into rubies.

basis_claims.quote: Literally, "a Shark-Person," but in this story the Samébito is a male.

statement.id: Catatan Hearn secara tegas menyebut manusia hiu ini laki-laki.
statement.en: Hearn’s note explicitly describes this shark-person as male.

kotobuki-folklore.depicted_variant: Twelve-zodiac composite with each documented anatomical component
visual_requirements: Rat head, rabbit ears, ox horns, rooster comb, goat beard
Scaled dragon neck and horse mane
Tiger shoulders, monkey forearms, boar back
Dog hind legs and snake tail
Auspicious protective aura

basis_claims.quote: is a yōkai in Japanese mythology.

statement.id: Kotobuki adalah yōkai dalam mitologi Jepang.
statement.en: Kotobuki is a yōkai in Japanese mythology.

basis_claims.quote: The Kotobuki is a Japanese Chimera that has the parts of the creatures of the animals on the Chinese zodiac where it sports the head of a rat, the ears of a rabbit, the horns of an ox, the comb of a rooster, the beard of a goat, the neck of a dragon, the mane of a horse, the shoulders of a tiger, the arms of a monkey, the back of a boar, the hind legs of a dog, and the tail of a snake.

statement.id: Tubuh gabungannya memadukan ciri dua belas hewan zodiak.
statement.en: Its composite body combines features of all twelve zodiac animals.

basis_claims.quote: the head of a rat, the ears of a rabbit, the horns of an ox

statement.id: Kepalanya memadukan kepala tikus dengan telinga kelinci dan tanduk sapi.
statement.en: Its head combines a rat’s head with rabbit ears and ox horns.

basis_claims.quote: the back of a boar, the hind legs of a dog, and the tail of a snake.

statement.id: Ia memiliki punggung babi hutan, kaki belakang anjing, dan ekor ular.
statement.en: It has a boar’s back, dog hind legs and a snake tail.

basis_claims.quote: Merely possessing an image of the kotobuki was thought to be enough to protect a person from sickness and disease.

statement.id: Gambarnya dipercaya melindungi pemilik dari penyakit.
statement.en: Images were believed to protect their owners from disease.

hito-gitsune.depicted_variant: Hearn's weasel-sized body with fox tail
visual_requirements: Weasel-sized mustelid body and muzzle
Bushy fox tail
Four legs one tail
Eerie secretive possession aura
hito-gitsune.aura: eerie secretive potentially dangerous possession spirit

basis_claims.quote: Hito-gitsune or ninko (人狐) is a type of spirit possession told about in legends of the Chūgoku region of western Japan.

statement.id: Hito-gitsune adalah roh perasuk dalam tradisi wilayah Chūgoku di Jepang barat.
statement.en: Hito-gitsune are possessing spirits in traditions of western Japan’s Chūgoku region.

basis_claims.quote: They are said to be the spirit of a Japanese marten-like animal, and it is said that those possessed by one would be afflicted with stomach aches and mental abnormalities.

statement.id: Roh digambarkan mirip marten, dengan kerasukan membawa penyakit dan gangguan pikiran.
statement.en: The spirit is described as martenlike, with possession bringing illness and mental disturbance.

basis_claims.quote: It is no larger than a weasel, and somewhat similar in shape, except for its tail, which is like the tail of any other fox.

statement.en: Hearn describes a weasel-sized body with a fox’s tail.
statement.id: Hearn menggambarkan tubuh seukuran cerpelai dengan ekor rubah.

basis_claims.quote: It is rarely seen, keeping itself invisible, except to those to whom it attaches itself.

statement.en: It stays invisible to people other than those it attaches to.
statement.id: Ia tetap tidak terlihat oleh orang selain mereka yang ditempelinya.

fanggen.depicted_variant: The Alpine giant Fängge described by Alpenburg: a huge hairy wild woman with distorted wide mouth, lichen-tangled black hair and bark-and-fur clothing.
visual_requirements: Female forest giantess as tall as a tree
Coarse dark hair and distorted wide-mouthed face
Black tangled hair hung with tree lichens
Tree-bark jacket and fur apron
Frightening Alpine forest presence
fanggen.aura: Terrifying primitive forest giantess, enormous wild elemental presence.

basis_claims.quote: The Fängge has been conceived of strictly as female, a hairy, ugly giantess (counterpart of the moss-grown male giant or wild man). However, the gender demarcation is vague.

statement.id: Fängge dibayangkan khusus perempuan, raksasa perempuan berbulu dan buruk rupa (padanan raksasa lelaki atau lelaki liar berlumut), meski batas jenis kelaminnya kabur.
statement.en: The Fängge is conceived as strictly female, a hairy, ugly giantess (counterpart of the moss-grown male giant or wild man), though the gender line is vague.

basis_claims.quote: The Fängge (var. Fangga ) is a giantess as tall as a tree, according to the lore of Tyrol and the Bavarian Alps.

statement.id: Menurut cerita Tirol (Tyrol) dan Alpen Bayern (Bavarian Alps), Fängge (Fangga) adalah raksasa perempuan setinggi pohon.
statement.en: Per the lore of Tyrol and the Bavarian Alps, the Fängge (Fangga) is a giantess as tall as a tree.

basis_claims.quote: riesengroß, am ganzen Körper behaart, geborstet, das Antlitz verzerrt, der Mund von einem Ohre zum anderen gezogen, das schwarze Haupthaar hängt voll Baumbart

statement.id: Johann Nepomuk von Alpenburg (1857) melukiskan Fänggen sangat besar, berbulu sekujur tubuh, wajah berkerut, mulut terentang dari telinga ke telinga, rambut hitam penuh lumut janggut pohon.
statement.en: Johann Nepomuk von Alpenburg (1857) describes the Fänggen as huge, hairy all over, with a distorted face, a mouth stretched from ear to ear and black hair hung with tree-beard.

basis_claims.quote: Sie sollen sowohl solitär, als auch in Gruppen auftreten, wie in den oben beschriebenen Sagen, sind dabei aber stets an einen bestimmten Wald mit ihrem Leben gebunden. Würde besagter Wald verschwinden, etwa durch Abholzung, würden auch sie verschwinden.

statement.id: Mereka muncul sendirian maupun berkelompok, tetapi hidupnya selalu terikat pada hutan tertentu; bila hutan itu hilang, misalnya karena ditebang, mereka pun lenyap.
statement.en: They appear alone or in groups, but their lives are always bound to a particular forest; if it disappears, say through felling, they disappear too.

basis_claims.quote: Die Augen sind dunkel und nachtschwarz wie Kohlen, glühen aber auch zu Zeiten und sprühen Blitze – die Stimme ist Mannesstimme, rauh und ungefüge. Ihre Kleidung sind Schurze von Wildkatzenpelzen, Joppen von Baumrinden und Zottelschurze von Füchsen und anderm Getier.

statement.id: Mata mereka gelap sehitam arang tetapi kadang menyala dan memancarkan kilat; suara mereka suara lelaki yang kasar; pakaiannya celemek kulit kucing hutan, jaket kulit kayu, dan celemek bulu rubah.
statement.en: Their eyes are dark and coal-black but sometimes glow and flash; their voice is a man's, rough and coarse; they wear aprons of wildcat fur, jackets of tree bark and shaggy fox-skin aprons.

marmennill.depicted_variant: Marmennill as a human-torso merman with fish tail, resting at an Icelandic shoreline with a knowing wry laugh.
visual_requirements: Male human upper body
One fish tail replacing both legs
Icelandic coastal sea setting
Prophetic knowing laugh and mysterious sea-spirit aura
marmennill.aura: Mysterious prophetic sea-goblin with amused wisdom, not a malevolent monster or regal sea god.

basis_claims.quote: is a merman that often features in stories after having been accidentally caught at sea by fishermen. The creature is typically known for its ability to see the future or to reveal otherwise hidden knowledge, often laughing when he sees others acting foolishly.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia (Scandinavian), marmennill adalah manusia laut yang sering muncul dalam kisah setelah tak sengaja tertangkap nelayan; ia dikenal dapat melihat masa depan atau mengungkap pengetahuan tersembunyi dan sering tertawa melihat orang bertindak bodoh.
statement.en: In Scandinavian folklore the marmennill is a merman often featured after being accidentally caught by fishermen; he is known for seeing the future or revealing hidden knowledge, and often laughs at others' folly.

basis_claims.quote: It tells the story of a farmer who catches a marbendill out at sea and takes it home with him. On the way home, the creature laughs three times at the farmer.

statement.id: Kisah "Þá hló marbendill" menceritakan petani yang menangkap marbendill di laut dan membawanya pulang; dalam perjalanan makhluk itu menertawakannya tiga kali.
statement.en: The tale 'Þá hló marbendill' tells of a farmer who catches a marbendill at sea and takes it home; on the way it laughs at him three times.

basis_claims.quote: Marmennill är i isländsk folktro ett havsväsen som liksom sjöjungfrun har en människas överkropp och en fiskstjärt som underkropp. Varelsen menades ha förmågan att förutspå framtiden. Den kvinnliga motsvarigheten kallades Margygur och en motsvarande varelse i Sverige och Danmark kallades Havmannen.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Islandia (isländsk), marmennill adalah makhluk laut yang, seperti putri duyung, bertubuh atas manusia dan berekor ikan; ia dianggap mampu meramal masa depan; padanan perempuannya Margygur, dan makhluk padanannya di Swedia (Sverige) dan Denmark (Danmark) disebut Havmannen.
statement.en: In Icelandic (isländsk) folk belief the marmennill is a sea being which, like a mermaid, has a human upper body and a fish tail; it was thought able to foretell the future; its female counterpart was Margygur, and the corresponding being in Sweden (Sverige) and Denmark (Danmark) was Havmannen.

basis_claims.quote: The phrase þá hló marbendill ("then the merman laughed") is used in Iceland to refer to a sudden and spiteful fit of laughter in reference to the motif in folktales.

statement.id: Ungkapan þá hló marbendill ("lalu manusia laut itu tertawa") dipakai di Islandia (Iceland) untuk tawa mendadak yang dengki, merujuk motif dalam kisah rakyat.
statement.en: The phrase þá hló marbendill ('then the merman laughed') is used in Iceland for a sudden spiteful laugh, after the folktale motif.

hemann.depicted_variant: The documented Lechrain Hojemännlein small-green-kobold variant of the Hemann, calling from a forest path at night.
visual_requirements: One small green kobold-like figure
Calling/yelling with open mouth
Nighttime forest setting
Frightening mischievous shouter aura
hemann.aura: Unsettling boisterous nocturnal shouter, threateningly mischievous rather than a friendly garden gnome.

basis_claims.quote: The Hemann ( German: [ˈheːˌman] ), also Homann, Hoymann, Hoimann, or Jochhoimann, (Mann = man), is a spirit from German folklore known to scare people through yelling, usually invisibly and at night.

statement.id: Hemann, juga Homann, Hoymann, Hoimann, atau Jochhoimann, adalah roh cerita rakyat Jerman yang menakut-nakuti orang dengan teriakan, biasanya tak terlihat dan pada malam hari.
statement.en: The Hemann, also Homann, Hoymann, Hoimann or Jochhoimann, is a German folklore spirit that scares people by yelling, usually invisibly and at night.

basis_claims.quote: The Hemann yells "he he!" or "he helfts!" ("Hey help!") and chases the people with its yelling without ever reaching them completely. Only, it will "aufhocken" (leap upon a person's back and force them to carry the aufhocking spirit) if anybody dares to imitate its yells.

statement.id: Hemann berteriak "he he!" atau "he helfts!" dan mengejar orang tanpa pernah menyusul; ia melakukan aufhocken, melompat ke punggung, bila ada yang meniru teriakannya.
statement.en: The Hemann yells "he he!" or "he helfts!" and chases people without reaching them; it will aufhocken, leap on a person's back, if anyone imitates its yells.

basis_claims.quote: In Upper Palatinate, there is the Hoymann or Hoimann haunting the mountain forests besides the Hemann proper. Its shout, sounding like a coarse male voice or like an owl, can still be heard a quarter hour away.

statement.id: Di Upper Palatinate ada Hoymann atau Hoimann yang menghantui hutan pegunungan; teriakannya terdengar sampai seperempat jam jauhnya.
statement.en: In the Upper Palatinate the Hoymann or Hoimann haunts the mountain forests; its shout can be heard a quarter hour away.

basis_claims.quote: In the Lechrain, the Hojemännlein, Hojemännl, Hojemännel, or Hojemannl (sg., pl.; Männlein, Männl or Mannl = manikin) are little Kobolds, tiny and green of appearance

statement.id: Di Lechrain, Hojemännlein adalah Kobold kecil berwarna hijau.
statement.en: In the Lechrain the Hojemännlein are little green Kobolds.

airavata.depicted_variant: Mackenzie's four-tusk Indra-mount form; no multi-headed regional interpretation
visual_requirements: Pristine white divine Asian elephant
Exactly four separate tusks
One head and one trunk
Coherent elephant anatomy
Cloud-water association and divine victorious majesty

basis_claims.quote: He is pristine white. ... He is the "king of elephants" and serves as the main vehicle for the deity Indra.

statement.id: Airavata adalah gajah ilahi putih yang menjadi raja gajah dan tunggangan Indra.
statement.en: Airavata is a white divine elephant, king of elephants, and Indra's mount.

basis_claims.quote: He is also called 'Abhra-matanga', meaning "elephant of the clouds"

statement.id: Epitet Abhra-matanga berarti gajah awan.
statement.en: The epithet Abhra matanga means elephant of the clouds.

basis_claims.quote: The appearance or birth of Airavata varies according to different Hindu texts. In the Ramayana, Airavata was born to Iravati (descendant of the sage, Kashyapa), whereas the Vishnu Purana notes that Airavata was born from the churning of the ocean of milk.

statement.id: Ramayana menyebutnya lahir dari Iravati, sementara Vishnu Purana menyebut kelahiran dari pengadukan samudra susu.
statement.en: The Ramayana gives his birth from Iravati, while the Vishnu Purana gives birth from churning the milk ocean.

basis_claims.quote: Prithu made Airavata king of all elephants. The name of his consort, Abhramu, means "the one who knits or binds the clouds," reflecting the idea that elephants can produce rain clouds. The connection of elephants with water and rain is emphasized in the mythology of Indra, who rides the elephant Airavata when he defeats Vritra.

statement.id: Legenda menghubungkan Airavata dan gajah dengan air serta hujan.
statement.en: Legend connects Airavata and elephants with water and rain.

basis_claims.quote:
seated
himself upon a great white elephant, “the handsome and
ever victorious”, named Airavata; it “was furnished with
four tusks”

statement.id: Versi Mackenzie menyebut Airavata sebagai gajah putih Indra bertaring empat.
statement.en: Mackenzie's version calls Airavata Indra's white elephant with four tusks.

heimchen.depicted_variant: Replace plain cricket with recorded Orlagau finger-tall earth spirit/dwarf living in household mousehole: tiny human-shaped manikin carries a wrapped dawn gift from mouse-hole, visibly smaller than adjacent adult human finger reaching near doorway and sewingthimble. Exactly humanhead/twoarms/twolegs, plain miniature clothes. Scale essential, no insectorgans. House stonefloor at dawn, curious adult hand only.
visual_requirements: Cited variant/episode readable
Coherent anatomy
No generic aura

basis_claims.quote: In the Orlagau in Thuringia the Heimchen, who are also called Heimele, Butzelmännchen (little bogeymen), and Erdmännele (earth manikins), are thought of as tiny earth spirits, as tall as a finger is long, who dwell in the mouse holes of houses.

statement.id: Di Orlagau, Thuringia, Heimchen, juga disebut Heimele, Butzelmännchen, dan Erdmännele, dianggap roh tanah setinggi jari yang tinggal di lubang tikus rumah.
statement.en: In the Orlagau in Thuringia the Heimchen, also called Heimele, Butzelmännchen and Erdmännele, are tiny finger-tall earth spirits living in the mouse holes of houses.

basis_claims.quote: They indicate beforehand whether the house dwellers will meet good or bad luck and, if well taken care of, at times might also place gifts in front of their mouse hole in the morning.

statement.id: Mereka memberi tanda lebih dahulu apakah penghuni rumah akan beruntung atau sial, dan bila dirawat baik kadang meninggalkan hadiah.
statement.en: They indicate in advance whether the house dwellers will meet good or bad luck and, if well cared for, sometimes leave gifts.

artistic_changes: Colours, human age/appearance, clothing, supporting props and scene arrangement are editorial staging rather than unique attested iconography.

worm-of-linton.depicted_variant: Scottish legend serpent, not heraldic wyvern
visual_requirements: One large legless wingless serpent
Single head and continuous thick coiled body
Scottish Linton Hill cave at dusk
Menacing crop-devouring wyrm aura

basis_claims.quote: The Linton Worm is a mythical beast referred to in a Scottish Borders legend dating back to the 12th century. "Wyrm" is the Old English for serpent.

statement.id: Linton Worm adalah makhluk mitos dalam legenda Scottish Borders abad ke-12; Wyrm adalah kata Old English (Inggris Kuno) untuk ular.
statement.en: The Linton Worm is a mythical beast of a 12th-century Scottish Borders legend; Wyrm is Old English for serpent.

basis_claims.quote: A 12th-century writer believed it to be "In length three Scots yards and bigger than an ordinary man’s leg – in form and callour to our common muir edders." The myth is similar to that of the Lambton Worm.

statement.id: Penulis abad ke-12 menggambarkannya sepanjang tiga Scots yards, lebih besar dari kaki manusia; mitos ini mirip Lambton Worm.
statement.en: A 12th-century writer put it at three Scots yards, bigger than a man's leg; the myth resembles the Lambton Worm.

basis_claims.quote: The monster lived in a hollow on the northeast side of Linton Hill, a spot still known as the "Worm’s Den", at Linton in Roxburghshire on the Scottish borders. Emerging from its lair at dusk and dawn to ravage the countryside, eating crops, livestock and people, it proved invulnerable to the weapons ranged against it.

statement.id: Monster itu tinggal di Worm's Den di Linton Hill, Roxburghshire, keluar saat senja dan fajar memakan tanaman, ternak, dan manusia, dan kebal senjata.
statement.en: The monster lived in the Worm's Den on Linton Hill, Roxburghshire, emerging at dusk and dawn to eat crops, livestock and people, invulnerable to weapons.

basis_claims.quote: During the 12th century, the area of Linton was being terrorised by a dragon-like monster known as The Linton Worm.

statement.id: Pada abad ke-12 daerah Linton diteror monster mirip naga (dragon-like) bernama The Linton Worm.
statement.en: In the 12th century Linton was terrorised by a dragon-like monster called The Linton Worm.

dokkaebi.depicted_variant: Academy Korean Studies one-legged humanlike variant
visual_requirements: Disheveled humanlike visible form
Exactly one black leg
Wooden club and playful trickster aura

basis_claims.quote: Dokkaebi (Korean: 도깨비) are legendary creatures from Korean mythology and folklore. Dokkaebi, also known as "Korean ogres", are nature deities or spirits possessing extraordinary powers and abilities that are used to interact with humans, at times playing tricks on them and at times helping them.

statement.id: Dokkaebi adalah makhluk legenda Korea yang berinteraksi dengan manusia melalui pertolongan atau tipu daya.
statement.en: Dokkaebi are Korean legendary beings who interact with people through assistance or tricks.

basis_claims.quote: Different versions of the dokkaebi mythology assign different attributes to them. In some cases, they are considered harmless but nevertheless mischievous, usually playing pranks on people or challenging wayward travelers to a ssireum (Korean wrestling) match for the right to pass. Dokkaebi are extremely skilled at wrestling and cannot be beaten unless their right side is exploited.

statement.id: Beberapa kisah menggambarkan tantangan gulat ssireum kepada pengelana.
statement.en: Some tales describe ssireum wrestling challenges to travelers.

basis_claims.quote: Dokkaebi fire is a glimmering light or tall blue flames that herald the appearance of dokkaebi.

statement.id: Cahaya atau nyala biru dapat menandai kedatangan dokkaebi.
statement.en: Glimmering light or blue flames may herald a dokkaebi's appearance.

basis_claims.quote: Dokkaebi possess magical items, such as the dokkaebi hat called the dokkaebi gamtu (도깨비 감투), which grants the wearer the ability of invisibility, and the dokkaebi magic club called the dokkaebi bangmangi (도깨비 방망이), which can summon things and act functionally as a magic wand. Dokkaebi like buckwheat jelly, sorghum and red bean rice cakes, mashed sorghum, and the drinks.

statement.id: Benda ajaibnya mencakup topi pemberi ketakterlihatan dan tongkat pemuncul barang.
statement.en: Their magical objects include an invisibility hat and a club that summons things.

basis_claims.quote: Goblins are called dokkaebi in Korea. Unlike other monsters, these dokkaebi are more playful than harmful, and some of them bring you treasure with their club.

statement.id: Korea.net menyebut dokkaebi cenderung bermain-main dan sebagian membawa harta melalui tongkatnya.
statement.en: Korea.net describes dokkaebi as playful and says some bring treasure using their clubs.

naga.depicted_variant: Single divine cobra-form naga guarding treasure and controlling water.

visual_requirements.description: One cobra in selected full-serpent form, not mixed humanoid.
Controller of water, river/lake guardian.
Precious gems and gold in naga realm.

naga.aura: Swirling controlled water grounded in naga-c11/c15, protective treasure authority.

basis_claims.quote: They are principally depicted in three forms: as entirely human with snakes on the heads and necks, as common serpents, or as half-human, half-snake beings in Hinduism and Buddhism.

statement.id: Mereka dapat tampil sebagai manusia, ular, atau makhluk campuran manusia dan ular.
statement.en: They can appear as humans, serpents, or mixed human and serpent beings.

basis_claims.quote: In Sanskrit, a nāga (नाग) primarily refers to a snake, most often specifically the Indian cobra (Naja naja). However, the term is also used generically to denote any snake, sharing this broader meaning with other common Sanskrit synonyms such as sarpa (सर्प) and phaṇin (फणिन्).

statement.id: Naga dalam Sanskerta terutama berarti ular, sering kali kobra India.
statement.en: Naga in Sanskrit primarily means snake, often the Indian cobra.

basis_claims.quote: Their domain is in the enchanted underworld, the underground realm filled with gems, gold and other earthly treasures called Naga-loka or Patala-loka.

statement.id: Alam Naga-loka digambarkan berisi permata, emas, dan harta bumi.
statement.en: Naga-loka is described as containing gems, gold, and earthly treasures.

basis_claims.quote: They are also often associated with bodies of waters—including rivers, lakes, seas, and wells—and are guardians of treasure.

statement.id: Naga dikaitkan dengan sungai, danau, laut, dan sumur serta peran penjaga harta.
statement.en: Nagas are associated with rivers, lakes, seas, and wells and with guarding treasure.

basis_claims.quote: Nagas continue to be important divinities in local piety, for they control the forces of water, essential for prosperity.

statement.id: Museum Cleveland menjelaskan pentingnya naga bagi pemuja lokal sebagai pengendali air yang menunjang kemakmuran.
statement.en: The Cleveland Museum explains the importance of nagas to local worshippers as controllers of water supporting prosperity.

artistic_changes: Single-head cobra variant, scale texture/color and subterranean river composition editorial.
No multi-headed Shesha iconography, human arms or antlers; water effect follows domain, no fire or lightning.

presentation_revision.rationale: Big names (major gods, archangels, demon princes, primordial monsters, famous literary beings) must look imposing and powerful: an epic, awe-inspiring or terrifying presence that matches their standing in the tradition.

At about30cm relative to enormous roots and mouse-sized treasure fragments; low ground-level camera gives imposing presence without claiming giant actual size. Flickering ordinary underground brazier fire casts dramatic heat/reflections on fur, no fire emitted from body or unsupported weapons. Mischievous malevolent fierce expression, primitive patched modest clothing. No film/game designs, no gore, no extra horns or wings.

At about30cm relative to enormous roots and mouse-sized treasure fragments; low ground-level camera gives imposing presence without claiming giant actual size. goblin.aura: Environmental cave fire and glowing gold reflections

basis_claims.quote: A goblin is a diminutive, grotesque, and often malevolent humanoid creature prominent in European folklore, typically characterized by its mischievous or demonic nature, small stature (around 30 cm (12 in) in some traditions), furry or leathery appearance, and ability to shapeshift.

statement.id: Goblin adalah makhluk humanoid kecil, aneh, sering jahat dalam cerita rakyat Eropa (European folklore), usil atau iblis, kecil (sekitar 30 cm), berbulu, dan dapat berubah wujud.
statement.en: A goblin is a small, grotesque, often malevolent humanoid of European folklore, mischievous or demonic, about 30 cm tall, furry, able to shapeshift.

basis_claims.quote: Goblins are believed to dwell in subterranean areas or households, where they engage in acts ranging from pranks to murder.

statement.id: Goblin dipercaya tinggal di bawah tanah atau di rumah, berbuat dari lelucon hingga pembunuhan.
statement.en: Goblins are believed to dwell underground or in households, doing anything from pranks to murder.

basis_claims.quote: Dalam cerita rakyat Eropa, Goblin merupakan bangsa peri atau makhluk supranatural. Ukuran tubuh mereka kecil dan kadang kala tidak terlihat oleh mata manusia. Mereka dilukiskan sebagai makhluk mungil berwarna hijau dan bertelinga runcing.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Eropa, Goblin bangsa peri, kecil, kadang tak terlihat, mungil berwarna hijau dan bertelinga runcing.
statement.en: In European (Eropa) folklore Goblins are fairy folk (bangsa peri), small, sometimes unseen, little green beings with pointed ears (telinga runcing).

basis_claims.quote: Mereka juga sangat serakah dan cinta emas atau jenis perhiasan. Goblin juga erat kaitannya dengan api dan memiliki kemahiran untuk menciptakannya. Menurut versi lain dalam beberapa dongeng dan kisah fantasi, Goblin merupakan bangsa makhluk yang buas dan ganas. Mereka tinggal di gua-gua yang gelap atau di bawah tanah.

statement.id: Goblin serakah dan cinta emas, terkait api (api), dan menurut versi lain buas serta tinggal di gua-gua gelap atau bawah tanah.
statement.en: Goblins are greedy and love gold (emas), are tied to fire (api), and in other versions are savage (buas), living in dark caves (gua-gua) or underground.

artistic_changes: Low-angle framing, painterly materials and environmental color are artistic rendering.
Effects are limited to the cited domains, deeds, attributes or iconography; natural light and scale supply presence where no elemental ability is documented.

presentation_revision.rationale: Big names (major gods, archangels, demon princes, primordial monsters, famous literary beings) must look imposing and powerful: an epic, awe-inspiring or terrifying presence that matches their standing in the tradition.

shuihu.depicted_variant: Chinese Hubei tiger-head/lower-limb account; not Wakan Sansai Zue kneecap reading or kappa synonym
visual_requirements: Child-sized river water-tiger
Tigerlike head and lower limbs
Overlapping tough scales
Sandbar with claws kept beneath shallow water
Territorial dangerous aura

basis_claims.quote: A shuihu or shui hu (Chinese: 水虎; pinyin: shuǐhǔ; Wade–Giles: shui-hu; Japanese pronunciation: suiko; lit. 'water tiger'), is a legendary creature said to have inhabited river systems in what is now Hubei Province, China.

statement.id: Shuihu adalah makhluk legenda sungai dari wilayah Hubei, Tiongkok.
statement.en: Shuihu is a legendary river creature from the Hubei region of China.

basis_claims.quote: The name shuihu (or suiko) derives from the creature possessing physical characteristics reminiscent of a tiger (虎, Chinese pronunciation: hu;  Japanese: ko/tora).

statement.id: Nama harimau air merujuk pada ciri tubuhnya yang menyerupai harimau.
statement.en: The water-tiger name refers to physical features resembling a tiger.

basis_claims.quote: The water tiger is described as similar (in size) to a 3 or 4-year old human child, with tiger-like head and lower limb, and covered with tough scales resisting arrows. It basks on sandbars, while keeping their claws submerged in water. If a human tries to tamper with he may be killed.

statement.id: Ukurannya disamakan dengan anak berusia tiga atau empat tahun dan tubuhnya memiliki sisik keras.
statement.en: Its size is compared to a three- or four-year-old child, with hard scales covering its body.

basis_claims.quote: The water tiger is described as similar (in size) to a 3 or 4-year old human child, with tiger-like head and lower limb, and covered with tough scales resisting arrows. It basks on sandbars, while keeping their claws submerged in water. If a human tries to tamper with he may be killed.

statement.id: Kisah menggambarkannya berjemur di gosong pasir dengan cakar tetap di air.
statement.en: The tale describes it basking on sandbars with its claws kept in water.

basis_claims.quote: 本綱、水虎、襄 記注云、中廬縣有二涑水一注二 中一、有物如二三四歲小兒一、甲如二鯪鯉一射不レ能レ入、

statement.id: Transkripsi Kojiruien membandingkan Shuihu dengan anak kecil dan mencatat sisik yang tidak tertembus panah.
statement.en: The Kojiruien transcription compares Shuihu to a small child and records arrow-resistant scales.

kelpie.depicted_variant: Kelpie in the explicitly recorded human manifestation RETAINING HORSE HOOVES: a handsome pale man with human head, torso and two human arms in a wet simple linen tunic and cloak, standing beside a Scottish loch. His two legs end in unmistakable SINGLE HORSE HOOVES instead of feet, both unobscured by garments, full-body view. Wet dark hair, unsettling intent toward a distant lone traveler; no horse head, no centaur body, no extra legs, no cloven goat hooves. Human guise retaining equine hoof clue is essential.
visual_requirements: Documented variant or episode clearly visible
Coherent required anatomy
No generic aura

basis_claims.quote: It is usually described as a grey or white horse-like creature, able to adopt human form. Some accounts state that the kelpie retains its hooves when appearing as a human, leading to its association with the Christian idea of Satan as alluded to by Robert Burns in his 1786 poem "Address to the Devil".

statement.id: Kelpie digambarkan seperti kuda kelabu atau putih yang dapat berwujud manusia, tetap berkuku, sehingga dikaitkan dengan Setan (Satan) oleh Robert Burns dalam Address to the Devil (1786).
statement.en: The kelpie is a grey or white horse-like creature that can take human form, keeping its hooves, tied to Satan by Robert Burns in Address to the Devil (1786).

basis_claims.quote: but the practical purposes of keeping children away from dangerous stretches of water and warning young women to be wary of handsome strangers has been noted in secondary literature.

statement.id: Kisah kelpie berguna menjauhkan anak dari perairan berbahaya dan memperingatkan perempuan muda terhadap orang asing tampan.
statement.en: Kelpie tales served to keep children from dangerous water and warn young women of handsome strangers.

artistic_changes: Clothing, coat colours, human age/appearance, material ornament and environmental arrangement are editorial staging.

presentation_revision.rationale: Replaces passive ordinary animal presentation with the stronger explicitly documented variant/episode recorded in assigned research.

visual_requirements: One humanlike-faced limbless serpent
Long coiled body blocks river gorge
Water held back and drought below
Fearsome oppressive drought-demon aura

basis_claims.quote: He serves as the personification of drought, and is an adversary of the king of the devas, Indra.

statement.id: Vritra adalah danava yang mempersonifikasikan kekeringan dan menjadi lawan Indra.
statement.en: Vritra is a danava personifying drought and opposing Indra.

basis_claims.quote: He appears as a human-like serpent blocking the course of the Rigvedic rivers, and is slain by Indra with his newly forged vajra.

statement.id: Ia tampil sebagai ular menyerupai manusia yang menghalangi aliran sungai Rigveda.
statement.en: He appears as a human like serpent blocking Rigvedic rivers.

basis_claims.quote: Vritra literally means "cover, obstacle", in reference of him holding back the waters. It stems from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wr̥trás, from the Proto-Indo-European root *wer- "to cover, to obstruct". The Indo-Iranian word is also found in Avestan as vərəθraγna (Vedic vṛtraghná), literally "(one who) slays obstacles".

statement.id: Namanya dijelaskan berarti penutup atau penghalang, berkaitan dengan penahanan air.
statement.en: His name is explained as cover or obstacle, linked to holding back waters.

kamadhenu.depicted_variant: Woman-headed winged white cow with peafowl tail
visual_requirements: White cow body with four hoofed legs
Woman's head with no human torso
Two feathered wings and peafowl tail

basis_claims.quote: is a divine bovine-goddess described in Hinduism as the mother of all cows.

statement.id: Kamadhenu atau Surabhi adalah dewi sapi dan ibu semua sapi dalam Hindu.
statement.en: Kamadhenu or Surabhi is a bovine goddess and mother of all cows in Hinduism.

basis_claims.quote: She is a miraculous cow of plenty who provides her owner whatever they desire

statement.id: Ia merupakan sapi ajaib yang menyediakan apa pun yang diinginkan pemiliknya.
statement.en: She is a miraculous cow providing whatever her owner desires.

basis_claims.quote: she is generally depicted as a white cow with a female head and breasts, the wings of a bird, and the tail of a peafowl

statement.id: Salah satu ikonografinya berupa sapi putih berkepala perempuan, bersayap burung, dan berekor merak.
statement.en: One iconographic form is a white cow with a woman's head, bird wings, and peafowl tail.

cwn-annwn.depicted_variant: One Ci Annwn from white-bodied red-eared Welsh spectral hounds, not Christian fiery hellhound
visual_requirements: One spectral white hound
Two red ears clearly visible
Coherent canine anatomy
Welsh nocturnal moor hunting setting
Ominous death-portent otherworld aura

basis_claims.quote: In Welsh mythology and folklore, Cŵn Annwn ( Welsh pronunciation: [kuːn ˈanʊn] , "hounds of Annwn"), singular Ci Annwn ( Welsh pronunciation: [kiː ˈanʊn] ), were the spectral hounds of Annwn, the otherworld of Welsh myth. They were associated with a form of the Wild Hunt, presided over by either Arawn, king of Annwn in Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Wales (Welsh), Cŵn Annwn (Hounds of Annwn; Ci Annwn) anjing hantu Annwn, dunia lain; Perburuan Liar (Wild Hunt) dipimpin Arawn (Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed, Cabang Pertama Mabinogi) atau Gwyn ap Nudd; di Britania Raya. (First Branch)
statement.en: In Welsh myth the Cŵn Annwn (hounds of Annwn; Ci Annwn) were spectral hounds of the otherworld Annwn; tied to the Wild Hunt led by Arawn (Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed) or Gwyn ap Nudd.

basis_claims.quote: According to Welsh folklore, their growling is loudest when they are at a distance, and as they draw nearer, it grows softer and softer. Their coming is generally seen as a death portent.

statement.id: Geraman paling keras saat jauh; kedatangan mereka pertanda kematian.
statement.en: Their growl is loudest at a distance; their coming is a death portent.

basis_claims.quote: The Annwn of medieval Welsh tradition is an otherworldly place of plenty and eternal youth and not a place of punishment like the Christian concept of Hell. Christians came to dub these mythical creatures as "The Hounds of Hell" or "Dogs of Hell" and theorised they were therefore owned by Satan.

statement.id: Annwn tempat kelimpahan; orang Kristen (Christians) menyebutnya Hounds of Hell, milik Setan (Satan).
statement.en: Annwn is a place of plenty; Christians called them the Hounds of Hell, owned by Satan.

basis_claims.quote: Diese Hunde haben rote Ohren und weiße, gespenstische Körper, ähnlich den übernatürlichen Kühe aus einigen irischen Sagen.

statement.id: Telinga merah (rote Ohren), tubuh putih seperti hantu (weiße, gespenstische Körper).
statement.en: Red ears (rote Ohren) and white ghostly bodies (weiße, gespenstische Körper).

kirtimukha.depicted_variant: Upper face and upper jaw stone lintel guardian
visual_requirements: Fierce face only architectural lintel motif
Bulging eyes enormous fangs gaping upper jaw
No lower jaw or body in chosen variant
Awe-inspiring auspicious threshold guardian aura

basis_claims.quote: is the name of a swallowing fierce face with huge fangs, and gaping mouth, very common in the iconography of Hindu temple architecture in South Asia and Southeast Asia, and often also found in Buddhist architecture.

statement.id: Kirtimukha adalah wajah ganas bertaring besar dan bermulut menganga dalam arsitektur Hindu dan Buddha.
statement.en: Kirtimukha is a fierce face with large fangs and a gaping mouth in Hindu and Buddhist architecture.

basis_claims.quote: The Kirtimukha is often used as a motif surmounting the pinnacle of a temple or the image of a deity, especially in South Indian architecture. As Zimmer writes, "Kirtimukha serves primarily as an apotropaic demon-mask, a gruesome, awe-inspiring guardian of the threshold."

statement.id: Zimmer menafsirkannya sebagai topeng demon penolak bahaya dan penjaga ambang.
statement.en: Zimmer interprets it as an apotropaic demon mask and guardian of the threshold.

basis_claims.quote: This fierce face with bulging eyes sits also as an embellishment over the lintel of the gate to the inner sanctum in many Hindu temples ... very often only the upper jaw and top of the face is visible

statement.id: Motif ini menghias lintel pintu ruang suci, sering hanya memperlihatkan rahang atas dan bagian atas wajah.
statement.en: The motif decorates sanctum doorway lintels, often showing only the upper jaw and upper face.

basis_claims.quote: The kirtimukha or auspicious face of glory is popular icon in South and Southeast Asian Hindu-Buddhist temple architecture.

statement.id: NHB Singapura menyebut kirtimukha sebagai wajah kemuliaan yang mujur dalam arsitektur kuil Hindu-Buddha Asia Selatan dan Tenggara.
statement.en: Singapore's NHB calls kirtimukha an auspicious face of glory in South and Southeast Asian Hindu Buddhist temple architecture.

fomorians.depicted_variant: Lebor na hUidre goat-headed human-bodied form, not one-limb variant
visual_requirements: One goat-headed human-bodied Fomorian
One head two arms two legs
Irish sea/earth context
Hostile monstrous destructive aura

basis_claims.quote: The Fomorians or Fomori (Old Irish: Fomóire , Modern Irish: Fomhóraigh / Fomóraigh ) are a supernatural race in Irish mythology, who are often portrayed as hostile and monstrous beings.

statement.id: Fomoria (Fomori; Old Irish Fomóire, Modern Irish Fomhóraigh) adalah bangsa gaib mitologi Irlandia (Irish mythology), bermusuhan dan mengerikan.
statement.en: The Fomorians (Fomori; Old Irish Fomóire, Modern Irish Fomhóraigh) are a hostile, monstrous supernatural race of Irish mythology.

basis_claims.quote: Originally they were said to come from under the sea or the earth. Later, they were portrayed as sea raiders and giants.

statement.id: Awalnya dari bawah laut atau bumi; kemudian perompak laut dan raksasa.
statement.en: At first from under the sea or earth; later sea raiders and giants.

basis_claims.quote: One theory is that the Fomorians were supernatural beings representing the wild or destructive powers of nature; personifications of chaos, darkness, death, blight and drought.

statement.id: Satu teori: Fomoria mewakili kekuatan alam yang liar atau merusak; kekacauan, kegelapan, kematian, hama, kekeringan.
statement.en: One theory: the Fomorians represent nature's wild, destructive powers; chaos, darkness, death, blight and drought.

basis_claims.quote: Sometimes they are said to have the body of a man and the head of a goat, according to an 11th-century text in Lebor na hUidre (the Book of the Dun Cow), or to have had one eye, one arm and one leg.

statement.id: Menurut Lebor na hUidre abad ke-11, mereka bertubuh manusia berkepala kambing, atau bermata, berlengan, dan berkaki satu.
statement.en: Per the 11th-century Lebor na hUidre, they have a man's body and goat's head, or one eye, arm and leg.

Make the purposeful cooperation and witch's attentive response the narrative focus. Natural cat anatomy, one head, four legs and one tail. Neither a simple pet portrait nor generic sinister glowing eyes.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris Utara (Northern English folklore), Barghest (Barguest) anjing hitam mengerikan bergigi dan bercakar besar, atau hantu atau elf rumah di Northumberland dan Durham, seperti Cauld Lad of Hylton.

basis_claims.quote: The Barghest often allegedly serves as an omen of death. At the passing of a notable person the Barghest may appear, followed by all the other dogs of the local area in a kind of funeral procession, heralding the person's death with howling and barking.

basis_claims.quote: A valravn is a supernatural raven in Danish renaissance folklore. It principally appears in the folk ballad "Valravnen" (Danish: The Valravn ) where it is depicted as a knight who was transformed into a raven, and whose curse can only be broken by consuming the blood of a boy.

statement.id: Valravn adalah gagak gaib dalam cerita rakyat Denmark masa Renaisans yang terutama muncul dalam balada rakyat "Valravnen" sebagai ksatria yang diubah menjadi gagak, yang kutukannya hanya dapat dipatahkan dengan meminum darah anak lelaki.
statement.en: A valravn is a supernatural raven of Danish Renaissance folklore, appearing mainly in the ballad 'Valravnen' as a knight transformed into a raven whose curse can only be broken by drinking a boy's blood.

basis_claims.quote: Un valraven ou valravn est, dans le folklore danois, un corbeau surnaturel décrit comme le corbeau des tués. ... Après avoir dévoré le cœur d'un enfant, il prend la forme d'un chevalier ou d'une créature mi-loup mi-corbeau.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Denmark, valraven atau valravn adalah gagak gaib yang disebut "gagak orang yang gugur"; setelah memakan jantung seorang anak ia berwujud ksatria atau makhluk setengah serigala setengah gagak.
statement.en: In Danish folklore the valraven or valravn is a supernatural raven called the 'raven of the slain'; after eating a child's heart it takes the form of a knight or a half-wolf, half-raven creature.

basis_claims.quote: An Alp is typically male, while the mara and mart appear to be more feminine versions of the same creature. Its victims are often females, whom it attacks during the night, controlling their dreams and creating horrible nightmares (hence the German word Alptraum ["elf-dream"], meaning a nightmare).

statement.id: Alp biasanya jantan, sedangkan mara dan mart tampaknya versi lebih feminin; korbannya sering perempuan yang diserangnya pada malam hari dengan mengendalikan mimpi mereka, dari situ kata Jerman Alptraum ("mimpi elf"), yaitu mimpi buruk.
statement.en: The Alp is typically male, the mara and mart appearing more feminine versions; its victims are often women whom it attacks at night by controlling their dreams, hence the German Alptraum ('elf-dream'), a nightmare.

basis_claims.quote: Alpdruck is when an Alp sits astride a sleeper's chest and becomes heavier until the crushing weight awakens the terrified and breathless dreamer. The victim awakes unable to move under the Alp's weight.

statement.id: Alpdruck terjadi saat Alp duduk mengangkangi dada orang tidur dan makin berat hingga korban terbangun ketakutan dan sesak napas, tak bisa bergerak di bawah bebannya.
statement.en: Alpdruck is when an Alp sits astride a sleeper's chest and grows heavier until the terrified, breathless dreamer wakes, unable to move under its weight.

basis_claims.quote: The hat is known as a Tarnkappe (the literal translation being "camouflage cap" or "cap of concealment") which is simply a hat (or less commonly a veil) that gives the Alp magic powers and the ability to turn invisible while worn ... An Alp who has lost this hat will offer a great reward for its safe return.

statement.id: Topi Alp disebut Tarnkappe ("topi penyamaran"), yang memberinya kekuatan gaib dan kemampuan tak terlihat selama dipakai; Alp yang kehilangan topi ini akan menawarkan imbalan besar untuk pengembaliannya.
statement.en: Its hat is called the Tarnkappe ('cap of concealment'), giving the Alp magic powers and invisibility while worn; an Alp that loses it will offer a great reward for its return.

basis_claims.quote: Nachtalb ist eine späte Bezeichnung für ein Fantasie- und Sagenwesen, das ursprünglich „Mahr“ hieß und in der Nacht auf Menschen lastet (vgl. Albtraum) und ihnen Grauen einflößt.

statement.id: Nachtalb adalah sebutan belakangan untuk makhluk khayalan dan legenda yang semula bernama Mahr, yang menindih manusia pada malam hari dan membuat mereka ngeri.
statement.en: Nachtalb is a late name for a fantasy and legendary being originally called Mahr that weighs on people at night and fills them with dread.

basis_claims.quote: Es handelt sich gewöhnlich um ein kleines, schwarzes Wesen, das schlafende Menschen und Haustiere anfällt, selten auch Gegenstände. Es dringt durch Schlüssel- oder Astlöcher ein.

statement.id: Makhluk ini biasanya kecil dan hitam, menyerang manusia dan hewan peliharaan yang tidur, jarang juga benda, dan masuk lewat lubang kunci atau lubang dahan.
statement.en: It is usually a small black being that attacks sleeping people and domestic animals, rarely objects, and enters through keyholes or knot-holes.

hafgufa.aura: Dreadful primordial ocean immensity and predatory menace

basis_claims.quote: Hafgufa (Old Norse: haf "sea" + Old Norse: gufa "steam"; "sea-reek"; "sea-steamer") is a sea creature, purported to inhabit Iceland's waters (Greenland Sea) and southward toward Helluland. Although it was thought to be a sea monster, research suggests that the stories originated from a specialized feeding technique among whales known as trap-feeding.

statement.id: Hafgufa (Nordik Kuno haf, "laut", + gufa, "uap") adalah makhluk laut yang konon menghuni perairan Islandia (Laut Greenland) hingga ke selatan menuju Helluland; meski dianggap monster laut, penelitian menduga kisahnya berasal dari teknik makan paus yang disebut trap-feeding.
statement.en: Hafgufa (Old Norse haf 'sea' + gufa 'steam') is a sea creature said to inhabit Iceland's waters (the Greenland Sea) and south toward Helluland; though thought a sea monster, research suggests the stories came from a whale feeding technique called trap-feeding.

basis_claims.quote: In the Snorra Edda, the hafgufa ("sea-steamer") appears in the list (þulur) of whales. The spelling is also hafgúa in some copies.

statement.id: Dalam Snorra Edda, hafgufa muncul dalam daftar (þulur) paus; di beberapa salinan ejaannya hafgúa.
statement.en: In the Snorra Edda the hafgufa appears in the list (þulur) of whales; some copies spell it hafgúa.

basis_claims.quote: In the later version of Örvar-Odds saga dating to the late 14th century, hafgufa is described as the largest sea monster (sjóskrímsl ) of all, which fed on whales, ships, men, and anything it could catch ... it was the nostril and lower jaw which they had sailed in-between, although they mistook these for two massive rocks rising from the sea.

statement.id: Dalam versi akhir Örvar-Odds saga dari akhir abad ke-14, hafgufa adalah monster laut (sjóskrímsl) terbesar yang memangsa paus, kapal, manusia, dan apa saja; awak kapal berlayar di antara lubang hidung dan rahang bawahnya, yang mereka kira dua batu besar.
statement.en: In the later version of Örvar-Odds saga from the late 14th century hafgufa is the largest sea monster (sjóskrímsl), feeding on whales, ships, men and anything else; the crew sailed between its nostril and lower jaw, mistaking them for two great rocks.

basis_claims.quote: Once a large number had crowded into its mouth and belly, it would close its mouth and devour them all at once.

statement.id: Setelah banyak ikan berdesakan di mulut dan perutnya, ia menutup mulut dan melahap semuanya sekaligus.
statement.en: Once many fish had crowded into its mouth and belly, it shut its mouth and devoured them all at once.

basis_claims.quote: was a monstrous cat in Welsh mythology associated with Arthurian legend. statement.id: Cath Palug (Cath Paluc, Cath Balug, Cath Balwg; Kucing Palug) kucing raksasa mitologi Wales (Welsh), legenda Arthurian; lahir di Gwynedd dari Henwen dari Cornwall; menghantui Anglesey (Isle of Anglesey) sampai Kay memburunya; di luar Wales lawannya Raja Arthur (King Arthur) atau Ogier the Dane; Chapalu (French, Prancis); di Britania dan Prancis.
statement.en: Cath Palug (Palug's Cat) was a monstrous cat of Welsh myth, born in Gwynedd to Henwen of Cornwall, haunting Anglesey until Kay hunted it; elsewhere its foe is King Arthur or Ogier the Dane.

basis_claims.quote: Cath Palug is always localised near water, such as the lakes of Lac du Bourget and Lake Geneva in France (cf. also § Local lore), or the sea in Wales.

statement.id: Selalu dekat air: Lac du Bourget, Danau Jenewa (Lake Geneva), Prancis (France), atau laut di Wales.
statement.en: Always near water: Lac du Bourget, Lake Geneva in France, or the sea in Wales.

basis_claims.quote: According to this source, it started life as a kitten (lit "whelp" ), given birth by the great white sow Henwen at the black rock in Llanfair [cy]. There the kitten was cast into the sea, but it crossed the Menai Strait and was found on Ynys Môn (Anglesey), where the sons of Palug raised it, not realizing the cat was to become one of the three great plagues of the island.

statement.id: Welsh Triads: lahir dari Henwen di Llanfair, dibuang ke laut, menyeberangi Selat Menai (Menai Strait) ke Anglesey (Ynys Môn), dibesarkan putra Palug; tiga wabah pulau.
statement.en: Welsh Triads: born to Henwen at Llanfair, cast into the sea, crossed the Menai Strait to Anglesey (Ynys Môn), raised by Palug's sons; one of the island's three plagues.

basis_claims.quote: Le Chapalu, Capalu ou Capalus est un chat monstrueux dont parlent des manuscrits médiévaux français rattachés à la légende arthurienne.

statement.id: Chapalu (Capalu, Capalus) kucing raksasa (chat monstrueux) dalam naskah abad pertengahan Prancis (français) legenda Arthurian.
statement.en: Chapalu (Capalu, Capalus) is a monstrous cat (chat monstrueux) in medieval French (français) Arthurian manuscripts.

basis_claims.quote: The Bahkauv is a mythical monster said to reside in Aachen, Germany. The creature has been featured in the folklore of both Aachen and the Rhineland. Often depicted as a deformed calf with fangs, the Bahkauv is commonly associated with drunken men.

statement.id: Bahkauv adalah monster mitos yang konon tinggal di Aachen, Jerman, muncul dalam cerita rakyat Aachen dan Rheinland, sering digambarkan sebagai anak sapi cacat bertaring, dan dikaitkan dengan lelaki mabuk.
statement.en: The Bahkauv is a mythical monster said to live in Aachen, Germany, featured in Aachen and Rhineland folklore, often shown as a deformed fanged calf and associated with drunken men.

basis_claims.quote: The Bahkauv is typically described as being similar to an elongated or deformed calf with sharp fangs. According to legend, the creature often lurks near fountains, streams, and sewers. The Aachen city sewers and the many thermal springs found under the city have been cited as a dwelling place for the Bahkauv.

statement.id: Bahkauv biasanya digambarkan seperti anak sapi memanjang atau cacat bertaring tajam; menurut legenda ia sering mengintai di dekat mata air, sungai kecil, dan selokan, dan saluran pembuangan serta mata air panas di bawah Aachen disebut sebagai tempat tinggalnya.
statement.en: The Bahkauv is typically described as an elongated or deformed calf with sharp fangs; legend says it lurks near fountains, streams and sewers, and Aachen's sewers and hot springs are cited as its home.

basis_claims.quote: Nach dieser Sage hauste das Bahkauv in dem Abwasserkanal der Thermalquellen am Büchel, dem so genannten Kolbert. Seine Gestalt glich einem großen Kalb mit einem zottigen Fell. Im Maul hatte es scharfe Zähne, und seine klobigen Augen leuchteten im Dunkeln. Seine Pfoten sahen aus wie Bärentatzen mit scharfen Krallen, und sein Schweif war geschuppt

statement.id: Menurut sage, Bahkauv tinggal di saluran buangan mata air panas di Büchel yang disebut Kolbert; wujudnya seperti anak sapi besar berbulu kusut, bergigi tajam, bermata menyala dalam gelap, bercakar seperti beruang, dan berekor bersisik.
statement.en: By the legend the Bahkauv lived in the drain of the hot springs at the Büchel, the Kolbert; it looked like a large shaggy calf with sharp teeth, eyes glowing in the dark, bear-like clawed paws and a scaly tail.

basis_claims.quote: Das Bahkauv hat aber nie jemanden umgebracht und auch Frauen und Kinder nie belästigt.

statement.id: Namun Bahkauv tak pernah membunuh siapa pun dan tak pernah mengganggu perempuan maupun anak-anak.
statement.en: But the Bahkauv never killed anyone and never troubled women or children.

basis_claims.quote: Worm, wurm or wyrm (Old English: wyrm ; Old Norse: ormr ; Old High German: wurm ), meaning serpent, are archaic terms for dragons (Old English: draca ; Old Norse: dreki/*draki ; Old High German: trahho ) in the wider Germanic mythology and folklore, in which they are often portrayed as large venomous snakes and hoarders of gold.

statement.id: Worm, wurm, atau wyrm (Inggris Kuno wyrm, Nordik Kuno ormr, Jerman Hulu Kuno wurm), berarti "ular", adalah istilah kuno untuk naga dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Jermanik, yang sering digambarkan sebagai ular besar berbisa dan penimbun emas.
statement.en: Worm, wurm or wyrm (Old English wyrm, Old Norse ormr, Old High German wurm), meaning serpent, are archaic terms for dragons in Germanic mythology and folklore, often shown as large venomous snakes hoarding gold.

basis_claims.quote: In Germaanske draak is in mytysk bist ôfkomstich út 'e mytology en folkloare fan 'e Germaanske folken, dat kwa skaaimerken sterk ôfwykt fan hoe't in draak ornaris foarsteld wurdt. Ynstee fan in mei skobben bepânsere lichem mei fjouwer poaten, in lange sturt en twa flearmûseftige wjukken op 'e rêch hat in Germaanske draak de foarm fan in gigantyske slange, sûnder poaten of wjukken.

statement.id: Naga Jermanik adalah hewan mitos dari mitologi dan cerita rakyat bangsa Jermanik yang cirinya sangat berbeda dari gambaran naga biasa: bukannya bertubuh bersisik berkaki empat, berekor panjang, dan bersayap kelelawar, ia berbentuk ular raksasa tanpa kaki atau sayap.
statement.en: The Germanic dragon (Germaanske draak) is a mythical beast of Germanic peoples' mythology and folklore that differs sharply from the usual dragon: instead of a scaly four-legged body, long tail and bat wings, it has the form of a gigantic snake (gigantyske slange) without legs (poaten) or wings (wjukken).

basis_claims.quote: The association between dragons and hoards of treasure is widespread in Germanic literature ... In the Völsung Cycle, Fáfnir , upon claiming a hoard of treasure, including the ring Andvaranaut, transforms into a dragon to protect and brood over it.

statement.id: Kaitan naga dengan timbunan harta tersebar luas dalam sastra Jermanik; dalam siklus Völsung, Fáfnir yang menguasai timbunan harta, termasuk cincin Andvaranaut, berubah menjadi naga untuk menjaga dan mengeraminya.
statement.en: The link between dragons and treasure hoards is widespread in Germanic literature; in the Völsung Cycle Fáfnir, having claimed a hoard including the ring Andvaranaut, becomes a dragon to guard and brood over it.

statement.en: In The Boyhood Deeds of Fionn, a salmon ate nine hazelnuts fallen into the Well of Wisdom and gained all the world's knowledge.

basis_claims.quote: The poet Finn Eces (or Finegas) spent seven years fishing for this salmon. Finally Finn caught the salmon and gave the fish to Fionn, his servant and son of Cumhall, with instructions to cook it but on no account eat any of it.

statement.id: Finn Eces (Finegas) memancing tujuh tahun, lalu memberi ikan kepada Fionn putra Cumhall untuk dimasak tanpa dimakan. Fionn mac Cumhaill.

statement.en: The Saumon de la sagesse ate nine hazelnuts fallen into the Boyne or Shannon, grew enormous and knew everything.

basis_claims.quote: The redcap (or powrie) is a type of malevolent, murderous goblin found in folklore of the Anglo-Scottish border region. basis_claims.quote: Redcap is depicted as "a short, thickset old elf with long prominent teeth, skinny fingers armed with talons like eagles, large eyes of a fiery red colour, grisly hair streaming down his shoulders, iron boots, a pikestaff in his left hand, and a red cap on his head".

basis_claims.quote: The ceasg [kʲʰɛsk] is a mermaid in Scottish folklore with the upper body of a beautiful woman merging with the tail of a grilse (a young salmon). She is also known in Scottish Gaelic as maighdean na tuinne ("maid of the wave") or maighdean mhara ("maid of the sea").

statement.id: Ceasg putri duyung folklor Skotlandia (Scottish, Skotlandia), tubuh perempuan cantik berekor grilse; disebut maighdean na tuinne / maighdean mhara dalam Gaelik Skotlandia (Scottish Gaelic).
statement.en: The ceasg is a mermaid of Scottish folklore with a woman's body and a grilse tail; called maighdean na tuinne / maighdean mhara in Scottish Gaelic.
