gana.depicted_variant: Three-headed dancing gana in 14th-century Kumbhesvara Uma-Mahesvara relief
visual_requirements: Exactly three distinct heads sharing one rotund torso
Two arms and two dancing legs, complete figure within frame
Joyful Shiva-attendant character without deity conflation

basis_claims.quote: In Hinduism, the Gaṇas are attendants of Shiva and live on Mount Kailash. Ganesha was chosen as their leader by Shiva; the deity's title is gaṇeśa or gaṇapati, meaning, "lord or leader of the ganas". They are referred to as Shivaganas or Rudraganas and Rudraganikas are considered the female equivalents.

statement.id: Gana dalam konteks mitologi Hindu adalah para pengiring Shiva yang tinggal di Kailash.
statement.en: Ganas in Hindu mythological context are Shiva's attendants living on Kailash.

basis_claims.quote: They are envisioned as rotund gnomes, often rambunctious and full of zest. They dance and play music for Shiva and his wife Parvati.

statement.id: LACMA menggambarkan gana sebagai sosok kerdil gemuk yang menari dan memainkan musik untuk Shiva serta Parvati.
statement.en: LACMA describes ganas as rotund gnomes dancing and playing music for Shiva and Parvati.

nonhuman_features: Three complete separate heads and necks joined to one stocky body
gana.historical_basis: Uses a specific attested historical gana iconographic variant, alongside existing research identifying ganas as Shiva's rotund dancing attendants.
artistic_changes: Living skin, black hair, ochre/ivory dhoti, jewelry arrangement, Himalayan terrace and golden woodland light are visual interpretation of a carved figure. No copied relief background or additional deity.

additional_sources.title: Global Nepali Museum — Uma-Mahesvara, Kumbhesvara, Patan, 14th century
additional_sources.evidence: Lain Singh Bangdel object catalogue identifies a three-headed dancing gana beside Ganesha in the lower register. Primary relief photograph individually viewed; figure has one body, three heads, two arms and two dancing legs.

visual_requirements: Female forest guardian Nordic Rå
Coherent anatomy and documented mythic scene
ra.aura: Presence through source-backed form and physical scene; no generic glow, ribbons or magical mist.

basis_claims.quote: short for rådare ("ruler") from råda (to rule, to advise) from old Norse ráða, is a spirit who is the keeper or warden of a particular location or landform. The rå is known both in Nordic culture and in the Sami culture, where it is called radie.

statement.id: Rå, kependekan dari rådare ("penguasa"), dari råda ("memerintah, menasihati") dan Nordik Kuno ráða, adalah roh penjaga suatu tempat atau bentang alam, dikenal dalam budaya Nordik maupun Sami, yang menyebutnya radie.
statement.en: Rå, short for rådare ('ruler'), from råda ('to rule, to advise') and Old Norse ráða, is a spirit keeping a particular place or landform, known in both Nordic and Sami culture, where it is called radie.

basis_claims.quote: It was important for humans to cultivate good relationships with them, since they had power over the natural forces and animals under their care, and could cause both good and bad luck for humans who interfered with the places and creatures under their watch.

statement.id: Manusia penting menjaga hubungan baik dengan mereka, karena mereka menguasai kekuatan alam dan hewan di bawah asuhannya dan dapat membawa untung maupun sial bagi orang yang mengganggu tempat dan makhluk yang dijaganya.
statement.en: It was important for people to keep good relations with them, as they ruled the natural forces and animals in their care and could bring good or bad luck to anyone interfering with what they watched over.

basis_claims.quote: The different species of rår are sometimes distinguished according to the different spheres of nature with which each was associated, such as skogsrå or hulder (forest), sjörå (freshwater) or havsrå (saltwater), and bergsrå (mountains).

statement.id: Jenis-jenis rår kadang dibedakan menurut wilayah alam yang dikaitkan dengannya, seperti skogsrå atau hulder (hutan), sjörå (air tawar), havsrå (air asin), dan bergsrå (gunung).
statement.en: The kinds of rår are sometimes told apart by their sphere of nature, such as skogsrå or hulder (forest), sjörå (fresh water), havsrå (salt water) and bergsrå (mountains).

basis_claims.quote: Les rår peuvent apparaître sous forme animale ou sous la forme d'un homme ou d'une femme ; le skogsrå et le bergsrå sont généralement décrits comme féminins.

statement.id: Rår bisa tampil berwujud hewan atau sebagai laki-laki atau perempuan; skogsrå dan bergsrå biasanya digambarkan perempuan.
statement.en: Rår may appear as animals or as a man or woman; the skogsrå and bergsrå are usually described as female.

artistic_changes: Painterly square composition
Clothing, weather and exact setting details are editorial unless identified in claims

presentation_revision.rationale: Replaces ordinary animal presentation with Female forest guardian Nordic Rå

pixie.depicted_variant: Joseph Jacobs Fairy Ointment pixie morphology: pointed ears, flat nose and long hairy paws
visual_requirements: One small adult fairy sprite with two naturally pointed bodily ears and two hairy paw hands
One head, two arms and two legs; full frame
Playful benign mischievous dance aura, no added wings or horns
pixie.aura: Playful benign mischievous dancing Cornish/Devon fairy sprite

basis_claims.quote: A pixie (also called pisky, pixy, pixi, pizkie, piskie, or pigsie in parts of Cornwall and Devon) is a mythical creature of British folklore.

statement.id: Pixie (pisky, pixy, pixi, pizkie, piskie, pigsie di Cornwall dan Devon) adalah makhluk mitos cerita rakyat Britania (British folklore).
statement.en: A pixie (pisky, pixy, piskie or pigsie in Cornwall and Devon) is a mythical creature of British folklore.

basis_claims.quote: Pixies are speculated to be particularly concentrated in the high moorland areas around Cornwall and Devon, suggesting some Celtic origin for the belief and name. However, the word 'pixie' (under various forms) also appears in Dorset, Somerset and to a lesser extent in Sussex, Wiltshire and Hampshire.

statement.id: Pixie terutama di dataran tinggi Cornwall dan Devon, mengisyaratkan asal Kelt (Celtic); kata pixie juga ada di Dorset, Somerset, dan lain-lain.
statement.en: Pixies cluster in the moorlands of Cornwall and Devon, suggesting a Celtic origin; the word also appears in Dorset, Somerset and elsewhere.

basis_claims.quote: Similar to the Irish and Scottish Aos Sí (also spelled Aos Sidhe), pixies are believed to inhabit ancient underground sites such as stone circles, barrows, dolmens, ringforts, or menhirs.

statement.id: Seperti Aos Sí Irlandia dan Skotlandia (Irish, Scottish), pixie mendiami situs bawah tanah kuno seperti lingkaran batu, barrow, dolmen, ringfort, menhir.
statement.en: Like the Irish and Scottish Aos Sí, pixies inhabit ancient underground sites such as stone circles, barrows, dolmens, ringforts or menhirs.

basis_claims.quote: In traditional regional lore, pixies are generally benign, mischievous, short of stature, and childlike; they are fond of dancing and wrestling outdoors, which they perform through the night.

statement.id: Pixie umumnya tak jahat, usil, pendek, kekanak-kanakan, suka menari dan bergulat sepanjang malam.
statement.en: Pixies are generally benign, mischievous, short and childlike, dancing and wrestling outdoors through the night.

nonhuman_features: Two long pointed bodily ears
Long hairy pawlike hands
pixie.historical_basis: Joseph Jacobs, English Fairy Tales, Fairy Ointment, directly describes revealed pixie household as flat-nosed imps with pointed ears and long hairy paws. Museum of Witchcraft and Magic's own pisky exhibition text documents pointed ears and squinting eyes. Current c01/c02 establish local type; c03 standing-stone habitat, c04 benign mischievous short childlike dancing character. Adult solitary depiction is generic sprite portrait of documented morphology, not reproduction of infant scene.
artistic_changes: Solitary adult generic pixie portrait rather than reproducing child/infant household episode
Ragged tunic, dance pose and standing-stone clearing combine documented general type/habitat traits

additional_sources.title: English Fairy Tales: Fairy Ointment
additional_sources.author: Joseph Jacobs
additional_sources.basis: Primary tale describes flat-nosed pixies, pointed ears and long hairy paws

additional_sources.title: The Upstairs Gallery part three
additional_sources.basis: Museum's pisky display documents pointed ears, round face, squinting eyes and medieval-style tunic

furutsubaki-no-rei.depicted_variant: Sekien's old camellia apparition tree, botanical form
visual_requirements: Ancient knotted camellia tree as the apparition itself
Glossy evergreen leaves and red layered camellia flowers
Whole fallen blooms and dense low flowering branch
Entire botanical canopy and roots within frame
furutsubaki-no-rei.aura: Ancient melancholic deceptive haunted tree; quiet foreboding

basis_claims.quote: The Furutsubaki-no-rei (Japanese: 古椿の霊, "old camellia spirit") is a yōkai said to inhabit and develop from old camellia trees.

statement.id: Furutsubaki-no-rei adalah yōkai yang dikaitkan dengan pohon kamelia tua.
statement.en: Furutsubaki-no-rei is a yōkai associated with old camellia trees.

basis_claims.quote: According to Toriyama Sekien's “Konjaku Gazu Zoku Hyakki”, a spirit dwells in an old camellia tree, turning into an apparition tree to fool people.

statement.id: Sekien menggambarkan kamelia tua yang dihuni roh penipu.
statement.en: Sekien describes an old camellia inhabited by a deceptive spirit.

basis_claims.quote: The tsubaki is an evergreen tree which has the strange behavior of not losing its flowers gradually, petal by petal, but dropping them all at once to the ground.

statement.id: Bunga pohon itu jatuh utuh, bukan helai demi helai.
statement.en: The tree’s flowers fall whole rather than petal by petal.

basis_claims.quote: As a result, it long been associated with death and strangeness in Japan (and is also taboo to bring as gifts to hospitals or sick people).

statement.id: Ciri tersebut dikaitkan dengan kematian dalam tradisi Jepang.
statement.en: This feature is associated with death in Japanese tradition.

basis_claims.quote: In Akita prefecture, long ago, a man heard a sad and lonely voice coming from the tree one night. ... the tsubaki would cry a warning every time something bad was going to happen.

statement.id: Cerita Akita menafsirkan tangisan pohon sebagai peringatan bencana.
statement.en: An Akita tale interprets the tree’s crying as a warning of misfortune.

nonhuman_features: Whole botanical camellia apparition rather than human woman disguise
Tree trunk, branches, evergreen leaves and flowers with no human anatomy
furutsubaki-no-rei.historical_basis: Reviewed c02 explicitly calls Sekien form an apparition tree; individually viewed 1779 Sekien plate corroborates botanical tree depiction. This is the yōkai's own source form, not merely a tree prop or merchant transformed into bee.
furutsubaki-no-rei.artistic_changes: Red camellia colour, twilight palette, textured bark and garden fence rendering are illustrative choices; historical plate supplies form and dense low flower mass.

additional_sources.title: Toriyama Sekien, Furutsubaki-no-rei (1779)
additional_sources.purpose: Primary historical plate individually inspected; shows old botanical tree and dense low branch flowers, not a humanoid tree-face.

kumbhanda.depicted_variant: Japanese Buddhist horse-headed seated kumbhanda playing cymbals
visual_requirements: One horse head on pot-bellied humanoid torso
Exactly two arms with two cymbals and coherently crossed clothed legs
Historic lesser guardian-spirit character without unrelated fantasy parts
kumbhanda.aura: Joyful yet uncanny musical guardian spirit

basis_claims.quote: A kumbhāṇḍa (Sanskrit) or kumbhaṇḍa (Pāli) is one of a group of dwarfish, misshapen spirits among the lesser deities of Buddhist mythology.

statement.id: Kumbhanda adalah kelompok roh bertubuh kecil dan tidak proporsional di antara dewa rendah Buddha.
statement.en: Kumbhandas are a group of dwarfish misshapen spirits among lesser Buddhist deities.

basis_claims.quote: Kumbhāṇḍa was a dialectal form for "gourd", so they may get their name from being thought to resemble gourds in some way, e.g. in having big stomachs.

statement.id: Namanya dikaitkan dengan labu dan perut besar yang menyerupai labu.
statement.en: Their name is associated with gourds and gourd like large bellies.

basis_claims.quote: The kumbhāṇḍas are classed among the Cāturmahārājika deities, and are subject to the Great King Virūḍhaka, Guardian of the South. One of their chiefs is called Kumbhīra.

statement.id: Mereka termasuk dewa Caturmaharajika dan tunduk kepada Virudhaka, penjaga selatan.
statement.en: They belong to the Caturmaharajika deities under Virudhaka, guardian of the south.

basis_claims.quote: a great king named Virulha who has a retinue of attendants, and is the sovereign lord of Kumbhandas. Attended by the Kumbhandas he enjoys their song and dance.

statement.id: Dalam Atanatiya Sutta, Virulha memimpin kumbhanda yang menyanyi dan menari bersamanya.
statement.en: In the Atanatiya Sutta Virulha rules the kumbhandas who sing and dance with him.

nonhuman_features: Complete equine head, elongated horse muzzle, horse ears and mane attached to humanoid body
kumbhanda.historical_basis: Specific Japanese/esoteric Buddhist iconographic variant, corroborated by historical drawing and Buddhist dictionary rather than importing the shape from a generic Kinnara or modern game.
artistic_changes: Brown colouring, exact cymbal/pendant finish, ivory cloth, gold light and temple garden are scene choices. Source supplies horse-headed body, belly, seated posture and cymbals.

additional_sources.title: Shinsan Butsuzō Zukan Ten no maki (1932), historical illustration labelled 鳩槃荼
additional_sources.evidence: Primary drawing individually viewed; selected the right horse-headed, round-bellied seated figure holding two small cymbals. Commons identifies original volume and NDL persistent ID1189759.

additional_sources.title: The Seeker's Glossary of Buddhism, 2nd ed.1998, p.397, Kumbhanda entry
additional_sources.evidence: Dictionary quotation citing Dait p205 explicitly describes horse head with man's body, Virudhaka retinue and Garbhadhatu mandala. Source indexed text verified; PDF fetch timed out on latest attempt.

fairy-queen.depicted_variant: Fairy Queen encounters Thomas the Rhymer
visual_requirements: Fairy Queen encounters Thomas the Rhymer
Coherent anatomy and documented mythic scene
fairy-queen.aura: Presence through source-backed form and physical scene; no generic glow, ribbons or magical mist.

basis_claims.quote: In folklore and literature, the Fairy Queen or Queen of the Fairies is a female ruler of the fairies, sometimes but not always paired with a king. Depending on the work, she may be named or unnamed; Titania and Mab are two frequently used names.

statement.id: Fairy Queen (Queen of the Fairies) penguasa perempuan peri, kadang berpasangan raja; nama Titania dan Mab; di Britania dan Irlandia.
statement.en: The Fairy Queen (Queen of the Fairies) is a female ruler of fairies, sometimes with a king; named Titania or Mab.

basis_claims.quote: An unnamed fairy queen appears in Thomas the Rhymer (Child 37), where she takes the titular character as her lover and leaves him with prophetic abilities.

statement.id: Dalam Thomas the Rhymer ratu peri menjadikan Thomas kekasih dan memberinya kemampuan bernubuat.
statement.en: In Thomas the Rhymer a fairy queen takes Thomas as lover and gives him prophetic powers.

artistic_changes: Painterly square composition
Clothing, weather and exact setting details are editorial unless identified in claims

presentation_revision.rationale: Replaces ordinary animal presentation with Fairy Queen encounters Thomas the Rhymer

brown-lady-of-raynham-hall.depicted_variant: Colonel Loftus1835 Brown Lady with empty eye sockets
visual_requirements: Both eyeballs absent with structural hollow orbital cavities
Brown brocade dress
Solemn haunted Raynham Hall apparition

basis_claims.quote: The Brown Lady of Raynham Hall is a ghost that reportedly haunts Raynham Hall in Norfolk, England. It became one of the most famous hauntings in the United Kingdom when photographers from Country Life magazine claimed to have captured its image. The "Brown Lady" is so named because of the brown brocade dress it is claimed she wears.

statement.id: Brown Lady of Raynham Hall hantu Raynham Hall, Norfolk, Inggris (England); terkenal di Britania Raya (United Kingdom) lewat foto Country Life; nama dari gaun brokat cokelat.
statement.en: The Brown Lady of Raynham Hall is a ghost of Raynham Hall, Norfolk, England, famous in the United Kingdom via a Country Life photograph; named for her brown brocade dress.

basis_claims.quote: Loftus and another guest named Hawkins said they had seen the "Brown Lady" one night as they approached their bedrooms, noting in particular the dated brown dress she wore. The following evening Loftus claimed to have seen the "Brown Lady" again, later reporting that on this occasion he was drawn to the spectre's empty eye-sockets

statement.id: Lucia C. Stone: Natal 1835, Kolonel Loftus dan Hawkins melihat Brown Lady; Loftus melihat rongga mata kosong.
statement.en: Lucia C. Stone: at Christmas 1835 Colonel Loftus and Hawkins saw the Brown Lady; Loftus noted her empty eye sockets.

basis_claims.quote: The first recorded claim of a sighting of the ghost was by Lucia C. Stone concerning a gathering at Raynham Hall in the Christmas of 1835.

statement.id: Penampakan pertama tercatat oleh Lucia C. Stone pada Natal 1835 di Raynham Hall.
statement.en: First recorded sighting by Lucia C. Stone at Christmas 1835 at Raynham Hall.

nonhuman_features: Two structurally hollow empty eye sockets without eyeballs
brown-lady-of-raynham-hall.historical_basis: Reviewed c04 quotes Colonel Loftus's1835 sighting of empty eye-sockets, c01 brown brocade identity. Selected a reported folklore apparition, not presented as proof that disputed1936 photograph is genuine.
brown-lady-of-raynham-hall.artistic_changes: Dress ornament, staircase arrangement, hair and candle lighting are illustrative choices; smooth clean recessed cavity rendering makes source detail legible without gore.

visual_requirements: Sorbian white-clad death messenger
Coherent source-supported anatomy and identifying features
No invented animal/monster additions or text
bozalosc.aura: One little white-clad female death messenger with long unkempt hair and red eyes, weeping under a dark cottage window beside an elder bush in Lusatia. Human anatomy retained, eyes bloodshot/red rather than lasers.

basis_claims.quote: Božalość, also transliterated as Božaloshtsh or Bozaloshtsh is a messenger of misfortune or death in Wendish mythology (Wends, Lusatian Sorbs).

statement.id: Božalość, juga ditulis Božaloshtsh atau Bozaloshtsh, adalah pembawa kabar kemalangan atau kematian dalam mitologi Wend (orang Sorbia Lusatia).
statement.en: Božalość, also transliterated Božaloshtsh or Bozaloshtsh, is a messenger of misfortune or death in Wendish mythology (the Wends, Lusatian Sorbs).

basis_claims.quote: An 1886 article Das Spreewaldhaus by W. v. Schulenburg associates it with the elder bush and describes it as a woman dressed in white with long, unkempt hair and red eyes

statement.id: Artikel tahun 1886 Das Spreewaldhaus karya W. v. Schulenburg mengaitkannya dengan semak elder dan menggambarkannya sebagai perempuan berpakaian putih, berambut panjang kusut, dan bermata merah.
statement.en: An 1886 article, Das Spreewaldhaus by W. v. Schulenburg, links it with the elder bush and describes it as a woman in white with long, unkempt hair and red eyes.

basis_claims.quote: Biren Bonnerjea describes it as a little woman with long hair, who cries under the window of someone who is about to die.

statement.id: Biren Bonnerjea menggambarkannya sebagai perempuan kecil berambut panjang yang menangis di bawah jendela orang yang akan meninggal.
statement.en: Biren Bonnerjea describes it as a little long-haired woman who weeps under the window of someone about to die.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; red eyes, weeping death-omen woman.
bozalosc.historical_basis: Božalość, also transliterated Božaloshtsh or Bozaloshtsh, is a messenger of misfortune or death in Wendish mythology (the Wends, Lusatian Sorbs). An 1886 article, Das Spreewaldhaus by W. v. Schulenburg, links it with the elder bush and describes it as a woman in white with long, unkempt hair and red eyes. Biren Bonnerjea describes it as a little long-haired woman who weeps under the window of someone about to die.
artistic_changes: Exact facial likeness, clothing folds, compositional details and painterly lighting are illustrative; no anatomical deformation asserted beyond selected documented account.

batibat.depicted_variant: Ilocano ancient corpulent female tree-post nightmare spirit
visual_requirements: One ancient extremely corpulent female spirit
Rough timber house support post
Empty sleeping mat and oppressive nightmare atmosphere

basis_claims.quote: The Batibat is a vengeful demon found in Ilocano folklore. In Tagalog folklore, the creature is called Bangungot. The batibat takes the form of an ancient, grotesquely obese, tree-dwelling female spirit.

statement.id: Batibat adalah setan pendendam dalam cerita rakyat Ilokano, disebut bangungot dalam cerita rakyat Tagalog, berwujud roh perempuan tua yang sangat gemuk penghuni pohon.
statement.en: The batibat is a vengeful demon of Ilocano folklore, called bangungot in Tagalog folklore, taking the form of an ancient, grossly obese, tree-dwelling female spirit.

basis_claims.quote: They usually come in contact with humans when the trees in which they reside are felled and are made homeless, especially when their tree is made into a support post for a house.

statement.id: Batibat biasanya bersentuhan dengan manusia ketika pohonnya ditebang, terutama bila dijadikan tiang rumah, lalu ia menghuni sisa pohonnya.
statement.en: Batibat usually meet humans when their trees are felled, especially when made into a house post, and then inhabit what is left of the tree.

basis_claims.quote: When a person does sleep near it, the batibat transforms into its true form and attacks the person by suffocating their victim and invading their dream space, causing sleep paralysis and waking nightmares. This condition lends itself to the Ilocano word for nightmare, "batíbat"

statement.id: Batibat melarang manusia tidur di dekat tiangnya; bila ada yang tidur di sana, ia berubah ke wujud aslinya, menindih korban dan memasuki mimpinya hingga terjadi ketindihan dan mimpi buruk; dari sinilah kata Ilokano batíbat untuk mimpi buruk.
statement.en: The batibat forbids sleeping near its post; if someone does, it takes its true form, smothers the victim and invades their dreams, causing sleep paralysis and nightmares; hence the Ilocano word batíbat for nightmare.

nonhuman_features: Aged extremely corpulent female spirit associated with her felled tree's house post and nightmare attacks; no anatomical deformation claimed
batibat.historical_basis: Ilocano folklore describes an ancient very obese woman-shaped tree spirit that moves into a support post made from her tree and induces nightmares near it. Retains source-described human female anatomy without added monster traits.
artistic_changes: Exact face, clothing folds, composition, lighting and environment details are artistic choices; no unsupported anatomy introduced.

dark-watchers.depicted_variant: Tall featureless dark Santa Lucia Mountains watcher with brimmed hat and walking stick
visual_requirements: Featureless tall dark humanlike silhouette
Broad-brimmed hat and plain walking stick
Santa Lucia mountain ridge at twilight
dark-watchers.aura: Motionless uncanny supernatural observer at twilight

basis_claims.quote: The Dark Watchers (also known by early Spanish settlers as Los Vigilantes Oscuros) is a name given to a group of entities in California folklore purportedly seen observing travelers along the Santa Lucia Mountains.

statement.id: Dark Watchers adalah kelompok entitas dalam cerita rakyat California yang mengamati pelancong di Pegunungan Santa Lucia.
statement.en: The Dark Watchers is a group of entities in California folklore seen observing travelers along the Santa Lucia Mountains.

basis_claims.quote: The Dark Watchers are described as tall, sometimes giant-sized featureless dark silhouettes often adorned with brimmed hats or walking sticks.

statement.id: Dark Watchers digambarkan sebagai siluet hitam jangkung tanpa wajah yang mengenakan topi atau tongkat jalan.
statement.en: The Dark Watchers are described as tall featureless dark silhouettes with brimmed hats or walking sticks.

basis_claims.quote: They are most often reported to be seen in the hours around twilight and dawn.

statement.id: Mereka paling sering dilaporkan terlihat pada saat senja dan fajar.
statement.en: They are most often reported to be seen in the hours around twilight and dawn.

nonhuman_features: Documented featureless dark silhouette and unusually tall stature; no anatomical deformation is claimed
dark-watchers.historical_basis: Documented California folklore describes tall featureless silhouettes watching mountain travelers at twilight or dawn; hat and walking stick are explicitly attested.
artistic_changes: Single figure selected; exact ridge, clothing outline, colors and clouds are artistic setting choices.

borda-legendary-creature.depicted_variant: Emilia-Romagna blindfolded marsh witch with rope
visual_requirements: One sinister witch with opaque cloth blindfold
Coiled rope held away from any victim
Foggy Italian swamp or canal context
borda-legendary-creature.aura: Oppressive silent fog and swamp darkness

basis_claims.quote: It is a sort of witch that appears, blindfolded and horrible, both at night and on foggy days and kills anyone who has the misfortune to meet her.

statement.id: Ia semacam penyihir mengerikan bermata tertutup yang muncul pada malam hari dan hari berkabut, dan membunuh siapa pun yang malang bertemu dengannya.
statement.en: It is a kind of witch, blindfolded and horrible, that appears at night and on foggy days and kills anyone unlucky enough to meet her.

basis_claims.quote: It is a personification of the fear related to swamps and marshlands, and to ponds and canals, invoked by adults to scare children and keep them away from such potentially dangerous places.

statement.id: Ia personifikasi ketakutan akan rawa, kolam, dan kanal, yang dipakai orang dewasa untuk menakuti anak-anak agar menjauhi tempat berbahaya itu.
statement.en: It personifies the fear of swamps, ponds and canals, invoked by adults to scare children away from such dangerous places.

basis_claims.quote: Lullaby, the Borda binds beautiful children with a rope.

statement.id: Sebuah lagu nina bobo menyebut Borda mengikat anak-anak manis dengan tali lalu membunuh mereka.
statement.en: A lullaby says the Borda binds beautiful children with a rope and then kills them.

nonhuman_features: Blindfolded nocturnal fog witch of marshes; no anatomical deformation claimed
borda-legendary-creature.historical_basis: Documented Borda is a blindfolded frightening witch of Emilia-Romagna wetlands carrying the threatening rope from the lullaby. Human-shaped appearance is retained without invented fangs or claws.
artistic_changes: Exact face, costume details and ornament, landscape layout and illumination are artistic choices rather than additional historical claims.

visual_requirements: Bolivian small wizened cave weather-fairy
Coherent source-supported anatomy and identifying features
No invented animal/monster additions or text
acalica.aura: One very small wizened old man, a rarely-seen Bolivian cave-dwelling weather fairy, standing at the mouth of a rocky high Andean cave while a storm passes across distant mountains. Wrinkled aged face, modest worn earth-toned tunic and cloak as illustrative clothing, normal rounded human ears. Diminutive scale anchored by large rocks, uncanny solemn weather-controlling presence suggested by contrasting calm cave and windy cloudscape.

basis_claims.quote: Acalica are mythological creatures (sometimes called "weather-fairies") from Bolivia.

statement.id: Acalica adalah makhluk mitologi yang kadang disebut peri cuaca dari Bolivia.
statement.en: Acalica are mythological creatures (sometimes called 'weather-fairies') from Bolivia.

basis_claims.quote: They are said to control the weather, live in caves, and are very rarely seen.

statement.id: Mereka konon mengendalikan cuaca, tinggal di gua, dan sangat jarang terlihat.
statement.en: They are said to control the weather, live in caves, and are very rarely seen.

basis_claims.quote: When they do appear they are said to take the form of small, wizened men.

statement.id: Saat muncul, mereka konon berwujud pria kerdil yang keriput.
statement.en: When they do appear they are said to take the form of small, wizened men.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; small wizened man, cave-dwelling weather fairy.

brown-man-of-the-muirs.aura: One short sturdy broad dwarf-like man, guardian of wild animals of the Anglo-Scottish border moors. Brown earth-toned clothes, red unruly hair, fierce intense human eyes which gleam LIKE the eyes of a bull without being anatomically bovine. Standing alone amid heather, berries and low moor woodland across a narrow brook, sternly warning an unseen hunter outside picture. Normal human ears and limbs, no bull horns, bull eyes or animal head.

basis_claims.quote: In the folklore on the Anglo-Scottish border, the Brown Man of the Muirs is a dwarf who serves as a guardian spirit of wild animals.

statement.id: Brown Man of the Muirs, kurcaci folklor perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia (Anglo-Scottish), roh pelindung hewan liar.
statement.en: Brown Man of the Muirs, a dwarf of Anglo-Scottish border folklore, guardian spirit of wild animals.

basis_claims.quote: the "Brown man of the Muirs", a dwarf very strong and stoutly built, his dress brown like withered bracken, his head covered with frizzled red hair, his countenance ferocious, and his eyes glowing like those of a bull.

statement.id: William Henderson, Folklore of the Northern Counties (1879); Robert Surtees, Sir Walter Scott; Pemberontakan Besar (Great Rebellion); Newcastle; Elsdon; kurcaci kuat, berbaju cokelat, rambut merah, mata banteng.
statement.en: William Henderson, Folklore of the Northern Counties (1879); Robert Surtees, Sir Walter Scott; Great Rebellion; Newcastle; Elsdon; strong dwarf, brown dress, red hair, bull's eyes.

basis_claims.quote: the stranger reproved the hunter for trespassing on his demesnes and slaying the creatures who were his subjects, and informed him how he himself lived only on whortleberries, nuts, and apples, he invited him home.

statement.id: Menegur pemburu; makan beri, kacang, apel; mengundangnya pulang.
statement.en: Rebuked the hunter; eats berries, nuts, apples; invited him home.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; dwarf-sized woodland guardian with intensely shining human eyes.

cliodhna.depicted_variant: Irish Otherworld banshee queen with three healing-song birds and coastal wave
visual_requirements: One Irish Otherworld woman
Exactly three healing-song birds
Rocky Munster coast and powerful distant wave
cliodhna.aura: Luminous melancholy Otherworld coast and healing birdsong

basis_claims.quote: In Irish mythology, Clíodhna (Clídna, Clíodna, Clíona, sometimes anglicised to Cleena) is a Queen of the Banshees of the Tuatha Dé Danann. Clíodna of Carrigcleena is the potent banshee that rules as queen over the sióga (fairies) of South Munster, or Desmond.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Irlandia (Irish), Clíodhna (Clídna, Clíodna, Clíona, Cleena) Ratu Banshee (Queen of the Banshees) Tuatha Dé Danann; Clíodna dari Carrigcleena memerintah sióga di South Munster (Desmond); di Irlandia.
statement.en: In Irish mythology Clíodhna (Clídna, Clíodna, Clíona, Cleena) is a Queen of the Banshees of the Tuatha Dé Danann; Clíodna of Carrigcleena rules the sióga of South Munster (Desmond).

basis_claims.quote: In some Irish myths, Clíodhna is a goddess of love and beauty, and the patron of County Cork. She is said to have three brightly coloured birds who eat apples from an otherworldly tree and whose sweet song heals sickness.

statement.id: Dalam sebagian mitos ia dewi cinta dan kecantikan, pelindung County Cork, dengan tiga burung yang nyanyiannya menyembuhkan.
statement.en: In some myths she is a goddess of love and beauty, patron of County Cork, with three birds whose song heals.

basis_claims.quote: One of them treacherously played music which caused Cleena to fall asleep. Then a great wave came and swept her away. The place was then called Tonn Chlíodhna, "Clíodhna's Wave", which is near Glandore harbour.

statement.id: Musik membuat Cleena tertidur, ombak besar menyapunya; tempat itu Tonn Chlíodhna, Ombak Clíodhna (Clíodhna's Wave), dekat Glandore; di pantai Irlandia (Irish).
statement.en: Music lulled Cleena asleep and a great wave swept her away; the spot is Tonn Chlíodhna, Clíodhna's Wave, near Glandore.

nonhuman_features: Queen of banshees with three birds whose song heals; no anatomical deformation claimed
cliodhna.historical_basis: Irish myth presents Clíodhna as a beautiful Tuatha Dé Danann queen, associated with three healing-song birds and Clíodhna's Wave. Depicted in human female form, not with invented banshee anatomy.
artistic_changes: Exact face, costume details and ornament, landscape layout and illumination are artistic choices rather than additional historical claims.

leprechaun.depicted_variant: One diminutive bearded Irish solitary fairy shoemaker in a historical RED coat and modest trousers, commanding fierce cunning expression. Low camera almost at grass level makes his small real body imposing; enormous ordinary grass stems and tiny shoe on cobbler bench establish that he is very small, not giant. A treasure-crock of gold lies nearby at the end of a vivid natural rainbow after rain. Anatomically ordinary two arms two legs, no horns or wings, red clothing rather than green modern mascot. No magically floating gold, energy beam or branded logo.

basis_claims.quote: A leprechaun (Irish: lucharachán/leipreachán/luchorpán ) is a diminutive supernatural being in Irish folklore, classed by some as a type of solitary fairy. They are usually depicted as little bearded men, wearing a coat and hat, who partake in mischief. In later times, they have been depicted as shoe-makers who have a hidden pot of gold at the end of the rainbow.

statement.id: Leprechaun (Irish: leipreachán) adalah makhluk gaib kecil cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish folklore), peri penyendiri (solitary fairy), lelaki kecil berjanggut yang usil, dan pembuat sepatu dengan sepanci emas di ujung pelangi.
statement.en: A leprechaun (Irish: leipreachán) is a diminutive supernatural being of Irish folklore, a solitary fairy, a little bearded man of mischief, and a shoemaker with a pot of gold at the rainbow's end.

basis_claims.quote: The leprechaun is said to be a solitary creature, whose principal occupation is making and cobbling shoes, and who enjoys practical jokes.

statement.id: Leprechaun adalah makhluk penyendiri (solitary) yang pekerjaan utamanya membuat dan menambal sepatu (shoes) dan gemar bercanda.
statement.en: The leprechaun is a solitary creature whose main work is making and cobbling shoes and who enjoys practical jokes.

basis_claims.quote: According to William Butler Yeats, the great wealth of the leprechauns comes from the "treasure-crocks, buried of old in war-time", which they have uncovered and appropriated.

statement.id: Menurut William Butler Yeats, kekayaan leprechaun berasal dari guci harta (treasure-crocks) yang dikubur pada masa perang (war-time).
statement.en: According to William Butler Yeats, leprechauns' wealth comes from treasure-crocks buried in war-time.

basis_claims.quote: Before the 20th century, it was generally held that the leprechaun wore red, not green.

statement.id: Sebelum abad ke-20 leprechaun umumnya dianggap berpakaian merah (red), bukan hijau (green).
statement.en: Before the 20th century the leprechaun was generally held to wear red, not green.

basis_claims.quote: Menurut legenda, leprechaun memiliki sebuah gentong yang berisi emas. Gentong tersebut dikatakan di letakkan di ujung pelangi. Dikatakan bahwa siapapun yang berhasil mencuri gentong emas tersebut, maka sang dewa muslihat tersebut harus mengabulkan 3 permintaan jika gentongnya ingin dikembalikan.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, leprechaun punya gentong emas di ujung pelangi; pencurinya mendapat 3 permintaan sebagai ganti gentong itu.
statement.en: By legend the leprechaun has a pot of gold (gentong emas) at the rainbow's end (ujung pelangi); its thief gets 3 wishes (permintaan) for its return.

artistic_changes: Low-angle framing, painterly materials and environmental color are artistic rendering.
Effects are limited to the cited domains, deeds, attributes or iconography; natural light and scale supply presence where no elemental ability is documented.

presentation_revision.rationale: Big names (major gods, archangels, demon princes, primordial monsters, famous literary beings) must look imposing and powerful: an epic, awe-inspiring or terrifying presence that matches their standing in the tradition.

arikura-no-baba.aura: One elderly human-shaped woman of Gifu's Takayama folklore in a modest unpatterned Japanese robe, grey hair tied simply, praying quietly beside an upright awl placed at a rural doorway. Far beyond doorway a mountain rises at night, its formerly violent rumbling settling into quiet. Both human hands joined coherently for prayer, face old and resolute, normal anatomy, no horse hooves attached to her body.

basis_claims.quote: Arikura-no-baba (蟻鞍の婆, ant-saddle hag) is a character from the folklore of Gifu Prefecture, Japan.

statement.id: Arikura-no-baba adalah sosok gaib dalam cerita rakyat Gifu.
statement.en: Arikura-no-baba is a supernatural figure in Gifu folklore.

basis_claims.quote: She was an old woman with supernatural powers who lived in Takayama.

statement.id: Ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan tua yang tinggal di Takayama.
statement.en: She is portrayed as an old woman living in Takayama.

basis_claims.quote: 昔小鳥山の南の方が鳴動した時、老婆が７日目の夜に神に祈り門口に錐を立てたら音は止んだ。また、温泉があったが若者の為にならないと老婆が馬の爪を湯の中に入れたところ温泉が冷たくなった。

statement.id: Ringkasan katalog menggambarkan doanya menghentikan gemuruh gunung.
statement.en: A catalogue summary describes her prayer stopping a mountain’s rumbling.

basis_claims.quote: 昔小鳥山の南の方が鳴動した時、老婆が７日目の夜に神に祈り門口に錐を立てたら音は止んだ。また、温泉があったが若者の為にならないと老婆が馬の爪を湯の中に入れたところ温泉が冷たくなった。

statement.en: She prays on the seventh night of the disturbance.
statement.id: Ia berdoa pada malam ketujuh gangguan tersebut.

basis_claims.quote: 昔小鳥山の南の方が鳴動した時、老婆が７日目の夜に神に祈り門口に錐を立てたら音は止んだ。また、温泉があったが若者の為にならないと老婆が馬の爪を湯の中に入れたところ温泉が冷たくなった。

statement.en: Her rite includes placing an awl upright at the entrance.
statement.id: Ritualnya mencakup penempatan penusuk dalam posisi tegak di pintu masuk.

Coherent source-supported anatomy and identifying features
No invented animal/monster additions or text
knocker-folklore.aura: One tiny approximately two-foot tall human-shaped Cornish mining spirit in humble old working clothes and cloth cap, wrinkled male face, normal rounded ears, knocking on a dark tin-mine rock wall with a small mining hammer. One other hand holds a simple candle whose warm light reveals mineral veins. Broad mine passage and tool size establish tiny scale. Solemn uncanny warning of mine collapse in damp subterranean darkness, no collapsed victims, no modern equipment.

basis_claims.quote: The Knocker, Knacker, or Tommyknocker (US) is a mythical, subterranean, gnome-like creature in Cornish and Devon folklore. The Welsh counterpart is the coblyn. It is closely related to the Irish leprechaun, Kentish kloker and the English and Scottish brownie. The Cornish describe the creature as a little person 2 ft 0 in (0.61 m) tall

statement.id: Knocker (Knacker, Tommyknocker, AS) makhluk bawah tanah mirip gnome cerita rakyat Cornwall (Cornish) dan Devon; Wales (Welsh) coblyn; kerabat leprechaun Irlandia (Irish), kloker Kent (Kentish), brownie Inggris dan Skotlandia (English and Scottish); 61 cm; usil mencuri perkakas (Coblyn, Leprechaun, Brownie); di Britania dan AS.
statement.en: The Knocker (Knacker, Tommyknocker) is a subterranean gnome-like creature of Cornish and Devon folklore; Welsh coblyn; kin to the Irish leprechaun, Kentish kloker, English and Scottish brownie; 0.61 m tall.

basis_claims.quote: Cornish miners believed that the diminutive Knockers beckoned them toward finding rich veins of tin. As miners changed from independent, family-owned operators to hired laborers for large industrialized companies, there was an increased concern for safety, reflected in the knockers' new role. They knocked on the mine walls to warn of impending collapse.

statement.id: Penambang Cornwall (Cornish): knocker menuntun ke urat timah, mengetuk untuk memperingatkan runtuhan.
statement.en: Cornish miners: knockers led them to tin and knocked to warn of collapse.

basis_claims.quote: Generally considered benevolent, they were also tricksters who would hide tools and extinguish candles. They are similar to the coblynau of Welsh miners.

statement.id: Umumnya baik, tetapi usil: menyembunyikan perkakas, memadamkan lilin; mirip coblynau Wales (Welsh).
statement.en: Generally benevolent but tricksters hiding tools and snuffing candles; like Welsh coblynau.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; two-foot subterranean spirit warning miners by knocking.
knocker-folklore.historical_basis: The Knocker (Knacker, Tommyknocker) is a subterranean gnome-like creature of Cornish and Devon folklore; Welsh coblyn; kin to the Irish leprechaun, Kentish kloker, English and Scottish brownie; 0.61 m tall. Cornish miners: knockers led them to tin and knocked to warn of collapse. Generally benevolent but tricksters hiding tools and snuffing candles; like Welsh coblynau.

moss-people.aura: One child-sized but elderly grey hairy human-shaped forest spirit of German Moss People, modestly clothed in actual moss-clad woven garments, standing beside a hollow old forest tree and holding a few healing herbs. Short old figure with grey hairy face, ordinary rounded human ears, both coherent hands visible, human limbs. Moss is clothing, NEVER botanical tissue or tree skin. Forest roots and hollow trunk establish size, protective herbal healing forest atmosphere, no invented tree-face or branch hands.

basis_claims.quote: are a class of fairy-folk, variously compared to dwarfs, elves, or spirits, described in German folklore as having an intimate connection to trees and the forest.

statement.id: Orang lumut (Moosleute), juga orang kayu (Holzleute) atau orang hutan (Waldleute), adalah golongan peri yang dibandingkan dengan kurcaci, elf, atau roh, digambarkan dalam cerita rakyat Jerman (German) memiliki ikatan erat dengan pohon dan hutan.
statement.en: Moss people (Moosleute), also wood folk (Holzleute) or forest folk (Waldleute), are a class of fairy-folk compared with dwarfs, elves or spirits, described in German folklore as intimately tied to trees and the forest.

basis_claims.quote: The moss people are sometimes described as similar to dwarfs, being the same size as children, but "grey and old-looking, hairy, and clad in moss." Sometimes, moss folk are also bigger. In other descriptions they are said to be pretty.

statement.id: Orang lumut kadang digambarkan mirip kurcaci, sebesar anak-anak, tetapi kelabu, tampak tua, berbulu, dan berbalut lumut; kadang lebih besar, dan dalam deskripsi lain cantik.
statement.en: Moss people are sometimes like dwarfs, child-sized but grey, old-looking, hairy and moss-clad; sometimes bigger, and in other accounts pretty.

basis_claims.quote: Moss people, especially the females of the species, are able to send plagues on one hand; on the other, they can also heal the victims of such plagues. During epidemics the Holzfräulein ("Wood ladies") would emerge from the forest to show the people which medicinal herbs could cure or ward off plague.

statement.id: Orang lumut, terutama yang perempuan, dapat mendatangkan wabah tetapi juga menyembuhkan korbannya; saat epidemi Holzfräulein keluar dari hutan untuk menunjukkan tanaman obat penyembuh atau penangkal wabah.
statement.en: Moss people, especially females, can send plagues yet also heal their victims; in epidemics the Holzfräulein came out of the forest to show which herbs cure or prevent plague.

basis_claims.quote: Die Moosweiblein leben im Wald. Sie wohnen auf der Heide, an dunklen Orten im Holz oder im tiefsten Wald. Ihre Behausung ist ein Erdloch, ein hohler Baum, ein Häuslein aus Baumwurzeln oder eine Mooshütte. Sie schlafen auf Moos und betten auch ihre Kinder auf Moos oder Rinde.

statement.id: Moosweiblein tinggal di hutan, di padang, di tempat gelap, atau di hutan terdalam; rumahnya rongga tanah, pohon berlubang, pondok dari akar, atau pondok lumut; mereka tidur di atas lumut dan membaringkan anak-anaknya di atas lumut atau kulit kayu.
statement.en: Moosweiblein live in the forest, on heaths, in dark places or the deepest woods; they dwell in earth holes, hollow trees, root huts or moss huts, sleep on moss and bed their children on moss or bark.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; child-sized grey hairy old forest spirit wearing moss garments, associated with trees and healing herbs.
moss-people.historical_basis: Moss people (Moosleute), also wood folk (Holzleute) or forest folk (Waldleute), are a class of fairy-folk compared with dwarfs, elves or spirits, described in German folklore as intimately tied to trees and the forest. Moss people are sometimes like dwarfs, child-sized but grey, old-looking, hairy and moss-clad; sometimes bigger, and in other accounts pretty. Moss people, especially females, can send plagues yet also heal their victims; in epidemics the Holzfräulein came out of the forest to show which herbs cure or prevent plague. Moosweiblein live in the forest, on heaths, in dark places or the deepest woods; they dwell in earth holes, hollow trees, root huts or moss huts, sleep on moss and bed their children on moss or bark.

gandharva.aura: One dignified adult male human-shaped Gandharva celestial musician from Indian traditions, wearing modest draped court garments with traditional crown and a few jewels, seated on a cloud-soft celestial court terrace playing a simple ancient Indian stringed lute. Human face and limbs, normal ears, exactly two hands coherently interacting with lute. Divine music aura conveyed by luminous sky and quiet golden atmosphere, not invented animal anatomy. No horse head, bird wings, bird legs, kinnara hybrid or other deities.

basis_claims.quote: A gandharva (Sanskrit: गन्धर्व) is a member of a class of celestial beings in Indian religions, such as Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism, whose males are divine performers such as musicians and singers, and the females are divine dancers. In Hinduism, they are regarded to be the celestial demigods who serve as the musicians of the devas.

statement.id: Gandharva adalah golongan makhluk surgawi dalam agama India yang berhubungan dengan musik dan tari.
statement.en: Gandharvas are a class of celestial beings in Indian religions associated with music and dance.

basis_claims.quote: In Hinduism, the gandharvas (Sanskrit: गन्धर्व, romanized: gandharva) are a class of minor deities who serve as divine musicians in Hindu mythology.

statement.id: Dalam Hindu mereka merupakan dewa kecil yang menjadi musisi ilahi.
statement.en: In Hinduism they are minor deities serving as divine musicians.

basis_claims.quote: Gandharvas usually live in Svarga and serve at Indra's court, though they also have their own realm, called the Gandharvaloka.

statement.id: Mereka biasanya hidup di Svarga dan melayani istana Indra.
statement.en: They usually live in Svarga and serve Indra's court.

basis_claims.quote:
When they play on their divine instruments the fairy-like
Apsaras, who are all females, dance merrily.

statement.id: Mackenzie menggambarkan musik Gandharva mengiringi tarian apsara.
statement.en: Mackenzie describes Gandharva music accompanying apsara dances.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; celestial musician serving the divine court.
gandharva.historical_basis: Gandharvas are a class of celestial beings in Indian religions associated with music and dance. In Hinduism they are minor deities serving as divine musicians. They usually live in Svarga and serve Indra's court. Mackenzie describes Gandharva music accompanying apsara dances.

Normal human ears, arms and legs, no mermaid tail. Disturbing uncanny presence in bright daylight, eerie still water and ancient woodland stones, no invented horns or bird parts.

basis_claims.quote: In Breton folklore, a Korrigan ( pronounced [kɔˈriːɡãn] ) is a fairy or dwarf-like spirit.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Breton (Breton folklore), Korrigan roh peri atau mirip kerdil; di Prancis.
statement.en: In Breton folklore a Korrigan is a fairy or dwarf-like spirit.

These creatures are very beautiful when seen at dusk or night, but by day their eyes are red, their hair white, and their skin wrinkled

statement.en: Siren-like female fairies of springs and rivers luring men to death; lovely at night, by day red-eyed, white-haired, wrinkled.

basis_claims.quote: They are sometimes described as important princesses or druidesses who were opposed to Christianity when the Apostles came to convert Brittany. They hate priests, churches, and especially the Virgin Mary. They can predict the future, change shape, and move at lightning speed.

statement.id: Putri atau druid perempuan yang menentang Kristen (Christianity) di Brittany (Apostles, Rasul; Virgin Mary); meramal, berubah wujud, cepat seperti kilat; mencuri anak, changeling (Changeling).
statement.en: Princesses or druidesses opposed to Christianity in Brittany; they predict the future, change shape and move at lightning speed.

buckriders.aura: One fully human-shaped adult folklore witch-rider in modest eighteenth-century dark travelling clothes and plain hat, riding ONE ordinary coherent horned male goat through the night sky above distant Limburg countryside and a rural church. Goat flies without wings as in recorded legend: exactly four normal legs and two horns, no hybrids. Rider and goat fully inside image, rider human normal limbs with hands holding simple reins. Ominous nocturnal supernatural flight, no victims, violence or devil character.

basis_claims.quote: The Buckriders (Dutch: Bokkenrijders ; French: Chevaliers du bouc ) are a part of South-Eastern Dutch and North-Eastern Belgian folklore. They are witches, who rode through the sky on the back of flying bucks provided to them by the Devil to rob and murder common people and church possessions. ... Once a year, they would visit their master, the Devil, on the Mook Heath.

statement.id: Bokkenrijders (Prancis: Chevaliers du bouc) adalah bagian dari cerita rakyat Belanda tenggara dan Belgia timur laut: penyihir yang terbang menunggangi kambing jantan pemberian Iblis untuk merampok dan membunuh rakyat serta merampas harta gereja, dan setahun sekali mereka menghadap Iblis di Padang Mook.
statement.en: The Buckriders (Dutch Bokkenrijders, French Chevaliers du bouc) belong to south-eastern Dutch and north-eastern Belgian folklore: witches flying on bucks from the Devil to rob and murder people and church property, who once a year visited the Devil on the Mook Heath.

basis_claims.quote: The belief existed that the buckriders could travel fast and vast distances through the skies to rob in a widespread area and be home before dawn to remain obscured in their crimes.

statement.id: Ada kepercayaan bahwa bokkenrijders dapat menempuh jarak jauh dengan cepat lewat udara untuk merampok di wilayah luas dan pulang sebelum fajar agar kejahatannya tersembunyi.
statement.en: It was believed the buckriders could travel fast and far through the skies to rob over a wide area and be home before dawn, hiding their crimes.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed for rider; supernatural flying goat mount distinguishes this folklore.

fenixmannlein.aura: One small human-shaped Silesian earth sprite, intermediate in size between a dwarf and a human, in modest worn old rural clothing with ordinary rounded ears, taking a cabbage-like baked cake from a stone oven in a hill cave. The warmly lit cavern is cozy yet mysteriously hidden, smoke rises toward a small earth opening overhead. One figure, no invisible duplicate hand. Supernatural secret baker atmosphere; no flames shaped into phoenix wings or invented bird anatomy.

basis_claims.quote: are earth sprites and dwarves from German folklore. They were historically known in Silesia, particularly in the Oderské vrchy and Hrubý Jeseník as well as in the part of Lusatia belonging to Saxony.

statement.id: Fenixmännlein (juga Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel, Fenesleute) adalah roh tanah dan kurcaci dari cerita rakyat Jerman (German), dahulu dikenal di Silesia, terutama Oderské vrchy dan Hrubý Jeseník, serta bagian Lusatia milik Sachsen (Saxony).
statement.en: The Fenixmännlein (also Fenixmännel, Fenskemännel, Fenesleute) are earth sprites and dwarfs of German folklore, once known in Silesia, especially the Oderské vrchy and Hrubý Jeseník, and in the Saxon part of Lusatia.

basis_claims.quote: The latter option is supported by the fact that both Fenixmännlein and Venedigermännlein are supposed to be bigger than dwarves (German Zwerge, sg. Zwerg) but smaller than humans. The Fenixmännlein are collective beings dwelling in hills and shrubbery.

statement.id: Asal nama dari Venedigermännlein ("lelaki kecil dari Venesia") didukung fakta bahwa keduanya lebih besar dari kurcaci tetapi lebih kecil dari manusia; Fenixmännlein hidup berkelompok di bukit dan semak.
statement.en: Derivation from the Venedigermännlein ('little Venetian men') is supported since both are bigger than dwarfs but smaller than humans; the Fenixmännlein live collectively in hills and shrubbery.

basis_claims.quote: Inside the mountains, they throw big parties. The Fenismannla (pl. Mannla = little men in Silesian German) are said to be the original owners of the recipe for Silesian streuselkuchen. When the Fänismännchen (sg., pl.;Männchen = little man) are baking cake in their caves, smoke is rising from earth holes and from beneath clods.

statement.id: Di dalam gunung mereka berpesta besar; mereka konon pemilik asli resep kue streusel Silesia (Silesian streuselkuchen), dan saat mereka memanggang di gua, asap naik dari lubang tanah.
statement.en: Inside the mountains they hold big parties; they are said to own the original Silesian streuselkuchen recipe, and when they bake in their caves smoke rises from earth holes.

basis_claims.quote: Immediately, an invisible hand gave him a Krautkuchen (cabbage cake) coated with green linseed oil. At the same time, he got threatened to eat this cake on a table made from iron or else he would be done for. The ploughboy fulfilled the condition by using his ploughshare as the iron table.

statement.id: Seorang pembajak yang meminta kue segera diberi kue kubis berlapis minyak biji rami oleh tangan tak terlihat, dengan ancaman harus memakannya di atas meja besi; ia memakai mata bajaknya sebagai meja besi.
statement.en: A ploughboy who asked for cake was at once handed a cabbage cake with linseed oil by an invisible hand, threatened to eat it on an iron table; he used his ploughshare as that table.

turst.aura: One dreadful but human-shaped Swiss spectral huntsman Türst, selecting Rickenbach GREEN hunting dress. Adult stern man in green coat and old hat sounding a curved hunting horn with one normal hand; other hand relaxed. Stormy Lucerne farm landscape in winter before Epiphany, open barn doorway behind and windblown clouds. No dogs pictured; distinctive three-legged or hybrid anatomy belongs to accompanying pack, not Türst, and MUST NOT be put on him. Ominous supernatural Wild Hunt atmosphere, normal ears and two human legs.

basis_claims.quote: is a legendary folkloric figure from the agricultural communities of Lucerne, dating to the pre-Christian era. He is described as a "dreadful huntsman", of whom people should be wary in stormy weather. Türst blows his hunting horn through villages in the tempestuous months preceding Epiphany, accompanied by a baying pack of three-legged hunting dogs.

statement.id: Türst adalah tokoh cerita rakyat dari komunitas petani Luzern yang berasal dari masa pra-Kristen, digambarkan sebagai "pemburu mengerikan" yang harus diwaspadai saat cuaca berbadai; ia meniup terompet berburu menembus desa-desa pada bulan-bulan berbadai menjelang Epifani bersama kawanan anjing berkaki tiga.
statement.en: Türst is a folk figure of Lucerne's farming communities dating to pre-Christian times, a 'dreadful huntsman' to beware of in stormy weather, who blows his horn through villages in the stormy months before Epiphany with a pack of three-legged hounds.

basis_claims.quote: He appears in a green hunting costume in Rickenbach, accompanied by a pack of animals which are half dog and half pig. In Wolhusen, to avoid Türst, the citizens erected crosses. If a cross were to fall, the farmers would have bad luck until the cross stood straight again. The local people of Pilatus say that Türst is a ghost and a "dreadful huntsman"

statement.id: Di Rickenbach ia tampil berpakaian berburu hijau dengan kawanan setengah anjing setengah babi; di Wolhusen warga mendirikan salib untuk menghindarinya, dan bila salib roboh petani akan sial sampai salib ditegakkan; warga Pilatus menyebutnya hantu dan "pemburu mengerikan".
statement.en: In Rickenbach he appears in green hunting dress with a half-dog, half-pig pack; in Wolhusen people raised crosses against him, and a fallen cross brought farmers bad luck until set upright; the people of Pilatus call him a ghost and a 'dreadful huntsman'.

basis_claims.quote: Der Türst (auch Dürst genannt) ist eine Sagenfigur aus dem Luzerner Hinterland, die noch aus heidnischen Zeiten stammt. Er wird als „höllischer Jäger“ bezeichnet

statement.id: Türst (juga disebut Dürst) adalah tokoh legenda dari pedalaman Luzern yang berasal dari masa kafir dan disebut "pemburu neraka".
statement.en: Türst (also called Dürst) is a legendary figure from the Lucerne hinterland dating from heathen times, called the 'hellish huntsman'.

basis_claims.quote: It is also said that barn doors should stay open at this time, enabling Türst to hunt through the barn unhindered. Sträggele, his wife, appears in some Türst legends. Other legends say that Türst terrifies dairy cows, causing them to sicken and cease their milk production.

statement.id: Konon pintu lumbung harus dibiarkan terbuka pada masa itu agar Türst dapat berburu menembus lumbung tanpa halangan; istrinya Sträggele muncul dalam sebagian legenda, dan legenda lain menyebut ia menakuti sapi perah hingga sakit dan berhenti menghasilkan susu.
statement.en: Barn doors should be left open at this time so Türst can hunt through unhindered; his wife Sträggele appears in some legends, and others say he terrifies dairy cows until they sicken and stop giving milk.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; green-clad dreadful huntsman blowing horn in storm, a supernatural hunt leader.

basis_claims.quote: "he who drinks in might"), also found as Móðsognir ([ˈmoːðˌsoɣnez̠] ; Hauksbók manuscript variant), "he who drinks in courage", is the ruler of the dwarves. In Völuspà 10, he is identified as mæztr um orðinn dverga allra, "lord of all the dwarves".

basis_claims.quote: "the dwarfs had taken shape first and acquired life in the flesh of Ymir and were then maggots, but by decision of the gods they became conscious with intelligence and had the shape of men though they live in the earth and in rocks. statement.id: Menurut Snorri dalam Gylfaginning 14, para kurcaci mula-mula terbentuk dan hidup di daging Ymir sebagai belatung, lalu atas keputusan para dewa memperoleh kesadaran, akal, dan rupa manusia walau tinggal di tanah dan bebatuan; Modsognir kurcaci pertama dan Durinn yang kedua.
statement.en: Per Snorri in Gylfaginning 14, the dwarfs first took shape and life in Ymir's flesh as maggots, then by the gods' decision gained awareness, intelligence and human shape though living in earth and rocks; Modsognir was a dwarf and the second was Durinn.

basis_claims.quote: According to Völuspà 9, the dwarfs were created by ginnheilög goð, "the high holy gods", who resolved to fashion them "out of Brimir's blood and Blainn's bones," a phrase typically interpreted to mean the blood and flesh of the primordial giant, Ymir.

statement.id: Menurut Völuspá 9, para kurcaci diciptakan "dewa-dewa yang mahasuci" yang memutuskan membentuk mereka "dari darah Brimir dan tulang Blainn", ungkapan yang biasa ditafsirkan sebagai darah dan daging raksasa purba Ymir.
statement.en: According to Völuspá 9, the dwarfs were made by 'the high holy gods', who resolved to shape them 'out of Brimir's blood and Blainn's bones', usually read as the blood and flesh of the primordial giant Ymir.

erlking.aura: One sinister human-shaped elderly forest elf-king from Goethe's literary Erlkönig, long beard and simple crown atop white hair, wearing a modest long archaic cloak, reaching one ordinary hand from among dark alder trunks. Ordinary rounded human ears, no tree-bark body, antlers, wings or animal anatomy. A literary supernatural king portrait rather than a literal alder-tree hybrid.

basis_claims.quote: In European folklore and myth, the Erlking is a sinister elf who lingers in the woods. He stalks children who stay in the woods for too long and kills them with a single touch.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat dan mitos Eropa, Erlking adalah elf jahat yang berdiam di hutan, mengintai anak-anak yang terlalu lama di hutan, dan membunuh mereka dengan sekali sentuh.
statement.en: In European folklore and myth the Erlking is a sinister elf lingering in the woods, stalking children who stay too long and killing them with a single touch.

basis_claims.quote: is a name used in German Romanticism for the figure of a spirit or "king of the fairies". It is usually assumed that the name is a derivation from the ellekonge (older elverkonge, i.e. "Elf-king") in Danish folklore.

statement.id: Nama Erlking (Erlkönig, "raja pohon alder") dipakai dalam Romantisisme Jerman untuk roh atau "raja para peri" dan umumnya dianggap turunan dari ellekonge (lebih tua: elverkonge, "raja elf") dalam cerita rakyat Denmark.
statement.en: The name Erlking (Erlkönig, 'alder-king') was used in German Romanticism for a spirit or 'king of the fairies' and is usually thought to derive from Danish folklore's ellekonge (older elverkonge, 'elf-king').

basis_claims.quote: The name was first used by Johann Gottfried Herder in his ballad Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), an adaptation of the Danish folk ballad Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), and was taken up by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe in his poem Erlkönig (1782), which was set to music by Schubert and others. Goethe added a new meaning, as "Erl" means not "elf" but "black alder"

statement.id: Nama ini pertama dipakai Johann Gottfried Herder dalam balada Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), saduran balada rakyat Denmark Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), lalu diambil Goethe dalam puisi Erlkönig (1782) yang digubah Schubert dan lainnya; Goethe menambah makna baru karena "Erl" berarti "alder hitam", bukan "elf".
statement.en: The name was first used by Johann Gottfried Herder in Erlkönigs Tochter (1778), adapted from the Danish ballad Hr. Oluf han rider (1739), then taken up by Goethe in Erlkönig (1782), set by Schubert and others; Goethe added a new sense, 'Erl' meaning 'black alder', not 'elf'.

basis_claims.quote: is a mischievous fairy in Irish folklore known for his great love of drinking and a tendency to haunt breweries, pubs and wine cellars. statement.en: The clurichaun (clúrachán, Irish clobhair-ceann) is a mischievous fairy of Irish folklore who loves drink and haunts cellars; related to the leprechaun.

statement.id: Ameonna berarti perempuan hujan dan Sekien menggambarkannya di tengah hujan.
statement.en: Ameonna means rain woman and Sekien depicts her in rain.

basis_claims.quote: You’ll find her first in Toriyama Sekien’s book, Konjaku Hyakki Shūi, supplement to the 100 demons from the present and past. In it is a black and white depiction of a rain-soaked woman, very creepily licking her hand.

statement.id: Gambar Sekien menunjukkan perempuan basah yang menjilat tangannya.
statement.en: Sekien pictures a rain-soaked woman licking her hand.

basis_claims.quote: It is said that the divine woman of Mount Wu in ancient China becomes a cloud in the morning and rain in the evening. I wonder if Ame-onna is also this kind of being.

statement.id: Keterangan Sekien membandingkan ameonna dengan perempuan ilahi Gunung Wu.
statement.en: Sekien compares ameonna with the divine woman of Mount Wu.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; supernatural rain woman performing documented hand-licking gesture.
ameonna.historical_basis: Ameonna means rain woman and Sekien depicts her in rain. Sekien pictures a rain-soaked woman licking her hand. Sekien compares ameonna with the divine woman of Mount Wu.
artistic_changes: Exact facial likeness, clothing folds, compositional details and painterly lighting are illustrative; no anatomical deformation asserted beyond selected documented account.

oshiroibaba.aura: One bent-backed elderly female Japanese yokai of Totsukawa, combining documented old-woman appearance and recorded visual accessories: heavy messy WHITE FACE POWDER with wrinkles still visible, modest old kimono, one hand supporting a worn paper umbrella, other hand with a walking cane, sake flask tied at waist. A small old mirror is tied to a loose trailing cord dragging behind her on the village lane, visibly separate from her anatomy. Entire figure and mirror inside image. Uncanny solitary nighttime village atmosphere, no floating head, extra limbs, horns or deformed face invented.

basis_claims.quote: is a yōkai old woman from the Totsukawa river in Yoshino District, Nara Prefecture.

statement.id: Oshiroibabā adalah yōkai perempuan tua dari daerah Totsukawa di Nara.
statement.en: Oshiroibabā is an old-woman yōkai from the Totsukawa area of Nara.

basis_claims.quote: The oshiroibabā is said to be a yōkai in the form of an old woman who appears while dragging a mirror and making a jingling sound.

statement.id: Ia menyeret cermin dengan suara gemerincing.
statement.en: She drags a mirror with a jingling sound.

basis_claims.quote: Toriyama Sekien's Konjaku Hyakki Shūi depicts an old woman with a very bent back, wearing a large broken umbrella on her head, holding a walking stick with her right hand and a tokkuri (flask for sake) in her left hand, under the name of oshiroibabā.

statement.id: Sekien menggambarkannya membungkuk dengan payung, tongkat, dan botol sake.
statement.en: Sekien depicts her bent-backed with an umbrella, cane and sake flask.

basis_claims.quote: Their most defining feature is their wrinkly old face caked with thick, sloppy, white face powder.

statement.id: Uraian belakangan menekankan riasan putih tebal yang berantakan.
statement.en: A later description emphasizes thick, messy white makeup.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; old-woman yokai with thick messy white makeup and jingling dragged mirror.
oshiroibaba.historical_basis: Oshiroibabā is an old-woman yōkai from the Totsukawa area of Nara. She drags a mirror with a jingling sound. Sekien depicts her bent-backed with an umbrella, cane and sake flask. A later description emphasizes thick, messy white makeup.

far-darrig.aura: One short approximately two-and-a-half-foot elderly Irish fairy in RED cap and RED coat, deeply wrinkled but human face, sitting alone beside the best place at a rural hearth with a sly unsettling expression and one ordinary hand held toward warmth. Tiny scale indicated by large hearth stones and normal-size empty wooden chair. Ordinary rounded human ears and human limbs. Nickname Rat Boys is NOT anatomical evidence: no rat snout, furred paws or tail. Quiet eerie prankster mood, no changeling infant or gore.

basis_claims.quote: A far darrig or fear dearg is a faerie type in Irish mythology. The name far darrig is an Anglophone pronunciation of the Irish words fear dearg, meaning Red Man, as the far darrig is said to wear a red coat and cap. They are sometimes known as Rat Boys as they are said to be rather fat, have dark, hairy skin, long snouts and skinny tails.

statement.id: Far darrig (fear dearg) peri mitologi Irlandia (Irish), Lelaki Merah (Red Man), bermantel dan bertopi merah; juga Rat Boys; di Irlandia. Pelafalan Anglophone.
statement.en: The far darrig (fear dearg) is an Irish fairy, Red Man, in a red coat and cap; also called Rat Boys.

basis_claims.quote: The far derrig is generally described as short, while sometimes described as tall. It's said the far derrig has the ability to change sizes. An 1832 description from T. Crofton Croaker in Munster says the far derrig are around 2.5 feet tall with a wrinkled face, long grey hair, and a sugarloaf hat.

statement.id: Pendek atau tinggi, dapat mengubah ukuran; T. Crofton Croker (Croaker), Munster, 1832: tinggi sekitar 2,5 kaki, wajah keriput.
statement.en: Short or tall, can change size; T. Crofton Croker, Munster, 1832: about 2.5 feet, wrinkled face.

basis_claims.quote: The Far Darrig (fear dearg), which means the Red Man, for he wears a red cap and coat, busies himself with practical joking, especially with gruesome joking.

statement.id: Yeats: Far Darrig (fear dearg), Red Man, bertopi dan bermantel merah, sibuk dengan lelucon keji; W. B. Yeats.
statement.en: Yeats: the Far Darrig (fear dearg), Red Man, in red cap and coat, busies himself with gruesome practical joking.

basis_claims.quote: On dit de lui qu'il a tendance à forcer les habitants d'une maison à l'accueillir chez eux, et à lui réserver la meilleure place, au coin du feu.

statement.id: Ia memaksa penghuni rumah menerimanya dan memberinya tempat terbaik dekat perapian (coin du feu).
statement.en: He forces householders to take him in and give him the best place by the fire (coin du feu).

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; size-changing solitary fairy represented in short red-clad form.
far-darrig.historical_basis: The far darrig (fear dearg) is an Irish fairy, Red Man, in a red coat and cap; also called Rat Boys. Short or tall, can change size; T. Crofton Croker, Munster, 1832: about 2.5 feet, wrinkled face. Yeats: the Far Darrig (fear dearg), Red Man, in red cap and coat, busies himself with gruesome practical joking. He forces householders to take him in and give him the best place by the fire (coin du feu).

hodekin.aura: One small human-shaped German castle house spirit Hödekin, an old sober-faced male in humble archaic clothes and a LITTLE FELT PILEUS CAP, sitting silently at the threshold of a bishop's medieval stone castle kitchen at night. Normal human face, rounded ears and human limbs, both hands visible. The tiny felt hat identifies him; eerie watchful house-spirit aura conveyed by empty kitchen, dim hearth and long shadow. No violent scene, blood, toads, horns or animal anatomy.

basis_claims.quote: Hödekin (variously spelled Hödeken, Hütgin, Hüdekin , and Hütchen , etc.) is a kobold (house spirit) of German folklore. The name, a diminutive meaning "Little Hat", refers to the pileus hat he wears

statement.id: Hödekin (juga Hödeken, Hütgin, Hüdekin, dan Hütchen) adalah kobold (roh rumah) dalam cerita rakyat Jerman; namanya bentuk kecil yang berarti "Topi Kecil", merujuk topi pileus yang dikenakannya.
statement.en: Hödekin (also Hödeken, Hütgin, Hüdekin and Hütchen) is a kobold (house spirit) of German folklore; the name, a diminutive meaning 'Little Hat', refers to the pileus cap he wears.

basis_claims.quote: Hödekin is known for haunting the castle of Bishop Bernard (Bernhardus), Prince-Bishopric of Hildesheim, located in Lower Saxony. In some versions of the legend, the spirit inhabits Winzenburg, a county which he helped the bishopric obtain.

statement.id: Hödekin dikenal menghantui kastel Uskup Bernhard (Bernhardus) dari Keuskupan-Pangeran Hildesheim di Niedersachsen; dalam sebagian versi ia menghuni Winzenburg, wilayah yang dibantunya diperoleh keuskupan.
statement.en: Hödekin is known for haunting the castle of Bishop Bernard (Bernhardus) of the Prince-Bishopric of Hildesheim in Lower Saxony; in some versions he inhabits Winzenburg, a county he helped the bishopric obtain.

basis_claims.quote: Der Hödeken ist der Burggeist der Winzenburg. Er wird als eine zwergenartige Gestalt beschrieben (Kobold), die auch als Bote zwischen Hildesheim und Winzenburg Nachrichten übermittelte. Der Weg zwischen Winzenburg und Hildesheimer Domhof, den Hödeken nach dem Tod des letzten Grafen von Winzenburg entlanggeeilt sein soll, um die Todesnachricht zu überbringen, wird „Rennstieg“ genannt.

statement.id: Hödeken adalah roh kastel Winzenburg, sosok mirip kurcaci (kobold) yang juga menjadi pembawa pesan antara Hildesheim dan Winzenburg; jalan antara Winzenburg dan Domhof Hildesheim yang konon dilaluinya untuk mengabarkan kematian Graf Winzenburg terakhir disebut "Rennstieg".
statement.en: Hödeken is the castle spirit of Winzenburg, a dwarf-like figure (kobold) who also carried messages between Hildesheim and Winzenburg; the road between Winzenburg and Hildesheim's Domhof that he reputedly ran to report the last count of Winzenburg's death is called the 'Rennstieg'.

basis_claims.quote: Der Hödeken war ein Geist, der sich am Hof des Bischofs von Hildesheim aufhielt. Er hinderte die Nachtwachen am Einschlafen, gab dem Bischof militärische Ratschläge und warnte ihn vor kommenden Gefahren. Gelegentlich half er auch anderen Hildesheimern. Einmal bat jemand den Hödeken, seine Frau während seiner Abwesenheit zu beschützen.

statement.id: Menurut Grimm bersaudara, Hödeken adalah roh di istana Uskup Hildesheim yang mencegah penjaga malam tertidur, memberi uskup nasihat perang, memperingatkannya akan bahaya, kadang menolong warga Hildesheim lain, dan pernah diminta menjaga istri seseorang selama suaminya pergi.
statement.en: Per the Brothers Grimm, Hödeken was a spirit at the court of the Bishop of Hildesheim who kept the night watch awake, gave the bishop military advice, warned him of dangers, sometimes helped other townsfolk, and was once asked to guard a man's wife in his absence.

basis_claims.quote: „[…] auf dem Haupt trug er einen kleinen Filzhut, wovon man ihm den Namen Hütchen auf Niedersächsisch Hödeken gegeben hatte.“

statement.id: Menurut Grimm bersaudara, ia memakai topi laken kecil di kepalanya, sehingga diberi nama Hütchen, dalam bahasa Saxon Rendah Hödeken.
statement.en: Per the Grimms, he wore a little felt hat, whence the name Hütchen, in Low Saxon Hödeken.

nonhuman_features: No anatomical deformation claimed; dwarf-like house spirit wearing the defining little felt hat.
hodekin.historical_basis: Hödekin (also Hödeken, Hütgin, Hüdekin and Hütchen) is a kobold (house spirit) of German folklore; the name, a diminutive meaning 'Little Hat', refers to the pileus cap he wears. Hödekin is known for haunting the castle of Bishop Bernard (Bernhardus) of the Prince-Bishopric of Hildesheim in Lower Saxony; in some versions he inhabits Winzenburg, a county he helped the bishopric obtain. Hödeken is the castle spirit of Winzenburg, a dwarf-like figure (kobold) who also carried messages between Hildesheim and Winzenburg; the road between Winzenburg and Hildesheim's Domhof that he reputedly ran to report the last count of Winzenburg's death is called the 'Rennstieg'. Per the Brothers Grimm, Hödeken was a spirit at the court of the Bishop of Hildesheim who kept the night watch awake, gave the bishop military advice, warned him of dangers, sometimes helped other townsfolk, and was once asked to guard a man's wife in his absence. Per the Grimms, he wore a little felt hat, whence the name Hütchen, in Low Saxon Hödeken.

knights-of-alleberg.depicted_variant: One representative sleeping armored Ålleberg ghost knight
visual_requirements: One representative sleeping armored Ålleberg ghost knight
