statement.en: The singa is often shown as a head alone, sometimes full body; other figures such as protective deities or ancestral figures may be shown standing or sitting on its head.

basis_claims.quote: Gorga ulu singa ("singa's gorga") represents the spiritual being singa of Batak mythology is placed on top of the front gable of a Batak house.
basis_claims.locator: Lead (gorga motifs of a Batak house)

statement.id: Gorga ulu singa ("gorga singa") menggambarkan makhluk rohani singa dari mitologi Batak dan dipasang di puncak gable depan rumah Batak.
statement.en: The gorga ulu singa ("singa's gorga") represents the spiritual being singa of Batak mythology and is placed on top of the front gable of a Batak house.

basis_claims.quote: Naga/singa heads are carved on the front gable as well as curvilinear designs in ochre, black and white.

statement.id: Kepala naga/singa diukir pada gable depan, bersama rancangan lengkung berwarna oker, hitam, dan putih.
statement.en: Naga/singa heads are carved on the front gable, together with curvilinear designs in ochre, black and white.

nawarupa.depicted_variant: Living c02 Nawarupa with elephant head, deer eyes, rhino horn, parrot tongue/wings, lion body/legs and peafowl tail.

visual_requirements.description: A LIVING BURMESE NAWARUPA in the c02 ELEPHANT/DEER/RHINO/PARROT/LION/PEAFOWL listed-feature variant only. One ELEPHANT HEAD with trunk and normal elephant ears, gentle DEER EYES, one RHINOCEROS-style nasal HORN, physical PARROT TONGUE glimpsed at mouth plus TWO PARROT FEATHERED WINGS, powerful LION BODY with FOUR lion LEGS/PAWS, and a long graceful PEAFOWL FEATHER TAIL (c02). Each documented feature individually visible, one coherent chimeric animal not multiple fused heads. Peaceful welcoming facial expression (c08,c10). Stands beside a Myanmar pagoda grove c09 in natural early sunlight, flesh/fur/scales/feathers alive, full body readable. NO bull hump, fish tail or horse legs borrowed from differing royal-barge c07 variant; no boat, statue, metal plating, extra limbs, laser or halo.

nawarupa.aura: Living c02 Nawarupa with elephant head, deer eyes, rhino horn, parrot tongue/wings, lion body/legs and peafowl tail.

basis_claims.quote: Nawarupa (Burmese: နဝရူပ, also spelt Nawa Rupa; Pali: navarūpa, Sanskrit: नवरूप, lit. 'nine forms'), also known as Byala (Rakhine: ဗျာလ, ဗျာလ္လ), is a chimeric creature found in Burmese and Rakhine (Arakanese) mythology.

statement.id: Nawarupa (နဝရူပ, juga Nawa Rupa; Pali navarūpa, 'sembilan wujud'), juga disebut Byala, adalah makhluk campuran dalam mitologi Myanmar dan Rakhine (Arakan).
statement.en: The nawarupa (နဝရူပ, also Nawa Rupa; Pali navarūpa, 'nine forms'), also called byala, is a chimeric creature of Burmese and Rakhine (Arakanese) mythology.

basis_claims.quote: The beast is made of 9 animals, possessing the head of an elephant, the eyes of a deer, the horns of a rhinoceros, the tongue and wings of a parrot, the body and legs of a lion, and the tail of a peafowl.

statement.id: Makhluk ini tersusun dari 9 hewan: kepala gajah, mata rusa, tanduk badak, lidah dan sayap burung nuri, tubuh dan kaki singa, serta ekor merak.
statement.en: The beast is made of 9 animals: an elephant's head, deer's eyes, rhinoceros horns, a parrot's tongue and wings, a lion's body and legs, and a peafowl's tail.

basis_claims.quote: Byala -The mythological animal of the Rakhuies- having four legs, smiling face, beautiful girdle of hair around the neck, and a beautiful tail is considered as a symbol of peace and prosperity.

statement.id: Byala, hewan mitologi orang Rakhine, digambarkan berkaki empat, berwajah tersenyum, dengan lingkaran rambut yang indah di leher dan ekor yang indah, serta dianggap sebagai lambang perdamaian dan kemakmuran.
statement.en: The byala, the mythological animal of the Rakhine, is described as having four legs, a smiling face, a beautiful girdle of hair around the neck and a beautiful tail, and is considered a symbol of peace and prosperity.

basis_claims.quote: The onlookers always derive pleasure from the ever-smiling looks of the animal. As an auspicious symbol the figure of byala can be found erected near the pagodas.

statement.id: Para penonton selalu senang melihat wajah hewan itu yang senantiasa tersenyum; sebagai lambang pertanda baik, patung byala dapat ditemukan didirikan di dekat pagoda.
statement.en: Onlookers always take pleasure in the ever-smiling looks of the animal; as an auspicious symbol, the figure of the byala can be found erected near the pagodas.

basis_claims.quote: Byala is a creature of peace always wearing a smiling face.

statement.id: Byala digambarkan sebagai makhluk perdamaian yang selalu berwajah tersenyum.
statement.en: The Byala is described as a creature of peace always wearing a smiling face.

duende.depicted_variant: Small Iberian humanlike house duende guarding a dark wall cavity and hidden coins.

visual_requirements.description: An IBERIAN DUENDE, small HUMANLIKE DWARF/GNOME house spirit (c01,c02,c14), one elderly-looking little figure with one head two arms two legs, natural human ears and face, mischievous sharp watchful expression. NO pointy ears, animal limbs or wings. Stands by a partly open old household wall cavity above a few small coins alluding to hidden underground treasure c12; towering ordinary floorboards, wooden stool and doorway establish dwarf stature without invented giant body. Modest rustic historic cloth tunic and trousers, grey beard and cap are explicitly editorial choices, not claimed fixed anatomy. Crouching half-step and tense direct gaze make eerie goblin presence, natural warm oil-lamp light against cold dark wall, no glow, curse beams or magical mist. Single living spirit, not Goya satire reproduction, toy or ordinary child.

duende.aura: Small Iberian humanlike house duende guarding a dark wall cavity and hidden coins.

basis_claims.quote: The Duende is a humanoid figure of folklore, with variations from Iberian, Ibero American, and Latin American cultures, comparable to dwarves, gnomes, or leprechauns.

statement.id: Duende adalah sosok mirip manusia dalam cerita rakyat Iberia, Ibero-Amerika, dan Amerika Latin, sebanding dengan kurcaci, gnome, atau leprechaun.
statement.en: The duende is a humanlike folklore figure from Iberian, Ibero-American and Latin American cultures, comparable to dwarves, gnomes or leprechauns.

basis_claims.quote: In Castilian, duende originated as a contraction of the phrase dueñ(o) de casa, effectively "master of the house"

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Kastilia, duende berasal dari singkatan dueñ(o) de casa, 'tuan rumah'.
statement.en: In Castilian, duende comes from a contraction of dueñ(o) de casa, 'master of the house'.

basis_claims.quote: In the 1600s, duendes (hobgoblins) were thought to be spirits that fell with Lucifer from heaven. Instead of going to hell, they lived in the world, where they frightened and tricked people and amassed untold treasures that they hid in underground lairs.

statement.id: Pada tahun 1600-an, duende dianggap roh yang jatuh bersama Lucifer dari surga; alih-alih ke neraka, mereka hidup di dunia, menakut-nakuti dan menipu orang, serta menimbun harta tak terhitung di sarang bawah tanah.
statement.en: In the 1600s, duendes (hobgoblins) were thought to be spirits that fell with Lucifer from heaven; instead of going to hell they lived in the world, frightening and tricking people and amassing untold treasures hidden in underground lairs.

basis_claims.quote: The word duende refers to a spirit in Spanish, Portuguese, and Filipino folklore and literally means "ghost" or "goblin" in Spanish. It is believed to derive from the phrase dueño de casa, which means "owner of a house."

statement.id: Kata duende merujuk pada roh dalam cerita rakyat Spanyol, Portugis, dan Filipina, dan dalam bahasa Spanyol secara harfiah berarti 'hantu' atau 'goblin'; diyakini berasal dari frasa dueño de casa, 'pemilik rumah'.
statement.en: The word duende refers to a spirit in Spanish, Portuguese and Filipino folklore and literally means 'ghost' or 'goblin' in Spanish; it is believed to derive from the phrase dueño de casa, 'owner of a house'.

pyinsarupa.depicted_variant: Living five-part catalog Pyinsarupa: elephant trunk, buffalo body, horse legs/ears, white carp tail/scales and goose wings.

visual_requirements.description: A LIVING BURMESE PYINSARUPA using the specific museum-catalog c05 FIVE-PART variant: ELEPHANT TRUNK at one head, BULL/WATER-BUFFALO BODY, exactly FOUR HORSE LEGS with hooves and HORSE EARS, WHITE CARP/FISH TAIL and pearly white CARP SCALES along rear body, TWO feathered HAMSA GOOSE WINGS at shoulders (c05). Natural coherent hybrid anatomy in broad side-three-quarter stance. Elephant trunk is not an extra leg; fish tail clear behind body, feather wings distinct from fish fins. NO added horns or antlers, lion mane or serpent body from conflicting zodiac/barge variants c08,c10. Alive with muscle, fine white scales, fur and feather texture rather than gilded instrument, ornamental boat or statue. Powerful noble alert stance beside riverbank in Myanmar, warm natural light, no emitted magical effects or ordinary elephant silhouette.

pyinsarupa.aura: Living five-part catalog Pyinsarupa: elephant trunk, buffalo body, horse legs/ears, white carp tail/scales and goose wings.

basis_claims.quote: Pyinsarupa (Burmese: ပဉ္စရူပ, [pjɪ̀ɴsa̰ jùpa̰], also spelt pyinsa rupa; Pali: pañcarūpa

statement.id: Pyinsarupa (ပဉ္စရူပ, juga pyinsa rupa; Pali pañcarūpa, 'lima wujud'), juga dikenal sebagai phaya luang (bahasa Thai), adalah hewan campuran dalam mitologi Myanmar.
statement.en: The pyinsarupa (ပဉ္စရူပ, also pyinsa rupa; Pali pañcarūpa, 'five forms'), also known in Thai as phaya luang, is a chimeric animal of Burmese mythology.

basis_claims.quote: The ‘Pyinsarupa’ is a chimeric animal from Burmese mythology, meaning an amalgamation of the physical characteristics of five different animals, symbolizing a combination of land, water, and winged creatures.

statement.id: Pyinsarupa adalah hewan campuran dari mitologi Myanmar yang menggabungkan ciri fisik lima hewan berbeda, melambangkan gabungan makhluk darat, air, dan bersayap.
statement.en: The pyinsarupa is a chimeric animal of Burmese mythology that combines physical features of five different animals, symbolizing a combination of land, water and winged creatures.

basis_claims.quote: The components of this ‘Pyinsarupa’ consist of the Elephant (trunk); Bullock/Water Buffalo (body); Horse (legs and ears); White Carp/Nga Gyin Fish (tail and scales); and Hamsa (wings).

statement.id: Menurut katalog koleksi ini, komponen pyinsarupa adalah gajah (belalai), sapi jantan atau kerbau (badan), kuda (kaki dan telinga), ikan karper putih atau nga gyin (ekor dan sisik), dan hamsa (sayap).
statement.en: According to this collection catalog, the pyinsarupa's components are the elephant (trunk), bullock or water buffalo (body), horse (legs and ears), white carp or nga gyin fish (tail and scales) and hamsa (wings).

red-boy.depicted_variant: Pre-subjugation young demon Red Boy in Journey to the West.

visual_requirements.description: Youthful fierce human-shaped boy, ONE head TWO arms TWO bare feet; embroidered war skirt c09 and modest sleeveless plain cloth top editorial for catalogue coverage, NO armor, bull horns, red skin or adult physique. Holds EXTRA LONG fire-tipped spear c09, diagonal full shaft eighteen chi indicated by being several body lengths; dynamic defiant stance before Mount Hao Fire Cloud Cave c10. Samadhi true fire billows in RED CLOUD c06 behind spear, localized but fierce, surviving natural rain c11, no hair made of fire. Pre-subjugation hair style editorial, do not mix later shaved three-tufts or golden restraint.

red-boy.aura: Samadhi fire and red fire cloud directly supported c05,c06,c11; no generic glow.

basis_claims.quote: Red Boy (紅孩兒) is the ferocious son of the Bull Demon King and Princess Iron Fan (a Rakshasa).
basis_claims.locator: Bagian "Life as Red Boy in Journey to the West"

statement.id: Red Boy (紅孩兒) adalah putra Bull Demon King dan Princess Iron Fan (seorang Rakshasa) yang digambarkan garang.
statement.en: Red Boy (紅孩兒) is the ferocious son of the Bull Demon King and Princess Iron Fan (a Rakshasa).

basis_claims.quote: 他曾在火燄山修行了三百年，煉成三昧真火，卻也神通廣大，牛魔王使他來鎮守號山。

statement.id: Dalam novel, dikatakan bahwa Red Boy berlatih tiga ratus tahun di Flaming Mountain (火燄山), menguasai sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火), berkesaktian besar, dan diutus Bull Demon King (牛魔王) menjaga Gunung Hao (號山).
statement.en: In the novel it is said that Red Boy trained for three hundred years on the Flaming Mountain (火燄山), mastered sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火), has great powers, and was sent by Bull Demon King (牛魔王) to guard Mount Hao (號山).

basis_claims.quote: 師徒們正當悚懼，又只見那山凹裡有一朵紅雲，直冒到九霄空內，結聚了一團火氣。

statement.id: Dalam novel, saat para peziarah melewati gunung itu, awan merah naik dari lembah hingga ke langit dan menggumpal menjadi hawa api.
statement.en: In the novel, as the travelers cross the mountain, a red cloud rises from the hollow into the sky and gathers into a mass of fire.

basis_claims.quote: 有那一夥管兵器的小妖，著兩個擡出一桿丈八長的火尖槍，遞與妖王。妖王掄槍拽步，也無甚麼盔甲，只是腰間束一條錦繡戰裙，赤著腳，走出門前。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Red Boy keluar bertarung membawa tombak ujung api (火尖槍) sepanjang satu zhang delapan chi, tanpa baju zirah, hanya mengenakan rok perang bersulam dan bertelanjang kaki.
statement.en: In the novel, Red Boy comes out to fight with a fire-tipped spear (火尖槍) eighteen chi long, wearing no armor, only an embroidered war skirt, and barefoot.

basis_claims.quote: 將近行到門前，見有一座石碣，上鐫八個大字，乃是「號山枯松澗火雲洞」。

statement.id: Dalam novel, gua tempat tinggal Red Boy berada di Gunung Hao (號山), di Lembah Pinus Kering (枯松澗), dan bernama Huoyun Dong (火雲洞).
statement.en: In the novel, Red Boy's cave lies on Mount Hao (號山), at the Withered Pine Ravine (枯松澗), and is named Huoyun Dong (火雲洞).

basis_claims.quote: 原來龍王私雨，只好潑得凡火，妖精的三昧真火如何潑得？好一似火上澆油，越潑越灼。

statement.id: Dalam novel, hujan yang dikirim Dragon King (龍王) hanya bisa memadamkan api biasa, bukan sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火) milik siluman itu; hujan justru membuat api makin membara.
statement.en: In the novel, the rain sent by the Dragon King (龍王) can only put out ordinary fire, not the demon's sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火); it only makes the fire burn the fiercer.

six-eared-macaque.depicted_variant: True form Six-Eared Macaque, distinct from impersonation variant.

visual_requirements.description: ONE living MACAQUE spiritual monkey in TRUE FORM, one head two arms two legs one tail. Show EXACT SIX EARS, three distinct natural macaque ears stacked vertically on EACH side of head, unobscured, not horns. Face alert sideways listening, brown fur, modest plain ancient Chinese travel tunic editorial. No Wukong golden circlet or modern purple black armored design. Poised crouch high ridge above small distant settlements, listens across vast country c11. No staff required for true form; no sound neon beams, wings or extra heads.

six-eared-macaque.aura: Distant-listening aura through attentive posture and vast landscape c10c11, no invented visible energy.

basis_claims.quote: The Six-Eared Macaque (Chinese: 六耳獼猴; pinyin: Liù'ěr míhóu)

statement.id: Nama Tionghoa Six-Eared Macaque adalah 六耳獼猴, dalam pinyin Liù'ěr míhóu.
statement.en: The Chinese name of the Six-Eared Macaque is 六耳獼猴, in pinyin Liù'ěr míhóu.

basis_claims.quote: according to the Buddha, one of the four spiritual primates that do not belong to any of the ten categories that all beings in the universe are classified under.

statement.id: Menurut Buddha dalam novel, Six-Eared Macaque adalah satu dari empat primata spiritual yang tidak termasuk dalam sepuluh golongan yang menjadi pengelompokan semua makhluk di alam semesta.
statement.en: According to the Buddha in the novel, the Six-Eared Macaque is one of the four spiritual primates that do not belong to any of the ten categories into which all beings in the universe are classified.

basis_claims.quote: Buddha also says that the Six-Eared Macaque is "near-omniscient" (thanks to his six ears eavesdropping upon many tidbits of information around him far and wide), "knowledgeable of past and future" and "comprehensive of all things".

statement.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, Buddha juga berkata bahwa Six-Eared Macaque "hampir mahatahu" (near-omniscient) karena enam telinganya menyadap banyak informasi di sekelilingnya, "mengetahui masa lalu dan masa depan", dan "memahami segala hal".
statement.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, the Buddha also says the Six-Eared Macaque is "near-omniscient" because his six ears eavesdrop on information around him, "knowledgeable of past and future" and "comprehensive of all things".

basis_claims.quote: 又有四猴混世，不入十類之種。」菩薩道：「敢問是那四猴？」如來道：「第一是靈明石猴，通變化，識天時，知地利，移星換斗；第二是赤尻馬猴，曉陰陽，會人事，善出入，避死延生；第三是通臂猿猴，拿日月，縮千山，辨休咎，乾坤摩弄；第四是六耳獼猴，善聆音，能察理，知前後，萬物皆明。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Rulai (如來, Buddha) menyebut empat kera yang tidak termasuk sepuluh golongan makhluk: kera batu Lingming (靈明石猴), kera pantat merah (赤尻馬猴), kera lengan panjang (通臂猿猴), dan yang keempat Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), yang pandai mendengar, mampu menelaah, tahu sebelum dan sesudah, dan memahami segala hal.
statement.en: In the novel, Rulai (如來, the Buddha) names four monkeys outside the ten categories of beings: the Lingming stone monkey (靈明石猴), the red-buttocked horse monkey (赤尻馬猴), the long-armed ape (通臂猿猴), and the fourth, Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), skilled at listening, able to discern reason, knowing before and after, and understanding all things.

basis_claims.quote: 此猴若立一處，能知千里外之事；凡人說話，亦能知之。故此善聆音，能察理，知前後，萬物皆明。與真悟空同像同音者，六耳獼猴也。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Rulai (如來) berkata bahwa bila kera ini berdiri di satu tempat ia dapat mengetahui kejadian sejauh seribu li dan juga ucapan manusia, dan bahwa Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴) adalah yang serupa rupa dan suara dengan Sun Wukong (真悟空) yang asli.
statement.en: In the novel, Rulai (如來) says that when this monkey stands in one place he can know events a thousand li away and also what people say, and that Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴) is the one who matches the real Sun Wukong (真悟空) in form and voice.

basis_claims.quote: 大眾一發上前，把缽盂揭起，果然見了本像，是一個六耳獼猴。孫大聖忍不住，掄起鐵棒，劈頭一下打死，至今絕此一種。

statement.id: Dalam novel, ketika mangkuk diangkat, tampaklah wujud aslinya, Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴); Sun Wukong (孫大聖) tak tahan dan memukul kepalanya dengan tongkat besi sampai mati, sehingga jenis ini punah.
statement.en: In the novel, when the bowl is lifted his true form appears, a Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴); Sun Wukong (孫大聖) cannot hold back and strikes his head dead with the iron staff, so that this kind is extinct.

abumi-guchi.depicted_variant: Furry stirrup-shaped Abumi-guchi with eyes and mouth on an abandoned field.

visual_requirements.description: ABUMI-GUCHI, animate Japanese STIRRUP-MOUTH YŌKAI (c01,c05). One small squat furry object-creature visibly shaped like old Japanese horse STIRRUP with curved loop/footplate and physical tack strap, TWO expressive eyes above a large open natural MOUTH integrated into the stirrup cavity (c05), no human torso, dog ears, arms or arbitrary animal legs. Shaggy dark soft fur covers the stirrup rim, worn metal footplate subtly remains visible as origin, fur physical not mist. On an abandoned grassy field path at dusk, sparse old horse tack nearby, speculative fallen commander's abandoned stirrup context is marked interpretation c06; no killed commander or war gore. Low intimate camera, expectant eerie intent eyes and mouth make supernatural object unmistakable. No modern dog-waits-for-owner story from c07, giant transformation, aura or text.

abumi-guchi.aura: Furry stirrup-shaped Abumi-guchi with eyes and mouth on an abandoned field.

basis_claims.quote: An abumi-guchi (鐙口; lit. "stirrup mouth") is a strange furry yōkai, or Japanese monster, that is illustrated in Sekien Toriyama's Gazu Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro.

statement.id: Abumi-guchi adalah yōkai Jepang berbulu yang berarti mulut sanggurdi dan digambar Sekien.
statement.en: Abumi-guchi is a furry Japanese yōkai meaning stirrup mouth, illustrated by Sekien.

basis_claims.quote: 鐙口（あぶみくち）は、鳥山石燕の妖怪画集『百器徒然袋』にある日本の妖怪

statement.id: Abumi-guchi (鐙口, dibaca あぶみくち) adalah yōkai Jepang dalam kumpulan gambar yōkai karya Toriyama Sekien, Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro.
statement.en: Abumi-guchi (鐙口, read あぶみくち) is a Japanese yōkai in Toriyama Sekien's yōkai picture collection Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro.

basis_claims.quote: 鐙（あぶみ、馬具のひとつ）の妖怪であり、鐙に口と目が生えた形をしている。

statement.id: Abumi-guchi adalah yōkai dari sanggurdi (abumi, salah satu perlengkapan berkuda), berbentuk sanggurdi yang ditumbuhi mulut dan mata.
statement.en: Abumi-guchi is a yōkai of the stirrup (abumi, a piece of horse tack), shaped like a stirrup with a mouth and eyes.

basis_claims.quote: 石燕の解説にはどうような妖怪かという描写はほぼなく、武将が戦死し野に捨てられたままの鐙が妖怪と化したものではないかと考えられている。また、石燕は鞍野郎とおなじ見開きに鐙口を描いており

statement.id: Keterangan Sekien hampir tidak menggambarkan jenis yōkai ini; ia diduga sanggurdi seorang panglima yang gugur dalam perang dan dibiarkan terbuang di padang lalu menjadi yōkai. Sekien juga menggambarnya pada halaman bentang yang sama dengan Kurayarō (鞍野郎).
statement.en: Sekien's caption hardly describes what kind of yōkai it is; it is thought to be the stirrup of a military commander killed in battle and left abandoned in the field, which became a yōkai. Sekien also drew it on the same double-page spread as Kurayarō (鞍野郎).

au-co.depicted_variant: Immortal Âu Cơ as compassionate mountain ancestral mother beside the hundred-egg sac.

visual_requirements.description: ÂU CƠ, respectful Vietnamese immortal MOUNTAIN FAIRY and compassionate ancestral mother, one beautiful living woman one head two arms two legs, modest historic Vietnamese ceremonial drapery and dignified headdress inspired by shrine statue without copying pose (c01,c03,c09). In snowy mountain sanctuary (c01,c03,c05), stands protectively over an immense partly opened EGG SAC holding MANY WHITE EGGS, narrative of the hundred-egg bundle (c01,c12); some eggs naturally occluded within sac, do not imply fewer than one hundred in whole bundle. One hand open over the sack, other carries simple herbs indicating medical skill c03, exact herbs editorial not claimed fixed attribute. Strong compassionate gaze and miracle egg sac unmistakably fairy mother, natural dawn/snow light gives grandeur. No invented wings, aura, half-crane anatomy, glowing egg magic or ordinary bride portrait.

au-co.aura: Immortal Âu Cơ as compassionate mountain ancestral mother beside the hundred-egg sac.

basis_claims.quote: was, according to the creation myth of the Vietnamese people, an immortal mountain snow goddess who married Lạc Long Quân (lit. 'Dragon Lord of Lạc'), and bore an egg sac that hatched a hundred children known collectively as Bách Việt, ancestors to the Vietnamese people. Âu Cơ is often honored as the mother of Vietnamese civilization.

statement.id: Menurut mitos penciptaan bangsa Vietnam, Âu Cơ (甌姬) adalah dewi salju pegunungan yang abadi, menikah dengan Lạc Long Quân, dan melahirkan kantong telur yang menetaskan seratus anak (Bách Việt), leluhur bangsa Vietnam; ia sering dihormati sebagai ibu peradaban Vietnam.
statement.en: According to the Vietnamese creation myth, Âu Cơ (甌姬) was an immortal mountain snow goddess who married Lạc Long Quân and bore an egg sac hatching a hundred children (Bách Việt), ancestors of the Vietnamese; she is honoured as mother of Vietnamese civilization.

basis_claims.quote: Âu Cơ was a beautiful tiên (immortal) who lived high in the snow-capped mountains. She traveled to help those who suffered from illnesses since she was very skillful in medicine and had a sympathetic heart.

statement.id: Âu Cơ adalah tiên (makhluk abadi) cantik yang tinggal di pegunungan bersalju dan berkelana menolong orang sakit karena mahir pengobatan dan berhati welas asih.
statement.en: Âu Cơ was a beautiful tiên (immortal) in the snowy mountains who travelled to help the sick, being skilled in medicine and compassionate.

basis_claims.quote: They separated, each taking 50 children. Âu Cơ settled in the Vietnamese snow-covered mountains where she raised fifty young, intelligent, strong leaders, later known as the Hùng Vương, Hùng kings.

statement.id: Mereka berpisah dengan masing-masing membawa 50 anak; Âu Cơ menetap di pegunungan bersalju dan membesarkan lima puluh pemimpin yang kemudian dikenal sebagai raja-raja Hùng (Hùng Vương).
statement.en: They separated, each taking 50 children; Âu Cơ settled in the snowy mountains and raised fifty leaders later known as the Hùng kings (Hùng Vương).

basis_claims.quote: One day, a beautiful fairy named Au Co, who was living in the mountain, visited the country of Lac Viet to see the legendary beauty of the place.

statement.id: Seorang peri cantik bernama Au Co yang tinggal di gunung mengunjungi negeri Lac Viet untuk melihat keindahannya.
statement.en: A beautiful fairy named Au Co, living in the mountain, visited the land of Lac Viet to see its beauty.

basis_claims.quote: However, Au Co gave birth to a big bundle rather than to an infant. The bundle kept growing. Seven days later, it hatched into one hundred eggs. Each egg then broke open to reveal a bonny son.

statement.id: Au Co melahirkan buntalan besar, bukan bayi; buntalan itu terus membesar dan tujuh hari kemudian menetas menjadi seratus telur, masing-masing berisi seorang anak laki-laki.
statement.en: Au Co bore a big bundle rather than an infant; it kept growing and seven days later hatched into a hundred eggs, each revealing a son.

baigujing.depicted_variant: White Bone Spirit true skeletal form; no modern adaptation.

visual_requirements.description: ONE FULL white HUMAN SKELETON, one head two arms two legs normal hands fingers, uncovered dry clean white skull ribs pelvis limbs c03c12. Upright threatening alert stance on steep Baihu mountain ridge c14c16. An opaque plain ragged robe drapes only shoulder and side for atmosphere, leave skeletal anatomy unmistakable; NO living woman's face, breasts, crown, armor, blue neon eyes or flesh. Place green clay jar and green porcelain bottle c06 at feet as symbols of abandoned disguise. Mountain mist natural and grave menace, no multiple bodies or falsecorpse gore.

baigujing.aura: No sourced generic supernatural glow; natural moonlight and mountain mist only.

basis_claims.quote: Baigujing is a shapeshifting demoness, and in her true form she is depicted as a skeleton.

statement.id: Baigujing adalah iblis perempuan (demoness) pengubah wujud, dan dalam wujud aslinya digambarkan sebagai kerangka.
statement.en: Baigujing is a shapeshifting demoness, and in her true form she is depicted as a skeleton.

basis_claims.quote: 好妖精，停下陰風，在那山凹裡搖身一變，變做個月貌花容的女兒，說不盡那眉清目秀，齒白唇紅。左手提著一個青砂罐兒，右手提著一個綠磁瓶兒，從西向東，徑奔唐僧

statement.id: Dalam novel, siluman itu berubah (搖身一變) menjadi gadis cantik yang membawa kendi hijau dan botol porselen hijau, lalu berjalan langsung menuju Tang Sanzang (唐僧).
statement.en: In the novel, the demon transforms (搖身一變) into a beautiful girl carrying a green clay jar and a green porcelain bottle, and walks straight toward Tang Sanzang (唐僧).

basis_claims.quote: 那怪物有些手段，使個「解屍法」，見行者棍子來時，他卻抖擻精神，預先走了，把一個假屍首打死在地下。

statement.id: Dalam novel, siluman itu memakai "jieshi fa" (解屍法) saat tongkat Sun Wukong datang: ia meloloskan diri lebih dulu dan meninggalkan mayat palsu yang terpukul mati.
statement.en: In the novel, the demon uses the "jieshi fa" (解屍法) technique when Sun Wukong's staff comes: she slips away beforehand and leaves a false corpse struck dead on the ground.

basis_claims.quote: 卻是一堆粉骷髏在那裡。唐僧大驚道：「悟空，這個人才死了，怎麼就化作一堆骷髏？」

statement.id: Dalam novel, tubuh yang baru mati itu ternyata berupa setumpuk tengkorak putih (粉骷髏), dan Tang Sanzang terkejut karenanya.
statement.en: In the novel, the body that has just died turns out to be a pile of white skeleton (粉骷髏), and Tang Sanzang is shocked.

basis_claims.quote: 師父，此山叫做蛇回獸怕的白虎嶺，正西下面是我家。我父母在堂，看經好善，廣齋方上遠近僧人。

statement.id: Dalam novel, sosok gadis yang menyamar itu menyebut bahwa gunung itu bernama Baihu Ling (白虎嶺), tempat ular mundur dan hewan buas takut.
statement.en: In the novel, the disguised girl says the mountain is called Baihu Ling (白虎嶺), where snakes turn back and beasts take fright.

basis_claims.quote: 卻說常言有云：「山高必有怪，嶺峻卻生精。」果然這山上有一個妖精，孫大聖去時，驚動那怪。

statement.id: Dalam novel, dikatakan bahwa ada pepatah "gunung tinggi pasti ada siluman, bukit curam melahirkan roh", dan memang ada seorang yaojing (妖精, siluman) di gunung itu.
statement.en: In the novel, a saying is cited, "where mountains are high there must be monsters, where ridges are steep spirits are born," and indeed there is a yaojing (妖精, demon) on that mountain.

suvannamaccha.depicted_variant: Golden-tailed Suvannamaccha returning a bridge stone underwater in the Thai/Cambodian narrative.

visual_requirements.description: SUVANNAMACCHA, golden mermaid princess of THAI RAMAKIEN and Cambodian REAMKER, not Valmiki's Ramayana (c01,c05,c10). One living beautiful woman with ONE head TWO arms, modest opaque Thai traditional fitted upper garment and tall restrained princess headdress informed by charm reference; lower body ONE long GOLDEN SCALED FISH TAIL with broad natural tail fins, NO human legs (c01,c06). Swims at sea bottom beside piled stones of Hanuman's bridge to Lanka, one hand returns a bridge stone (c03,c07,c14,c20), tail curves in powerful graceful swimming pose and whole hybrid anatomy readable. Warm natural sunlight shafts through blue-green water glint physically on gold scales, dignified princess presence not ordinary fish, no coloured magic, modern cartoon/film mermaid costume, trident or unsupported powers.

suvannamaccha.aura: Golden-tailed Suvannamaccha returning a bridge stone underwater in the Thai/Cambodian narrative.

basis_claims.quote: literally "golden fish") is a daughter of Ravana (Thotsakan) appearing in the Thailand and other Southeast Asian versions of Ramayana. She is a mermaid princess who tries to spoil Hanuman's plans to build a bridge to Lanka but falls in love with him instead.

statement.id: Suvannamaccha (สุพรรณมัจฉา, Suphannamatcha; Pali suvaṇṇamacchā, 'ikan emas') adalah putri Rahwana (Thotsakan) dalam Ramayana versi Thailand dan Asia Tenggara, putri duyung yang mencoba menggagalkan jembatan Hanoman ke Lanka tetapi jatuh cinta kepadanya.
statement.en: Suvannamaccha (สุพรรณมัจฉา, Suphannamatcha; Pali suvaṇṇamacchā, 'golden fish') is a daughter of Ravana (Thotsakan) in Thai and Southeast Asian Ramayanas, a mermaid princess who tries to spoil Hanuman's bridge to Lanka but falls in love with him.

basis_claims.quote: They tell him that each day they throw rocks into the sea and the next day they are gone.

statement.id: Pasukan kera melapor bahwa batu yang mereka lempar ke laut setiap hari hilang keesokan harinya.
statement.en: The monkey army reports that the rocks they throw into the sea each day are gone the next.

basis_claims.quote: The story of Hanuman falling in love underwater with the mermaid daughter of Ravana, the demon king of Lanka, is not a tale one would encounter in Valmiki’s Ramayana.

statement.id: Kisah Hanoman jatuh cinta di bawah laut dengan putri duyung putri Rahwana tidak ada dalam Ramayana karya Walmiki.
statement.en: The tale of Hanuman falling in love underwater with Ravana's mermaid daughter is not found in Valmiki's Ramayana.

basis_claims.quote: Suvannamaccha—Suvarnamatsya in Sanskrit—the Golden Mermaid is perhaps a rare example in our storytelling oeuvre.

statement.id: Suvannamaccha, dalam bahasa Sanskerta Suvarnamatsya, adalah Putri Duyung Emas.
statement.en: Suvannamaccha, Suvarnamatsya in Sanskrit, is the Golden Mermaid.

basis_claims.quote: She reveals she was acting on her father Ravana’s orders. Upon learning the true purpose of the bridge from Hanuman, Suvannamaccha has a change of heart, and she promises to return all of the stolen rocks.

statement.id: Ia mengaku bertindak atas perintah ayahnya, Rahwana; setelah tahu tujuan jembatan dari Hanoman, ia berubah pikiran dan berjanji mengembalikan semua batu yang dicuri.
statement.en: She reveals she acted on Ravana's orders; learning the bridge's purpose from Hanuman, she changes her mind and promises to return all the stolen rocks.

basis_claims.quote: particularly prominent in Reamker, Cambodia’s epic poem and Ramakien, Thailand’s national epic.

statement.id: Kisahnya menonjol dalam Reamker, epos Kamboja, dan Ramakien, epos nasional Thailand.
statement.en: Her story is prominent in the Reamker, Cambodia's epic, and the Ramakien, Thailand's national epic.

basis_claims.quote: Hanuman, the valiant monkey god in Hinduism, and his vanara army of anthropomorphic monkeys embark on the monumental task of building a bridge to Lanka to help Rama rescue his wife, Sita, from the clutches of Ravana.

statement.id: Hanoman, dewa kera perkasa dalam agama Hindu, bersama pasukan vanara memulai tugas besar membangun jembatan ke Lanka untuk membantu Rama menyelamatkan istrinya, Sita, dari cengkeraman Rahwana.
statement.en: Hanuman, the valiant monkey god in Hinduism, and his vanara army set out on the monumental task of building a bridge to Lanka to help Rama rescue his wife Sita from Ravana's clutches.

basis_claims.quote: As the stones laid for the bridge mysteriously disappear, Hanuman investigates the cause and during this mission, he encounters and falls in love with Sovann Machha, the Golden Mermaid.

statement.id: Ketika batu-batu jembatan lenyap secara misterius, Hanoman menyelidiki sebabnya dan dalam tugas itu ia bertemu dan jatuh cinta kepada Sovann Machha, Putri Duyung Emas.
statement.en: As the stones laid for the bridge mysteriously disappear, Hanuman investigates the cause and in that mission meets and falls in love with Sovann Machha, the Golden Mermaid.

nang-ta-khian.depicted_variant: Reddish-brown-dressed human-form Nang Ta-khian protecting a satin-wrapped ancient Hopea tree.

visual_requirements.description: NANG TA-KHIAN, beautiful living young female Thai TREE SPIRIT of enormous HOPEA ODORATA (c01,c02,c23). One head two arms two legs, opaque reddish-brown traditional Thai dress, natural human skin and long black hair; NO green skin, green dress, hovering feet or other Nang Tani traits. Protective but formidable gaze as she stands at huge ancient buttressed tree trunk, one hand gently touching bark, huge canopy and trunk dominate dark forest scale around her. Physical coloured satin wrapped round trunk and small offerings at root (c05,c14). Distant subtle cemetery stones in shadow allude to c11, no victims or skeletons. Shape in leaves and focused natural moonlight produce uncanny revered guardian presence without transparency, tree-fusion anatomy, coloured mist, energy beams or invented magic glow.

nang-ta-khian.aura: Reddish-brown-dressed human-form Nang Ta-khian protecting a satin-wrapped ancient Hopea tree.

basis_claims.quote: Nang Ta-khian (Thai: นางตะเคียน, "Lady of Ta-khian") is a female spirit of the folklore of Thailand. It manifests itself as a woman that haunts Hopea odorata trees. These are very large trees known as Ta-khian (ตะเคียน) in Thai, hence her name.

statement.id: Nang Ta-khian (นางตะเคียน, 'Nona dari Ta-khian') adalah roh perempuan cerita rakyat Thailand yang tampil sebagai perempuan penghuni pohon Hopea odorata, pohon sangat besar yang disebut ta-khian.
statement.en: Nang Ta-khian (นางตะเคียน, 'Lady of Ta-khian') is a female spirit of Thai folklore appearing as a woman haunting Hopea odorata trees, very large trees called ta-khian.

basis_claims.quote: Legends in the Thai oral tradition say the spirit inhabits a Ta-khian tree and sometimes appears as a beautiful young woman wearing traditional Thai attire, usually in reddish or brownish colours, contrasting with Nang Tani who is mostly represented in a green dress.

statement.id: Nang Ta-khian termasuk roh pohon nang mai; menurut tradisi lisan ia menghuni pohon ta-khian dan kadang tampil sebagai perempuan muda cantik berbusana Thai kemerahan atau kecokelatan, berbeda dengan Nang Tani yang berbusana hijau.
statement.en: Nang Ta-khian is a nang mai tree spirit; oral tradition says she inhabits a ta-khian tree and sometimes appears as a beautiful young woman in reddish or brownish Thai dress, unlike the green-clad Nang Tani.

basis_claims.quote: Like all Nang Mai, Nang Ta-khian haunts the immediate environment of her tree and she may also haunt a house having beams, stilts or pillars made from Ta-khian wood. She may hurt wicked or immoral people that come close to her abode, but righteous persons have nothing to fear from her.

statement.id: Nang Ta-khian, roh hutan, menghantui sekitar pohonnya dan rumah berbalok, bertiang, atau berpilar kayu ta-khian; ia dapat mencelakai orang jahat yang mendekat, tetapi orang baik tak perlu takut.
statement.en: Nang Ta-khian, a forest spirit, haunts her tree's surroundings and houses with ta-khian beams, stilts or pillars; she may hurt the wicked who approach, but the righteous need not fear.

basis_claims.quote: Traditionally trees where Ta-khian resides have lengths of colored satin cloth wrapped around their trunk. In order to protect venerable old trees from logging, Buddhist monks use to wrap lengths of satin around them

statement.id: Pohon tempat Ta-khian tinggal biasanya dililit kain satin berwarna, dan biksu melilitkan kain satin pada pohon tua untuk melindunginya dari penebangan; penebangan harus didahului upacara meminta izin.
statement.en: Trees housing Ta-khian are traditionally wrapped in coloured satin, and monks wrap old trees to protect them from logging; felling requires a ceremony to ask permission.

basis_claims.quote: ซึ่งกล่าวถึง “ผีนางตะเคียน” และการมีอยู่ของต้นตะเคียนในป่าช้า รวมทั้งคาบอกเล่าที่เชื่อกันว่าศพที่ ฝังใต้ร่มเงาต้นตะเคียนจะเป็นศพผีตายโหง และผีนางตะเคียนจะคอยควบคุมดูแล
basis_claims.locator: หัวข้อ ความเชื่อและการบูชาเจ้าแม่ตะเคียน

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, pohon ta-khian ada di pekuburan, dan dipercaya jenazah yang dikubur di bawah naungannya menjadi hantu yang mati tak wajar, yang diawasi oleh hantu Nang Ta-khian.
statement.en: According to the article, ta-khian trees stand in cemeteries, and bodies buried in their shade are believed to become ghosts of violent death, overseen by the ghost Nang Ta-khian.

basis_claims.quote: ชี้ให้เห็นว่าในช่วงต้นรัตนโกสินทร์ การกราบ ไหว้บูชาเจ้าแม่ตะเคียนในฐานะเป็นรุกขเทวดาและนางไม้ที่ศักดิ์สิทธิ์และมีความน่ากลัว เป็น เรื่องที่พบเห็นได้ทั่วไปในท้องถิ่น ซึ่งซากต้นตะเคียนที่จมอยู่ในแม่น้าจะถูกนามาบูชาด้วย เครื่องเซ่นสังเวยพร้อมสร้างศาลเพียงตาเพื่อให้นางตะเคียนช่วยคุ้มครองป้องกันและดล บันดาลให้ประสบความสาเร็จในสิ่งที่ต้องการ
basis_claims.locator: หัวข้อ ความเชื่อและการบูชาเจ้าแม่ตะเคียน

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, pada awal periode Rattanakosin pemujaan Chao Mae Ta-khian sebagai dewa pohon dan peri pohon yang sakral dan menakutkan lazim ditemui di daerah; sisa pohon ta-khian yang tenggelam di sungai dipuja dengan sesajen dan altar kecil agar Nang Ta-khian melindungi dan memberi keberhasilan.
statement.en: According to the article, in the early Rattanakosin period worship of Chao Mae Ta-khian as a sacred and fearsome tree deity and tree nymph was commonly seen locally; remains of ta-khian trees sunk in rivers were worshipped with offerings and a small shrine so that Nang Ta-khian would protect people and grant success.

basis_claims.quote: Nang Ta-khian is generally a sylvan spirit, for the Ta-khian is a tall, massive tree that can live for centuries, naturally found in the forest and not near inhabited areas.

statement.id: Nang Ta-khian umumnya roh hutan, karena ta-khian adalah pohon tinggi dan besar yang bisa hidup berabad-abad dan tumbuh alami di hutan, bukan di dekat permukiman.
statement.en: Nang Ta-khian is generally a sylvan spirit, because the ta-khian is a tall, massive tree that can live for centuries and grows naturally in forests, not near inhabited areas.

princess-iron-fan.depicted_variant: Journey to the West Luocha Nu with banana-leaf fan.

visual_requirements.description: Beautiful formidable adult HUMAN-shaped female rakshasa c02c03, TWO arms TWO legs, modest flowing Chinese robes. Wields ENORMOUS BANANA-LEAF FAN twelve chi long c11, realistic broad green leaflike ribbed fan with stalk, no metal handheld folding fan. One sweeping motion raises cold gale and drives away flames at Flaming Mountains c04c05c06; rolling extinguishing flames and windblown dust/clothes. Cuiyun mountain and cave background c18. No bull horns, insect wings, armor or modern adaptation.

princess-iron-fan.aura: Cold wind and extinguishing fire from banana fan c04c05c06, physically visible winds, no luminous energy rings.

basis_claims.quote: She is also addressed as Rākṣasī (羅剎女; Luóchànǚ).

statement.id: Ia juga disebut Rākṣasī (羅剎女, Luóchànǚ), yaitu raksasi.
statement.en: She is also addressed as Rākṣasī (羅剎女, Luóchànǚ), a female rakshasa.

basis_claims.quote: Princess Iron Fan is a beautiful demoness, married to the Bull Demon King and mother to the Red Boy.

statement.id: Princess Iron Fan adalah iblis perempuan (demoness) yang cantik, istri Bull Demon King dan ibu Red Boy.
statement.en: Princess Iron Fan is a beautiful demoness, married to Bull Demon King and mother to Red Boy.

basis_claims.quote: 這芭蕉洞雖有，卻無個鐵扇仙，只有個鐵扇公主，又名羅剎女。」行者道：「人言他有一柄芭蕉扇，能熄得火焰山，敢是他麼？」樵子道：「正是，正是。這聖賢有這件寶貝，善能熄火，保護那方人家，故此稱為鐵扇仙。我這裡人家用不著他，只知他叫做羅剎女，乃大力牛魔王妻也。

statement.id: Dalam novel, seorang penebang kayu menyebut bahwa yang ada adalah Tieshan Gongzhu (鐵扇公主), juga bernama Luocha Nü (羅剎女), pemilik kipas pisang (芭蕉扇) yang bisa memadamkan Flaming Mountains (火焰山) dan istri Bull Demon King (大力牛魔王).
statement.en: In the novel, a woodcutter says that the one who lives there is Tieshan Gongzhu (鐵扇公主), also called Luocha Nü (羅剎女), owner of a banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇) able to extinguish the Flaming Mountains (火焰山) and wife of the mighty Bull Demon King (大力牛魔王).

basis_claims.quote: 行者道：「鐵扇仙怎的？」那人道：「鐵扇仙有柄芭蕉扇，求得來，一扇息火，二扇生風，三扇下雨。

statement.id: Dalam novel, seseorang menjelaskan bahwa kipas pisang (芭蕉扇) milik Tieshan Xian (鐵扇仙) bila dimohon dapat memadamkan api dengan satu kibasan, membangkitkan angin dengan dua kibasan, dan menurunkan hujan dengan tiga kibasan.
statement.en: In the novel, a man explains that the banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇) of Tieshan Xian (鐵扇仙), if obtained, puts out fire with one fanning, raises wind with two, and brings rain with three.

basis_claims.quote: 那羅剎女與行者相持到晚，見行者棒重，卻又解數周密，料鬥他不過，即便取出芭蕉扇，幌一幌，一扇陰風，把行者搧得無影無形，莫想收留得住。

statement.id: Dalam novel, setelah bertarung sampai petang dengan Sun Wukong (行者), Luocha Nü (羅剎女) mengeluarkan kipas pisang (芭蕉扇) dan satu kibasan angin dinginnya menyapu Sun Wukong hingga tak terlihat lagi.
statement.en: In the novel, after fighting Sun Wukong (行者) until evening, Luocha Nü (羅剎女) takes out the banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇) and one fanning of its cold wind sweeps Sun Wukong out of sight.

basis_claims.quote: 羅剎聽叫，急卸了釵環，脫了色服，挽青絲如道姑，穿縞素似比丘，雙手捧那柄丈二長短的芭蕉扇子，走出門。又見有金剛眾聖與天王父子，慌忙跪在地下，磕頭禮拜道：「望菩薩饒我夫妻之命，願將此扇奉承孫叔叔成功去也。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Luocha Nü (羅剎) keluar membawa kipas pisang (芭蕉扇) sepanjang satu zhang dua chi; melihat para dewa, ia berlutut dan memohon agar nyawa suami-istri itu diampuni sambil menyerahkan kipas itu kepada Sun Wukong (孫叔叔).
statement.en: In the novel, Luocha Nü (羅剎) comes out carrying the banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇), twelve chi long; seeing the gods, she kneels and begs for the couple's lives, offering the fan to Sun Wukong (孫叔叔).

basis_claims.quote: 行者近前作禮道：「樵哥，問訊了。」那樵子撇了柯斧，答禮道：「長老何往？」行者道：「敢問樵哥，這可是翠雲山？」樵子道：「正是。」行者道：「有個鐵扇仙的芭蕉洞，在何處？」

statement.id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong menanyakan Gunung Cuiyun (翠雲山) dan keberadaan Gua Pisang (芭蕉洞) milik Tieshan Xian (鐵扇仙); penebang kayu membenarkan bahwa itu Gunung Cuiyun.
statement.en: In the novel, Sun Wukong asks about Cuiyun Mountain (翠雲山) and the Banana Cave (芭蕉洞) of Tieshan Xian (鐵扇仙); the woodcutter confirms that it is Cuiyun Mountain.

abura-akago.depicted_variant: Clothed baby-form Abura-akago uncannily licking oil from a traditional lamp.

visual_requirements.description: ABURA-AKAGO, Japanese BABY YŌKAI licking lamp oil as Sekien depicts (c01,c04). One infant-shaped supernatural figure with one head TWO arms TWO legs, completely wrapped in opaque traditional cloth robe/diaper, no infant nudity. Crouches beside a low OLD JAPANESE OIL LAMP in a dark wood/tatami house, face bent to lamp bowl, little tongue clearly reaches a safe side lip with lamp OIL, flame at other side well separated from mouth. Oil thief rebirth c04 gives uncanny eerily intent adult-like watchful expression but natural infant anatomy; physical old household scene inspired by reference but original. Natural small lamp flame casts dramatic shadows and warm highlights against dark room, no luminous fireball surrounding infant or simultaneous transformation borrowed from modern c05, no burns or victims.

abura-akago.aura: Clothed baby-form Abura-akago uncannily licking oil from a traditional lamp.

basis_claims.quote: Abura-akago (油赤子; "oil baby") is a type of Japanese infant spirit or ghost. It is a yōkai that appeared illustrated in Toriyama Sekien's mid-Edo period Konjaku Gazu Zoku Hyakki, as an infant spirit lapping oil out of an andon lamp.

statement.id: Abura-akago berarti bayi minyak dan digambar Sekien sebagai bayi yōkai yang menjilat minyak lampu.
statement.en: Abura-akago means oil baby and was drawn by Sekien as a baby yōkai licking lamp oil.

basis_claims.quote: Sekien's accompanying notes describe it: ... If it is so, then the baby who licks the oil is this person's rebirth.

statement.id: Sekien mengusulkan bayi penjilat minyak sebagai kemungkinan kelahiran kembali pencuri itu.
statement.en: Sekien suggests the oil-licking baby might be the thief reborn.

akabeko.depicted_variant: Living red Akabeko leading temple-material cattle and hauling timber toward Enzoji.

visual_requirements.description: AKABEKO, living mysterious RED COW of AIZU legend leading cattle carrying materials to build ENZOJI TEMPLE around 807 (c01,c02,c03). One great crimson-red furred cow, normal bovine anatomy one head FOUR strong legs with hooves, small natural cow horns and one tail, body muscular and alive; no painted target circles, papier-mâché texture, bobble-head neck joint or toy proportions. A simple wooden harness lets the RED LEAD COW pull massive old timber along rough temple path, a few smaller distant natural cattle and partly built wooden Buddhist temple establish documented construction narrative (c03). Steady determined wise gaze and forceful forward stride create legendary protective presence. Natural warm mountain morning and physical dusty beam scale, no emitted holy aura or disease-healing magic, statue or ordinary grazing cattle portrait.

akabeko.aura: Living red Akabeko leading temple-material cattle and hauling timber toward Enzoji.

basis_claims.quote: There are several theories about the origins of akabeko, but one of the most popular comes from Enzoji Temple in the Aizu region.

statement.id: Salah satu cerita asal Akabeko terkait Kuil Enzoji di Aizu.
statement.en: One Akabeko origin story is linked to Enzoji Temple in Aizu.

basis_claims.quote: A mysterious “red” cow (probably a brown cow) suddenly appeared and began leading the other animals, working tirelessly until the task was completed.

statement.id: Cerita menggambarkan Akabeko sebagai sapi merah misterius yang memimpin ternak lain.
statement.en: The tale depicts Akabeko as a mysterious red cow leading the other cattle.

basis_claims.quote: Residents used cattle to help transport heavy materials when they were building the temple circa 807. A mysterious “red” cow (probably a brown cow) suddenly appeared and began leading the other animals, working tirelessly until the task was completed.

statement.id: Sekitar tahun 807 dalam cerita, sapi-sapi mengangkut bahan pembangunan kuil dan sapi merah memimpin mereka hingga pekerjaan selesai.
statement.en: Around 807 in the story, cattle carried temple materials and the red cow led them until the work was complete.

basis_claims.quote: The grateful people erected statues of the cow in the temple grounds, and over the years akabeko became associated with good health and fortune.

statement.id: Penduduk mendirikan arca sapi itu di kuil; Akabeko kemudian dikaitkan dengan kesehatan dan keberuntungan.
statement.en: Residents erected cow statues at the temple, and Akabeko became associated with health and fortune.

basis_claims.quote: In some Tohoku dialects, especially in the Aizu region, the word for "cow" is "beko" ("be" imitates the sound of a cow and "ko" is added to indicate affection). The name "Akabeko" comes from the fact that it is a toy of a cow colored red.

statement.id: Beko berarti sapi dalam sejumlah dialek Tohoku, dan Akabeko menamai sapi merah.
statement.en: Beko means cow in some Tohoku dialects, and Akabeko names the red cow.

apsonsi.depicted_variant: Living upright woman-lion Apsonsi with two lion hindlegs, tail and protective wai in Himavanta.

visual_requirements.description: A LIVING THAI APSONSI female-lion guardian of Himavanta (c01,c04,c07,c11), one beautiful woman HEAD, human upper TORSO and TWO human ARMS, lower body transitions coherently into exactly TWO strong LION HINDLEGS with paws and one long lion TAIL, upright biped arrangement matching inspected Wat Phra Kaew statue rather than centaur anatomy. Opaque traditional Thai fitted upper drapery, ornate restrained tall headdress; paws and golden tawny FUR clearly biological, no metal plating or carved surface. Hands held in protective wai gesture before mythical deep Himalayan forest grove (c04,c11), strong serene gaze and poised guardian stance. Slight low camera, natural warm forest shafts and cool distant mountain shade, unmistakable woman-lion union not ordinary dancer. NO swan wings or feathers, human feet, additional lion forelegs or generic aura.

apsonsi.aura: Living upright woman-lion Apsonsi with two lion hindlegs, tail and protective wai in Himavanta.

basis_claims.quote: Apsonsi (Thai: อัปสรสีห์) is a half-woman half-lion mythical creature from Thai mythology. Apsonsi is one of the many hybrid creatures depicted in ancient South and Southeast Asian folklore.

statement.id: Apsonsi (อัปสรสีห์) adalah makhluk mitos setengah perempuan setengah singa dari mitologi Thai, salah satu dari banyak makhluk campuran dalam cerita rakyat kuno Asia Selatan dan Tenggara.
statement.en: The apsonsi (อัปสรสีห์) is a half-woman, half-lion mythical creature of Thai mythology, one of many hybrid beings of ancient South and Southeast Asian folklore.

basis_claims.quote: In Legend, Apsonsi lived in Himavanta, an invisible mythical forest set deep in the Himalaya Mountains. The Apsonsi is a half-woman, half-lion figure believed to be the protector from harm. Apsonsi figures stand guard at Wat Phra Kaew (The Emerald Buddha Temple), a historic site in Bangkok, Thailand.

statement.id: Menurut legenda apsonsi tinggal di Himavanta, hutan mitos tak kasatmata jauh di Himalaya; ia diyakini pelindung dari marabahaya, dan patungnya berjaga di Wat Phra Kaew (Kuil Buddha Zamrud), Bangkok, Thailand.
statement.en: In legend the apsonsi lived in Himavanta, an invisible mythical forest deep in the Himalayas; believed to protect from harm, its figures guard Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha), Bangkok, Thailand.

basis_claims.quote: The Apsonsi, or Thai angels, are one of the many hybrid creatures depicted in ancient Southeast Asian folklore. These mythical half-women, half-lion figures are protectors against harm in ancient Thai literature.

statement.id: Apsonsi, atau "malaikat Thai", adalah salah satu makhluk campuran dalam cerita rakyat kuno Asia Tenggara; sosok mitos setengah perempuan setengah singa ini adalah pelindung dari marabahaya dalam sastra Thai kuno.
statement.en: The Apsonsi, or "Thai angels", are one of the many hybrid creatures in ancient Southeast Asian folklore; these mythical half-women, half-lion figures are protectors against harm in ancient Thai literature.

basis_claims.quote: Himavanta is a legendary forest, also called Himmapan (or Himmapun) Mountain, which is said to be located in the Himalayas.

statement.id: Himavanta adalah hutan legendaris, juga disebut Gunung Himmapan, yang dikatakan terletak di Himalaya.
statement.en: Himavanta is a legendary forest, also called Himmapan Mountain, said to be located in the Himalayas.

basis_claims.quote: Himavanta is a vast, deep, sacred forest atop Himmapan Mountain. ... The beautiful forest is home to gods and the dwelling place for sorcerers, priests, hermits, clerics, and bizarre mythical creatures.

statement.id: Himavanta adalah hutan suci yang luas dan dalam di puncak Gunung Himmapan, tempat tinggal para dewa serta kediaman penyihir, pendeta, pertapa, rohaniwan, dan makhluk mitos yang ganjil.
statement.en: Himavanta is a vast, deep, sacred forest atop Himmapan Mountain, home to gods and the dwelling place of sorcerers, priests, hermits, clerics and bizarre mythical creatures.

mae-nak-phra-khanong.depicted_variant: Human-form Mae Nak on a canal-house veranda stretching one arm impossibly down to retrieve a lime.

visual_requirements.description: MAE NAK PHRA KHANONG, ghost of a young Thai wife appearing in HUMAN FORM (c10), one head TWO arms TWO legs, modest historical Thai opaque wrapped blouse and skirt. On the raised wooden veranda of her old canal-side home (c09), one normal hand supports her while her OTHER ARM stretches to an IMPOSSIBLE several-metre LENGTH as a single anatomically continuous arm down from veranda to a small GREEN LIME on the ground (c04). Only one elbow and one hand on stretched arm, no branching limbs or giant finger tendrils. Show entire long curving arm from shoulder to hand and lime so uncanny tale reads immediately. Grieving watchful face turns towards viewer, body proportion normal but impossible arm unmistakably ghostly. Natural night side-light, dark canal below, sorrowful eerie horror without monstrous added teeth or skin, blood or extra babies. No aura or energy effects.

mae-nak-phra-khanong.aura: Human-form Mae Nak on a canal-house veranda stretching one arm impossibly down to retrieve a lime.

basis_claims.quote: lit. 'Lady Nak of Phra Khanong'), or simply Mae Nak (แม่นาก, 'Lady Nak') or Nang Nak (นางนาก, 'Miss Nak'), is a well-known Thai ghost. According to local folklore the story is based on events that took place during the reign of King Rama IV.

statement.id: Mae Nak Phra Khanong (แม่นากพระโขนง, 'Nyonya Nak dari Phra Khanong'), atau Mae Nak dan Nang Nak, adalah hantu Thailand yang terkenal; menurut cerita rakyat, kisahnya berdasarkan peristiwa pada masa Raja Rama IV.
statement.en: Mae Nak Phra Khanong (แม่นากพระโขนง, 'Lady Nak of Phra Khanong'), or Mae Nak and Nang Nak, is a well-known Thai ghost; folklore says her story is based on events in King Rama IV's reign.

basis_claims.quote: In her haste to retrieve it, she stretched her arm to an impossible length to pick it up from the ground below. Upon seeing this, Mak realised his wife was a ghost.

statement.id: Nak menjulurkan lengannya sangat panjang untuk memungut jeruk nipis dari tanah, dan Mak pun sadar istrinya hantu; ia lalu melarikan diri ke Wat Mahabut yang tak bisa dimasuki hantu.
statement.en: Nak stretched her arm to an impossible length to pick up a lime, and Mak realized she was a ghost; he then fled to Wat Mahabut, which ghosts cannot enter.

basis_claims.quote: Believed to date back to the early Rattanakosin period (around the 18th century), the legend has it that Mae Nak (“Mae” was used for “Miss” in those days) lived in the area near Wat Mahabut along a canal.

statement.id: Legenda yang diyakini berasal dari awal periode Rattanakosin ini menyebut Mae Nak tinggal di dekat Wat Mahabut di tepi kanal.
statement.en: The legend, believed to date to the early Rattanakosin period, says Mae Nak lived near Wat Mahabut beside a canal.

basis_claims.quote: making her a “Pee tai tang klom” (ghost of a woman who died during childbirth with the baby still inside her). Her body was buried in the cemetery at Wat Mahabut. But because of love, Nak’s spirit was bound to her former life, re-appearing in human form to carry on daily chores at home.

statement.id: Nak menjadi pee tai tang klom (arwah perempuan yang mati saat melahirkan dengan bayi masih di kandungan); karena cinta, arwahnya terikat pada kehidupan lamanya dan muncul dalam wujud manusia untuk mengurus rumah.
statement.en: Nak became a pee tai tang klom (ghost of a woman who died in childbirth with the baby inside); out of love her spirit stayed bound to her old life, appearing in human form to do the housework.

rangda.depicted_variant: Living mask-faced clawed Rangda with fangs, goggle eyes, unkempt hair and long tongue at cemetery.

visual_requirements.description: RANGDA, sacred Balinese leyak queen represented respectfully as a living terrifying old woman, ONE head TWO arms TWO legs (c01,c04). Huge goggle eyes, long fangs, LONG protruding tongue, unkempt pale hair and long sharp physical finger claws (c04), face mask-like but living spirit rather than stage dancer or prop. Pendulous breast contour covered completely by opaque traditional layered cloth to obey modesty; no exposed breasts or nudity. Wild animal-like reckless leaping gesture (c11), claws thrust outward with readable fingers. Cemetery setting among dark stone graves and a temple-of-the-dead gateway (c12), blighted dry vegetation may allude to crop harm c09 without inventing energy. Natural moonlight and deep shadows, fearsome supernatural character presence, no emitted coloured glow or attack spell.

rangda.aura: Living mask-faced clawed Rangda with fangs, goggle eyes, unkempt hair and long tongue at cemetery.

basis_claims.quote: Rangda (Balinese: ᬭᬗ᭄ᬤ) is the demon queen of the Leyaks in Bali, according to traditional Balinese mythology.

statement.id: Menurut mitologi tradisional Bali, Rangda (aksara Bali: ᬭᬗ᭄ᬤ) adalah ratu iblis para leak di Bali.
statement.en: According to traditional Balinese mythology, Rangda (Balinese: ᬭᬗ᭄ᬤ) is the demon queen of the leyaks in Bali.

basis_claims.quote: She is depicted as a mostly nude old woman, with long and unkempt hair, pendulous breasts, and claws. Her face is traditionally a horrifying fanged and goggle-eyed mask, with a long, protruding tongue.

statement.id: Rangda digambarkan sebagai perempuan tua hampir telanjang, berambut panjang kusut, berpayudara menggantung, bercakar, dengan topeng bertaring, bermata melotot, dan lidah panjang menjulur.
statement.en: Rangda is depicted as a mostly nude old woman with long unkempt hair, pendulous breasts and claws, with a fanged, goggle-eyed mask and long protruding tongue.

basis_claims.quote: It is said that Calon Arang was a widow, who had mastered the art of black magic, who often damaged farmers' crops and caused disease to come. She had a daughter, named Ratna Manggali, who, though beautiful, could not get a husband because people were afraid of her mother.

statement.id: Calon Arang adalah janda penguasa ilmu hitam yang merusak panen dan mendatangkan penyakit; putrinya, Ratna Manggali, tidak mendapat suami karena orang takut pada ibunya.
statement.en: Calon Arang was a widow skilled in black magic who damaged crops and brought disease; her daughter Ratna Manggali could not find a husband because people feared her mother.

basis_claims.quote: her wild and untamed energy is made visible as she moves animal-like, with reckless gestures and a leaping gait.

statement.id: Dalam pertunjukan, Rangda bergerak liar seperti binatang dengan gerak sembrono dan langkah melompat.
statement.en: In performance Rangda moves wildly like an animal with reckless gestures and a leaping gait.

basis_claims.quote: As the manifestation of the great Hindu goddess Durga, Rangda is the consort of the god Siwa the destroyer (known as Shiva in Sanskrit). Her realm is the cemetery, and sacred masks of Rangda are kept in the nearby village temples of the dead

statement.id: Sebagai perwujudan Durga, Rangda adalah pasangan Dewa Siwa; wilayahnya adalah kuburan, dan topeng sakralnya disimpan di pura desa untuk orang mati (pura dalem).
statement.en: As a manifestation of Durga, Rangda is consort of the god Siwa; her realm is the cemetery, and her sacred masks are kept in village temples of the dead.

basis_claims.quote: However, further research shows that Rangda’s role in Bali is more than an artistic device; she also serves an important religious function as a sacred symbol

statement.id: Penelitian menunjukkan peran Rangda di Bali lebih dari sekadar perangkat seni; ia juga berfungsi religius sebagai simbol sakral.
statement.en: Research shows Rangda's role in Bali is more than an artistic device; she also serves a religious function as a sacred symbol.

shachihoko.depicted_variant: Living tiger-headed fish Shachihoko spraying water to protect a castle.

visual_requirements.description: A LIVING JAPANESE SHACHIHOKO, one TIGER HEAD physically joins one FISH BODY (c02), strong tiger muzzle, striped fur head, actual feline ears, expressive fierce protective eyes, scaled fish trunk, fins and broad curled fish tail; NO human torso, wings or tiger legs. Curves upward in active water-leap beside a distant Japanese castle roof, SPRAYS ONE CLEAR STREAM OF WATER from mouth toward a small distant roof fire to protect castle (c03), restrained localized action not apocalyptic magic. Fish body and tiger head full silhouette visible, tail bends skyward matching reference iconic outline but not composition. Natural dusk and water highlights, flesh/scales/fur alive rather than bronze/gold roof ornament, strong guardian presence. No flame-breathing, generic glowing aura, statue or toy.

shachihoko.aura: Living tiger-headed fish Shachihoko spraying water to protect a castle.

basis_claims.quote: The roofs of many castles are adorned with ornamental ridge-end tiles in the shape of creatures called shachi (or shachihoko).

statement.id: Shachihoko juga disebut shachi dan dijadikan hiasan atap kastel.
statement.en: Shachihoko are also called shachi and used as castle-roof ornaments.

basis_claims.quote: These legendary beasts have the heads of tigers and the bodies of fish.

statement.id: Makhluk legenda ini berkepala harimau dan bertubuh ikan.
statement.en: These legendary creatures have tiger heads and fish bodies.

basis_claims.quote: According to folklore, shachi can spray water from their mouths to put out fires, and the tiles were believed to protect the castle.

statement.id: Menurut cerita rakyat, shachi menyemburkan air untuk memadamkan api dan hiasannya dianggap melindungi kastel.
statement.en: Folklore says shachi spray water to put out fires, and their ornaments were believed to protect castles.

nat-deity.depicted_variant: Respectful generalized human-origin Burmese guardian nat in ceremonial attire over a village shrine and mountain tree.

visual_requirements.description: One BURMESE NAT GUARDIAN SPIRIT, generalized deified high-status human nat sein rather than an unresearched specific named nat (c02,c14,c20). One living dignified adult with one head two arms two legs, beautifully tailored historic Burmese green ceremonial coat, patterned longyi and traditional head ornament informed by inspected Brother Nats shrine sculpture, no new animal parts. Protector of village, tree and mountain (c16), foreground upright protective open-palmed gesture above a small shrine and old banyan-like tree in Myanmar mountain setting near Popa (c04,c08). Low devotional camera and strong commanding expression create revered guardian presence, unusually solemn natural side-light, cloth moving in mountain wind. NOT a statue, medium or ordinary everyday portrait, no ghost transparency, supernatural enlargement asserted as fact, arbitrary halo, energy effect, weapons or generic mist.

nat-deity.aura: Respectful generalized human-origin Burmese guardian nat in ceremonial attire over a village shrine and mountain tree.

basis_claims.quote: The nats (နတ်; MLCTS: nat; IPA: [naʔ]) are god-like spirits venerated in Myanmar and neighbouring countries in conjunction with Buddhism. They are divided between the 37 Great Nats who were given that status by King Anawrahta

statement.id: Nat (နတ်) adalah roh serupa dewa yang dipuja di Myanmar dan negara sekitarnya bersama agama Buddha; ada 37 Nat Agung yang statusnya diberikan Raja Anawrahta.
statement.en: Nats (နတ်) are god-like spirits venerated in Myanmar and neighbouring countries alongside Buddhism; the 37 Great Nats received that status from King Anawrahta.

basis_claims.quote: Most of the 37 Great Nats were human beings who met violent deaths. There are two types of nats in Burmese Belief: nat sein (နတ်စိမ်း), which are humans that were deified after their deaths, and all other nats, which are spirits of nature (spirits of water, trees etc.).

statement.id: Sebagian besar 37 Nat Agung adalah manusia yang mati secara kejam; ada dua jenis nat: nat sein (manusia yang didewakan setelah mati) dan roh alam seperti roh air dan pohon.
statement.en: Most of the 37 Great Nats were humans who died violently; there are two kinds of nats: nat sein (humans deified after death) and nature spirits such as those of water and trees.

basis_claims.quote: Every Burmese village has a nat kun (နတ်ကွန်း) or nat sin (နတ်စင်), which essentially serves as a shrine to the village guardian nat called the ywa saung nat (ရွာစောင့်နတ်). Individual houses also have a shrine to a nat, usually a coconut is hung on a corner of the house

statement.id: Setiap desa Myanmar punya kuil untuk nat penjaga desa (ywa saung nat), dan rumah-rumah punya tempat pemujaan nat, biasanya kelapa yang digantung di sudut rumah.
statement.en: Every Burmese village has a shrine for the village guardian nat (ywa saung nat), and houses have a nat shrine, usually a coconut hung in a corner of the house.

basis_claims.quote: The most important nat pilgrimage site in Burma is Mount Popa, an extinct volcano with numerous temples and relic sites atop a 1,300-metre-tall (4,300 ft) mountain located near Bagan in central Burma.

statement.id: Tempat ziarah nat terpenting di Myanmar adalah Gunung Popa, gunung api mati setinggi 1.300 meter di dekat Bagan.
statement.en: Burma's most important nat pilgrimage site is Mount Popa, a 1,300-metre extinct volcano near Bagan.

basis_claims.quote: The 37 Great Nats, first recognized during the 11th century, were once high-status humans. All but one—Thagyamin, the lucky sod—perished in violent or painful circumstances. Snake bites, leprosy, beheading, forceful immolation, drowning, and falling off a swing are but a few of the myriad ways in which they died.

statement.id: 37 Nat Agung, yang diakui sejak abad ke-11, dulunya manusia berstatus tinggi; semua kecuali Thagyamin mati secara kejam atau menyakitkan, misalnya gigitan ular, kusta, dipenggal, dibakar, tenggelam, atau jatuh dari ayunan.
statement.en: The 37 Great Nats, recognized since the 11th century, were once high-status humans; all but Thagyamin died violently or painfully, e.g. snake bites, leprosy, beheading, immolation, drowning or falling off a swing.

basis_claims.quote: Guardian Spirits of tree, mountain, land house, village, town, country, roads. Some Nat Spirits overlap categories: Min Mahagiri is a leader of the 37 Pantheon and also a protector Nat of the household.

statement.id: Ada roh penjaga pohon, gunung, tanah, rumah, desa, kota, negara, dan jalan; sebagian nat masuk beberapa golongan, misalnya Min Mahagiri, pemimpin jajaran 37 sekaligus pelindung rumah.
statement.en: There are guardian spirits of trees, mountains, land, houses, villages, towns, the country and roads; some overlap, e.g. Min Mahagiri, leader of the 37 and protector of the household.

basis_claims.quote: Nat Spirits who are deceased humans still in limbo between lives, stuck in their regret or bitterness. THESE are the predominant Pantheon of 37, called “Nat Sein” – those who died a violent death

statement.id: Nat yang merupakan manusia yang telah meninggal dan masih terjebak di antara kehidupan disebut nat sein, yaitu mereka yang mati secara kejam; merekalah sebagian besar jajaran 37.
statement.en: Nats who are deceased humans still in limbo between lives are called nat sein, those who died a violent death; they make up most of the 37.

oyamatsumi.depicted_variant: Respectful elderly humanlike Ōyamatsumi mountain kami in historical robe iconography above mountain shrine.

visual_requirements.description: ŌYAMATSUMI, respectful JAPANESE MOUNTAIN KAMI (c01,c04,c05), humanlike elderly masculine presentation based on inspected historical Shinbutsu-zue icon: long solemn beard, simple tall traditional court/ritual hat, enormous draped opaque old Japanese robes with wide sleeves. One head two arms two legs, NO rock skin, horns, wings or animal attributes. Foreground imposing upright figure framed against great layered Japanese mountain peaks and small shrine torii below (c01,c04), deeply commanding calm gaze and wind-moved robe silhouette provide mountain-deity presence, not an ordinary contemporary hiker. A distant natural sea visible between mountain valleys may reflect documented Toba shrine mountain/sea domain c06. Natural slanting dawn through cloud, no emitted magic, cosmic aura, elemental attack, conflation with fire birth as fire power, sword or invented fixed anatomy.

oyamatsumi.aura: Respectful elderly humanlike Ōyamatsumi mountain kami in historical robe iconography above mountain shrine.

basis_claims.quote: The term yamatsumi means a spirit dwelling within a mountain, with the result that the name Ōyamatsumi means a great deity with jurisdiction over mountains.

statement.id: Nama Ōyamatsumi mengacu pada dewa yang menguasai pegunungan.
statement.en: The name Ōyamatsumi refers to a great deity over mountains.

basis_claims.quote: Shrines to kami with this name can be found throughout Japan.

statement.id: Kuil untuk kami bernama Ōyamatsumi tersebar di Jepang.
statement.en: Shrines to kami with this name are found throughout Japan.

basis_claims.quote: In Japanese folk religion, the kami of any given mountain is sometimes called Ōyamatsumi, as is the spirit of someone who has died within the mountains; in many cases, cairns of stones are erected as a place of worship.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Jepang, nama itu dapat menunjuk kami suatu gunung atau roh orang yang meninggal di pegunungan.
statement.en: In Japanese folk religion, the name can mean a mountain kami or the spirit of someone who died in the mountains.

basis_claims.quote: this shrine to Oyamazumi, the kami (Shinto deity) of mountains and seas, was located on the hilltop where construction was taking place.

statement.id: Kuil di Toba memuja Oyamazumi sebagai dewa gunung dan laut.
statement.en: The Toba shrine worships Oyamazumi as a deity of mountains and seas.

tenjin.depicted_variant: Tenjin as dignified deified court scholar with closed scroll at shrine under restrained distant thunder.

visual_requirements.description: TENJIN, respectful Japanese deified scholar SUGAWARA NO MICHIZANE (c01,c04), one living spirit with elderly scholarly face, short beard, exactly one head two arms two legs. Opaque historic Japanese court scholar robe with broad sleeves and traditional court cap inspired by inspected Sengai icon; no modern scholar clothes, war armour or weapons. Holds a plain CLOSED UNLETTERED SCROLL as editorial symbol of scholarship c04. Upright imposing guardian of learning before a small Kitano-style shrine gateway (c08), strong wise calm gaze and sweeping robe in natural wind create revered kami presence, not ordinary everyday male portrait. A few distant storm clouds with ONE faint far-off LIGHTNING FLASH express the documented thunder-deity combination c06, restrained background only; no beams from hands or eyes. Natural cool storm-break daylight, original dignified composition.

tenjin.aura: Tenjin as dignified deified court scholar with closed scroll at shrine under restrained distant thunder.

basis_claims.quote: Originally meant "Heavenly God," but later came to refer exclusively to the spirit of courtier-scholar Sugawara Michizane (845-903).

statement.id: Tenjin semula berarti dewa langit tetapi kemudian merujuk pada roh Sugawara no Michizane.
statement.en: Tenjin originally meant heavenly god but later referred to Sugawara Michizane’s spirit.

basis_claims.quote: He is revered as the patron saint of scholarship at such shrines as the Dazaifu Tenmangû in Fukuoka Prefecture and Kitano Tenjin shrines throughout Japan.

statement.id: Tenjin dihormati sebagai pelindung ilmu pengetahuan di kuil-kuil Jepang.
statement.en: Tenjin is revered as a patron of scholarship at shrines across Japan.

basis_claims.quote: The kami Tenman Daijizai Tenjin is a combination of the tenjin "thunder deity" (raijin) who rules the weather, Michizane's "vengeful spirit" (goryō ), a Chinese deity for whom oxen were killed and offered, the esoteric Buddhist (Mikkyō) "Dharma protector deity" (gohōjin), and the mythological Amatsukami (Tenjin).

statement.id: Sosok Tenjin memadukan roh Michizane dengan dewa guntur dan unsur keagamaan lain.
statement.en: The figure of Tenjin combines Michizane’s spirit with a thunder deity and other religious elements.

basis_claims.quote: This shrine was dedicated to noted scholar and poet Sugawara-no-Michizane (posthumously named Tenjin) in 947. It was revered by the court and the shogunate and spawned many branch shrines along with temple schools throughout the country.

statement.id: Kitano Tenmangū didedikasikan kepada Michizane pada 947 dan memunculkan kuil cabang.
statement.en: Kitano Tenmangū was dedicated to Michizane in 947 and gave rise to branch shrines.
